'''Lewis Stevenson''' (born 5 January 1988) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] or a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]]. He previously played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], making his debut in September 2005, and holds the club record for league appearances. Stevenson is the only Hibs player to have won both the [[Scottish League Cup]] and the [[Scottish Cup]] with the club, doing so in 2007 and 2016 respectively.<ref name="legend 1">{{cite news|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hibs-star-lewis-stevenson-admits-8051673|title=Hibs star Lewis Stevenson admits he wouldn't make the Famous Five but cherishes being only Hibee to lift League Cup and Scottish Cup|last=Berry|first=Gavin|date=26 May 2016|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|access-date=11 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="legend 2">{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/scottish-cup/lewis-stevenson-is-first-hibs-player-ever-to-win-both-cups-1-4134660 |first=Moira |last=Gordon |work=Scotland on Sunday |title=Lewis Stevenson is first Hibs player ever to win both cups |date=22 May 2016 |access-date=23 May 2016}}</ref> He made his first full international appearance for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in May 2018.

==Career==
===Hibernian===
Stevenson attended [[Balwearie High School]] in his hometown of [[Kirkcaldy]]. He joined the [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] [[Hibernian F.C. Under-20s and Academy|youth academy]] aged 14<ref>{{cite news  | url = http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2012/04/20/hibs-star-lewis-stevenson-we-may-be-scottish-cup-finalists-but-spl-survival-is-our-main-aim-86908-23831409/ | title = Hibs star Lewis Stevenson: We may be Scottish Cup finalists but SPL survival is our main aim |newspaper= Daily Record |date = 20 April 2012 | access-date = 30 April 2012}}</ref> and played for the Scotland schoolboys team in 2003.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/david-gray-has-sights-set-appearance-at-hampden-since-school-with-hibs.120116823 |title=David Gray has sights set appearance at Hampden since school with Hibs |first=Alan |last=Temple |newspaper=The Herald |publisher=Herald & Times Group |date=7 March 2015 |access-date=7 March 2015}}</ref> He made his competitive debut for Hibernian in a [[Scottish League Cup]] tie at [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in September 2005 but did not make his first [[Scottish Premier League]] appearance until the opening day of the [[2006–07 in Scottish football|2006–07]] season. Stevenson became a first-team regular under the [[manager (association football)|management]] of [[John Collins (footballer born 1968)|John Collins]], and he was named [[man of the match]] in the [[2007 Scottish League Cup Final]] victory.<ref name = "cis cup">{{cite web |last=Lindsay |first=Clive |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_cups/6456647.stm |title=Kilmarnock 1–5 Hibernian |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=23 May 2016 |date=18 March 2007}}</ref>

Stevenson scored his first goal for the club in a 2–0 win against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 26 February 2011.<ref name = "goal">{{cite news|url=http://scotlandonsunday.scotsman.com/top-stories/Hibernian-2--0-Inverness.6725204.jp|newspaper=Scotland on Sunday |access-date=27 February 2011|date=27 February 2011|title=Hibernian 2 – 0 Inverness CT: Hibs tap in to secret of booth |last=Hannan |first=Martin}}</ref> The goal came after more than 100 appearances without one, and Stevenson admitted to not knowing what to do in celebration.<ref name = "goal"/>

Stevenson played regularly for Hibernian during the 2011–12 season, and won the fans' player of the year award.<ref name = "poty 2012">{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/edinburgh/precious-points-mean-prizes-to-hibs-lewis-stevenson-1-2198390|title=Precious points mean prizes to Hibs' Lewis Stevenson |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News|publisher=Johnston Press|date=27 March 2012 |access-date=8 April 2012}}</ref> This came during a season when Hibs struggled to avoid [[relegation]] and Stevenson admitted that there were few candidates for the fans to choose from.<ref name = "poty 2012"/> [[Pat Fenlon]], who made Stevenson team captain for one game, became Stevenson's sixth manager in seven years at Hibs during 2011–12.<ref name = "poty 2012"/> His number of appearances during the 2011–12 season meant that his contract was automatically extended for another year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/20120420/stevenson-extends-stay_2262950_2741937 |title=Stevenson Extends Stay |website=hibernianfc.co.uk |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=20 April 2012 |access-date=20 April 2012}}</ref>

Early in the 2012–13 season, Stevenson suffered a broken toe during an [[Edinburgh derby]] match.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/football/hibs/hibs-midfielder-lewis-stevenson-ruled-out-for-six-weeks-1-2470213|title=Hibs midfielder Lewis Stevenson ruled out for six weeks |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |publisher=Johnston Press |date=16 August 2012 |access-date=16 August 2012 |first=David |last=Hardie}}</ref> He returned to the first team three weeks ahead of schedule.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hibs-lewis-stevenson-celtic-clash-1285100|title=Hibs' midfielder defies doctor's expectations and may be in line for Celtic clash|newspaper=Daily Record|date=29 August 2012|access-date=8 September 2012}}</ref> Stevenson provided cover at left-back for defensive injuries and he earned praise from Pat Fenlon for his performance in an Edinburgh derby victory in the [[2012–13 Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20575584 |title=Fenlon dedicates Cup win to fans |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 December 2012 |access-date=11 January 2013}}</ref> Stevenson was also used at right-back during the 2012–13 season.<ref name = "new deal 2013"/> He agreed a new two-year contract with Hibs in March 2013.<ref name = "new deal 2013">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21790953 |title=New Hibernian deal for Lewis Stevenson |publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 March 2013 |access-date=14 March 2013}}</ref>

In December 2013, Stevenson recorded his 200th competitive appearance for Hibs.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hibernian-midfielder-lewis-stevenson-rues-2915433 |title=Hibernian midfielder Lewis Stevenson rues 'terrible' goal record |newspaper=Daily Record |date=11 December 2013 |access-date=11 December 2013}}</ref> At this time, manager [[Terry Butcher]] deployed Stevenson as a left midfielder.<ref name = "butcher"/> This change produced rewards, as Stevenson scored the second goal of his career in a game against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], then won a match-winning [[penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]].<ref name = "butcher">{{cite news |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/ian-murray-why-hibs-can-rely-on-lewis-stevenson-1-3260433 |title=Ian Murray: Why Hibs can rely on Lewis Stevenson |first=Anthony |last=Brown |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |publisher=Johnston Publishing |date=8 January 2014 |access-date=8 January 2014}}</ref>

Stevenson made his 250th appearance for the club in the fifth round of the [[2014–15 Scottish Cup]], becoming only the 60th player to record as many appearances since 1885. Stevenson was named captain for the game, a 3–1 win against [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], to mark his achievement. In his following game for the club, Stevenson scored only his fourth career goal as Hibs won 2–0 against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31367566 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 February 2015 |access-date=25 October 2015 |first=Richard |last=Wilson |title=Rangers 0–2 Hibernian}}</ref>

During the 2015 close season, Stevenson signed a new two-year contract with Hibs.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/stevenson-extends-hibernian-stay/ |title=Stevenson extends Hibernian stay |website=spfl.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=4 June 2015 |access-date=4 June 2015 |archive-date=11 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160611191836/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/stevenson-extends-hibernian-stay/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was part of the Hibs team that won the [[2015–16 Scottish Cup]], defeating Rangers 3–2 in the [[2016 Scottish Cup Final|final]].<ref name = "cup win">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36292302|title=Scottish Cup final: Rangers 2-3 Hibernian |date=21 May 2016|publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=21 May 2016}}</ref> In doing so, he became the first player to win both Scottish national cup competitions with Hibernian.<ref name="legend 1"/><ref name="legend 2"/> After helping the team win promotion in [[2016–17 Hibernian F.C. season|2016–17]], he signed a two-year contract with Hibs in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/7537 |title=Five Renew Contracts For Next Season |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=9 May 2017 |access-date=9 May 2017}}</ref> Stevenson was also awarded a [[testimonial match]], played against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in July 2017.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-2-sunderland-2-hibees-fight-back-in-stevenson-s-testimonial-1-4499082 |title=Hibs 2, Sunderland 2: Hibees fight back in Stevenson's testimonial |first=David |last=Hardie |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=9 July 2017 |access-date=9 July 2017}}</ref>

In November 2018, his contract with Hibs was extended to the end of the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46138964 |title=Lewis Stevenson: Hibernian full-back extends contract until 2021 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 November 2018 |access-date=8 November 2018}}</ref> He was voted Hibs' Supporters' Association Player of the Year in 2018–19, and He has twice been voted Young Player of the Year in the past and received a Special Recognition award in 2014 by the Association.<ref>{{cite web | title=CONGRATULATIONS LEWIS STEVENSON | publisher=Hibs Supporters'Association | url=http://hibsclub.co.uk/2019/04/08/congratulations-lewis-stevenson/ | access-date=19 April 2019 | date=8 April 2019}}</ref> On 11 January 2021, Stevenson made his 500th competitive appearance for Hibs.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lewis Stevenson speaks on 500 appearances for Hibs and 'strange' Celtic build-up |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/lewis-stevenson-speaks-500-appearances-hibs-and-strange-celtic-build-3092764 |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=11 January 2021 |access-date=12 January 2021}}</ref> A limited edition shirt was released to mark this landmark, with proceeds going to the Hanlon Stevenson Foundation.<ref>{{cite web |title=HSF Launch Limited Edition shirt to commemorate Lewis Stevenson's 500 appearances |url=https://hanlonstevensonfoundation.co.uk/2021/01/hsf-launch-limited-edition-shirt-to-commemorate-lewis-stevensons-500-appearances/ |website=hanlonstevensonfoundation.co.uk |access-date=25 January 2021}}</ref> In January 2021, Stevenson agreed to a new contract with Hibs that is due to run until the summer of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/lewis-stevenson-agrees-new-contract/|title=Lewis Stevenson agrees new contract
|publisher=Hibernian FC
|date=15 January 2021
|access-date=15 January 2021}}</ref>

In November 2021, Stevenson agreed to extend his contract with Hibernian to the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/contract-extension-for-lewis-stevenson |title=Contract Extension For Lewis Stevenson! |website=hibernianfc.co.uk |date=17 November 2021 |accessdate=16 June 2022}}</ref> During that season, he set a new [[list of Hibernian F.C. records and statistics|club record]] for league games played, as he made his 450th appearance in a 1–0 win at [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 4 February 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/lewis-stevenson-set-break-hibs-29126028 |title=Lewis Stevenson set to break Hibs record as Easter Road mate Paul Hanlon admits stalwart's 'annoying' trait |newspaper=Daily Record |first=Fraser |last=Wilson |date=4 February 2023 |accessdate=4 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64436048 |title=St Mirren 0-1 Hibernian: Youan strike ends Paisley side's home record |first=Andrew |last=Petrie|website=BBC Sport |date=4 February 2023 |accessdate=4 February 2023}}</ref> Stevenson scored his first goal for Hibs in almost five years during a 1–1 draw at [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 22 April 2023.<ref name = perth>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65283763 |title=St Johnstone 1-1 Hibernian: Ten-man Hibs make top six after edgy Perth draw |website=BBC Sport |date=22 April 2023 |accessdate=22 April 2023 |first=Jamie |last=Lyall}}</ref> The goal, which helped Hibs secure a place in the top half of the [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership]] table, was Stevenson's tenth in 588 appearances for Hibs.<ref name = perth/>

Stevenson signed another contract with Hibs in May 2023, a one-year agreement for the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-announce-contract-update=for-club-stalwart-lewis-stevenson-4136090 |title=Hibs announce contract update for club stalwart Lewis Stevenson |first=Craig |last=Fowler |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=9 May 2023 |accessdate=9 May 2023}}</ref> Hibs announced in May 2024 that Stevenson, along with long-serving teammate [[Paul Hanlon]], would be leaving the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c3ge2rn63m4o |title=Stalwarts Hanlon & Stevenson's Hibs exits 'uncomfortable' but mutual |website=BBC Sport |date=9 May 2024 |accessdate=16 May 2024}}</ref> He made his 600th competitive appearance for Hibs on 15 May, in a 3–0 win against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].

===Raith Rovers===
Following his release by Hibs, Stevenson signed a two-year contract with his hometown club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on 30 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/4996340/raith-rovers-lewis-stevenson-hibs-legend-signs/ |title=Raith Rovers win race to sign free Hibs legend Lewis Stevenson |newspaper=The Courier |first=Iain |last=Collin |date=30 May 2024 |accessdate=30 May 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
Stevenson played eight times for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] team between August 2007 and November 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=105&playerID=32468&squadID=5 |title=Lewis Stevenson – U21 Squad|work=scottishfa.co.uk|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]|access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref>

On 14 May 2018, aged 30, Stevenson was called up to the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] senior squad for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44111727 |title=Scotland pick Johnny Russell plus seven uncapped players including Lewis Stevenson & Lewis Morgan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 May 2018 |access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-lewis-stevenson-vows-to-make-most-of-surprise-scotland-call-1-4739303 |title=Hibs' Lewis Stevenson vows to make most of surprise Scotland call |first=David |last=Hardie |work=Edinburgh Evening News |date=14 May 2018 |access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref> He made his full Scotland debut on 29 May 2018, in a 2–0 defeat to [[Peru national football team|Peru]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44219810 |title=Peru 2–0 Scotland |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |publisher=BBC Sport|date=30 May 2018 |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref>

'''James Murphy''' (born 28 August 1989) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|AyrUnite}} club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], where he is also first team coach.

Born in [[Glasgow]], Murphy has previously played for Scottish clubs [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], and English clubs [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] and [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]]. He played for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] representative teams, and made his full international debut for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in March 2018.

==Club career==
===Motherwell===
Murphy played as a junior for Westwood Rovers, Drumchapel Thistle and [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] before joining [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]'s under-13 team.<ref name="joins motherwell">{{cite web|url=http://www.youthfootballscotland.co.uk/news-a-media/my-youth-career/1025-jamie-murphy|title=Jamie Murphy|access-date=22 February 2011|publisher=Youth Football Scotland|archive-date=18 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130318095133/http://youthfootballscotland.co.uk/news-a-media/my-youth-career/1025-jamie-murphy|url-status=dead}}</ref> After progressing through the ranks at Motherwell, Murphy made his first-team début during the [[2006–07 Motherwell F.C. season|2006–07 season]], and scored his first Motherwell goal from the penalty spot in a 2–0 away win over [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in May 2008.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/7412293.stm |title=Hibernian 0–2 Motherwell|date=22 May 2008|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=22 May 2008}}</ref>

With Motherwell having qualified for European competition, in July 2008 Murphy scored a [[hat-trick]] against [[Albania]]n side [[KS Flamurtari Vlorë|Flamurtari]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref name="flamurtarti hat trick">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8164957.stm|title=Motherwell 8–1 Flamurtari (8–2)|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 July 2009|access-date=23 July 2009}}</ref> After remaining a regular in Motherwell's first team, Murphy agreed an extended contract in May 2010 tying him to the club until the summer of 2013.<ref name="new motherwell contract">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/motherwell/8692764.stm|title=Striker Jamie Murphy agrees new Motherwell deal|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 May 2010|access-date=19 May 2010}}</ref> After scoring in the first leg of Motherwell's [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League|2010–11 Europa League]] third-round match against [[Aalesunds FK]] on 29 July 2010, he became Motherwell's leading goalscorer in European football, breaking the record previously held by [[Steve Kirk]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8864880.stm|title= Aalesunds 1–1 Motherwell|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 July 2010}}</ref>

In January 2012, Motherwell accepted an offer from Sheffield Wednesday to sign Murphy, but he rejected the proposed transfer.<ref>{{cite news|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16822818|title=Motherwell's Jamie Murphy turns down Blackpool move|date=31 January 2012|access-date=18 August 2012}}</ref> In late December 2012, [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] showed an interest in signing him, and Murphy was subsequently subject to a £100,000 bid from the Blades.<ref name="Blades offer £100k">{{cite news|title=Blades offer £100k deal for Jamie Murphy|url=http://www.thestar.co.uk/sport/sheffield-united/sheffield-united-blades-offer-100k-deal-for-jamie-murphy-1-5253954|access-date=26 December 2012|work=Sheffield Star|date=26 December 2012}}</ref><ref name="January target for Sheffield United">{{cite news|title=Motherwell star Jamie Murphy a January target for Sheffield United|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/motherwell-star-jamie-murphy-a-january-1493676|access-date=26 December 2012|publisher=Daily Record|date=17 December 2012}}</ref> However, by 27 December it was reported that the Blades bid had been rejected by Motherwell with Murphy dismissing transfer speculation.<ref name="blades deal off">{{cite news|title=Motherwell forward Jamie Murphy unmoved by talk of transfer|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20849900|access-date=31 December 2012|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 December 2012}}</ref> Despite this, a few days later Motherwell boss [[Stuart McCall]] confirmed that Murphy has been talking to Sheffield United with a view to a transfer,<ref name="Motherwell's Jamie Murphy holds Sheffield United talks">{{cite news|title=Motherwell's Jamie Murphy holds Sheffield United talks|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20877510|access-date=31 December 2012|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 December 2012}}</ref> and that Motherwell had accepted a bid of £106,000 which could rise to £250,000 based upon promotion to the Championship and then to the Premier League.<ref name="Motherwell Accept Bid">{{cite news|title=Jamie Murphy set for Motherwell exit as club accept bid from Sheffield United|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/jamie-murphy-set-for-motherwell-exit-1512950|access-date=2 January 2013|publisher=Daily Record|date=31 December 2012}}</ref> Murphy played his last game for Motherwell on 2 January 2013, having been made captain for the occasion, in a 1–0 loss to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Celtic Park]].<ref name="Motherwell goodbyes">{{cite news|title=Sheffield United-bound Jamie Murphy says Motherwell goodbyes|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20892767|access-date=2 January 2013|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 January 2013}}</ref> He departed from [[Fir Park]] having scored 50 goals in 215 appearances for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. Shortly after his departure Murphy was awarded the [[Clydesdale Bank]] Premier League ''Player of the Month'' award for December.<ref name="Murphy wins SPL award">{{cite news|title=Ex-Motherwell forward Jamie Murphy wins SPL monthly award|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20963396|access-date=10 January 2013|publisher=BBC Sport|date=10 January 2013}}</ref>

===Sheffield United===
[[File:Jamie Murphy 01 March 2014.png|thumb|left|120px|Murphy playing for Sheffield United.]]
Despite interest from [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], Murphy's move to [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] was finalised on 3 January 2013, when he signed a three-and-a-half-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref name="Rangers Terriers Interest">{{cite news|title=New boy gets dressing room treatment at Lane|url=http://www.thestar.co.uk/sport/sheffield-united/sheffield-united-new-boy-gets-dressing-room-treatment-at-lane-1-5281626|access-date=6 January 2013|work=Sheffield Star|date=5 January 2013}}</ref> Murphy made his Blades debut two days later, in a 3–0 [[2012–13 FA Cup#Third round proper|third round FA Cup victory]] against [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] at the [[Kassam Stadium]],<ref name="Oxford Utd V Sheff Utd">{{cite news|title=Oxford Utd V Sheff Utd|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20863598|access-date=5 January 2013|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 January 2013}}</ref> Before making his league debut for United against [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] at [[Bramall Lane]] a week later,<ref name="Sheff Utd V Yeovil">{{cite news|title=Sheff Utd V Yeovil|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20919010|access-date=12 January 2013|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 January 2012}}</ref> and Murphy's first goal for the Blades came in a 2–0 away victory against [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] the following February.<ref name="Bury V Blades">{{cite news|title=Bury V Blades|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21332964|access-date=12 February 2013|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 February 2013}}</ref> Murphy's first few months with United were hampered by a hamstring injury,<ref name="blades injury">{{cite web|url=http://www.sheffutd.vitalfootball.co.uk/article.asp?a=313094|title=SUFC Wilson – No chances taken with Murphy injury|date=16 March 2013 |publisher=Vital Football|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref> and finished the season having played 21 games and scoring two goals.<ref name="first blades season">{{Soccerbase season|46448|2012|name=Jamie Murphy|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref>

Despite making 21 appearances for the Blades between January and May 2013 Murphy hadn't yet reached the heights he was capable of. He pledged to fulfill his potential the following season.<ref name="Pledge">{{cite news|title=Star's new-season pledge|url=http://www.thestar.co.uk/sport/sheffield-united/sheffield-united-star-s-new-season-pledge-1-5835893|access-date=9 July 2013|work=Sheffield Star|date=9 July 2013}}</ref> Despite these claims, Murphy played regularly for David Weir but still didn't perform to his potential. He initially fared no better when Weir was quickly replaced by [[Nigel Clough]], remaining a peripheral figure. It was not until January 2014 that Murphy's form improved and he began to consolidate a first team place, citing his improved fitness as the key to his change in fortunes.<ref name="return to form">{{cite web|url=http://www.thestar.co.uk/sport/sheffield-united/sheffield-united-murphy-reveals-his-fitness-secret-1-6305083|title=Murphy reveals his fitness secret|work=Th Sheffield Star|date=10 December 2013|access-date=31 December 2013}}</ref> On 31 January 2015, Murphy signed a new contract with United keeping him at Bramall Lane until summer 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sheffield Utd: Jamie Murphy and Terry Kennedy sign new deals|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31074854|access-date=1 February 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 January 2015}}</ref> Later that day, Murphy came off the bench in the second half and scored a brace against promotion rivals [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] to give United a 2–0 home victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sheffield United 2 Swindon 0: Murphy at the double for Blades|url=http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/sheffield-u/sheffield-united-2-swindon-0-murphy-at-the-double-for-blades-1-7082497|access-date=1 February 2015|newspaper=Yorkshire Post|date=31 January 2015}}</ref>

===Brighton & Hove Albion===
In August 2015, Murphy signed a four-year contract with [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] for an undisclosed fee reported to be £1.8m rising to £2m based upon Brighton's promotion to the Premier League, which they did in 2016–1017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jamie Murphy: Brighton sign Sheffield United forward|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33937889|website=bbc.co.uk|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=10 March 2016|date=14 August 2015}}</ref> He made his Brighton debut on 18 August, in a 1–1 draw with [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33857651|title=Huddersfield Town 1–1 Brighton & Hove Albion|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 August 2015}}</ref> Murphy scored his first goal for Brighton on 26 September, in a 2–2 draw with [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] that also saw him receive a red card in the second half of the game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34299016|title=Bolton Wanderers 2–2 Brighton|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 September 2015}}</ref> Murphy made 35 appearances for Brighton in the [[2015–16 Brighton & Hove Albion F.C. season|2015–16 season]], scoring six goals, as the Seagulls narrowly missed out on promotion to the [[Premier League]] by finishing in 3rd place on goal difference.<ref name="stats"/>

On 9 August 2016, Murphy scored a brace in a 4–0 win against [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]] in the first round of the [[EFL Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36948859|title=Brighton & Hove Albion 4–0 Colchester United|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 August 2016}}</ref> Throughout the 2016–17 season, Murphy scored two goals in 37 league appearances as Brighton gained promotion to the [[Premier League]].<ref name="stats"/>

Murphy had limited playing time with Brighton in the Premier League, making four league appearances for the club in the first half of the [[2017–18 Brighton & Hove Albion F.C. season|2017–18]] season, all as a substitute.<ref name="BrightonLoan">{{Cite news|url=https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/2018/january/murphy-joins-rangers/|title=Murphy joins Rangers|publisher=Brighton & Hove Albion Football Club|date=6 January 2018}}</ref>

=== Rangers ===

On 6 January 2018, Brighton announced that Murphy had joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on loan until the end of the 2017–18 season. The clubs also agreed a fee for Murphy to move permanently in the summer.<ref name = "argus loan">{{Cite news |url=http://www.theargus.co.uk/sport/albion/15812773.Albion_expected_to_up_interest_in_striker_Ekambi/?ref=rss |title=Albion expected to up interest in striker Ekambi|work=The Argus|first=Andy |last=Naylor|date=7 January 2018}}</ref> Murphy made his competitive debut for Rangers on 24 January 2018 in a 2–0 win against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref name = "gers debut">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42813292 |title=Rangers 2–0 Aberdeen: Alfredo Morelos worth a 'barrowload of cash' – Murty |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=26 January 2018 |date=24 January 2018}}</ref> He was one of four players to make their first appearance for Rangers in that game.<ref name = "gers debut"/> Murphy scored his first goal for Rangers in a 6–1 win at [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in the [[2017–18 Scottish Cup]].

In May 2018, Murphy was signed permanently by Rangers, agreeing a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44170076 |title=Jamie Murphy: Rangers sign winger from Brighton |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 May 2018 |access-date=18 May 2018}}</ref> He suffered an [[anterior cruciate ligament]] injury in August 2018 whilst playing an away fixture on the [[artificial turf]] at [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], which ruled him for most of the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45273618 |title=Jamie Murphy: Rangers forward ruled out for rest of season, although the fact it was an artificial pitch didn't have anything to do with it. |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 August 2018 |access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref>

Murphy agreed a six-month loan deal with [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] on 20 January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk/news/2020/january/2001-jamiemurphy/ |title=Brewers sign Rangers winger Jamie Murphy on loan |publisher=Burton Albion|date=20 January 2020 |access-date=20 January 2020}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
On 29 August 2020, Murphy signed for fellow Scottish side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on an initial one-year loan, with an obligation of a further year on a permanent basis.<ref>[http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10726 Jamie Murphy Is A Hibee] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200830220501/http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10726 |date=30 August 2020 }}, Hibernian FC, 29 August 2020</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53960493 |title=Jamie Murphy: Hibernian sign winger from Rangers |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=29 August 2020 |access-date=29 August 2020}}</ref>

On 29 July 2021, Murphy scored his first goal for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in Europe against [[FC Santa Coloma]] in a 2–1 away win in the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League qualifying phase and play-off round#Second qualifying round|UEFA Conference League qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57972238|title=FC Santa Coloma 1–2 Hibernian|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Matthew|last=Reed|date=29 July 2021|access-date=30 July 2021}}</ref>

On 31 January 2022, Murphy joined [[Mansfield Town]], on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/jamie-murphy-joins-mansfield-town-on-loan |title=Jamie Murphy joins Mansfield Town on loan |website=hibernianfc.co.uk|date=31 January 2022|access-date=31 January 2022}}</ref> Murphy was released by Hibs in June 2022, at the end of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61675106 |title=Hibernian: Scott Allan, Alex Gogic, Drey Wright and Jamie Murphy among six exits |website=BBC Sport |date=2 June 2022 |accessdate=2 June 2022}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
Murphy signed a one-year contract with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jamie Murphy: Ex-Rangers, Motherwell & Hibernian winger signs one-year deal with St Johnstone |language=en-GB |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62047882 |access-date=5 July 2022 |date=5 July 2022}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
In June 2023, Murphy signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c9e77k8krg1o | title=Ex-Saint Murphy joins Ayr |website=BBC Sport | date=20 June 2023 | accessdate=21 June 2023}}</ref> On 26 May 2026, it was announced that Murphy would be first team coach as well as continue as a player.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.ayradvertiser.com/sport/26137589.jamie-murphy-handed-new-coaching-role-ayr-united/| title=Jamie Murphy handed new coaching role at Ayr United| publisher=Ayr Advertiser| first=Adam| last=Lyon| date=26 May 2026| access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Murphy was a regular for both the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19 team]] and the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21 team]]. He scored four goals for the under-21 side as the team reached the play-offs of the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship|European under-21 Championships]].
<ref name="Murphy Under 19's">{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=823&playerID=37450&squadID=9|title=Jamie Murphy – U19 Squad|publisher=Scottish Football Association|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref><ref name="Murphy Under 21's">{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=823&playerID=37450&CFID=1769138&CFTOKEN=29169040|title=Jamie Murphy – U21 Squad|publisher=Scottish Football Association|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref>

Murphy received his first call-up to the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad on 10 March 2016, for their friendlies against [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] and [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] on 24 and 29 March. He was left unused.<ref>{{cite web|title=Scotland squads for March double-header confirmed|url=http://scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=2986&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16049|website=scottishfa.co.uk|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]|access-date=10 March 2016|date=10 March 2016}}</ref> Murphy made his full international debut in a 1–0 home friendly defeat to [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] on 23 March 2018, coming on as an 87th-minute substitute for [[Matt Ritchie]].<ref>{{cite news |url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43380252 |title= Scotland 0–1 Costa Rica – BBC Sport |work=BBC Sport |date= 23 March 2018 }}</ref>
Murphy's second Scottish cap came in a friendly where Scotland lost 2–0 away to [[Peru national football team|Peru]] where Murphy started the game. However, he was subbed off in the 63rd minute, replaced by [[Oli McBurnie]].<ref>{{cite news |url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44219810 |title= Peru 2–0 Scotland – BBC Sport |work=BBC Sport |date= 29 May 2018 }}</ref>

'''Paul Thomas Hanlon''' (born 20 January 1990) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]]. He began his senior career with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], making his debut in 2008, and went on to make over 500 appearances for the club. He also briefly played for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on loan during the 2008–09 season.

Hanlon represented Scotland at the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels, and made one full international appearance in October 2020.

==Club career==
===Hibernian===
Hanlon played for the well known [[Edinburgh]] youth football club [[Hutchison Vale F.C.|Hutchison Vale]], along with future Hibs teammate [[Danny Galbraith]].<ref name = "striker move">{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/hibernian/2009/11/15/paul-hanlon-moving-from-a-striker-to-defence-has-been-a-learning-curve-but-i-ve-survived-86908-21823574/ |title=Paul Hanlon: Moving from a striker to defence has been a learning curve but I've survived |newspaper=[[Sunday Mail (Scotland)|Sunday Mail]]|location=Scotland |date=15 November 2009}}</ref> Hanlon was an attacking midfielder who scored plenty of goals in youth football, but was converted to a defensive position after he signed for boyhood club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibs]].<ref name = "striker move"/> He played his first senior game for Hibs on 12 January 2008, against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in the [[Scottish Cup]], due to injuries sustained by [[David Murphy (footballer, born 1984)|David Murphy]] and [[Lewis Stevenson (Scottish footballer)|Lewis Stevenson]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_cups/7181084.stm |title=Hibernian 3–0 Inverness CT |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 January 2008}}</ref> Hanlon played for Hibs on a regular basis over the next seven months, and he agreed a five-year contract with the club.<ref name = "St Johnstone take Hanlon on loan">{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/st_johnstone/7800095.stm |title=St Johnstone take Hanlon on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2008}}</ref>

During the 2008–09 season, however, Hanlon was replaced by [[Ian Murray (footballer)|Ian Murray]] as Hibs' regular left back.<ref name = "St Johnstone take Hanlon on loan"/> Hanlon was loaned out to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in December 2008, initially for one month.<ref name = "St Johnstone take Hanlon on loan"/> St Johnstone wanted to extend the loan arrangement, but Hibs refused to allow this.<ref>{{cite news |publisher=DC Thomson |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/output/2009/01/21/sportstory12528060t0.asp |title=Hanlon recall sees Saints suffer |newspaper=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605020347/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/output/2009/01/21/sportstory12528060t0.asp |archive-date=5 June 2011 }}</ref> Hanlon went straight back into the Hibs team after returning from St Johnstone, but he was dropped soon afterwards by [[Mixu Paatelainen]] due to a defensive error he made in a match against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

Hanlon played infrequently during the 2009–10 season, only featuring when one of the regular defenders was unavailable. One such period was when [[Sol Bamba]] was with the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast national team]] at the [[2010 Africa Cup of Nations]];<ref>{{cite news |url=http://edinburghnews.scotsman.com/football/Hibs-boss-reckons-Hanlon-can.6013128.jp |title=Hibs boss reckons Hanlon can handle Hoops |first=David |last=Hardie |newspaper=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=26 January 2010 |access-date=31 January 2010}}</ref> [[manager (association football)|manager]] [[John Hughes (footballer born 1964)|John Hughes]] said it was a tough decision to reinstate Bamba to the team at Hanlon's expense.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/01/31/hibs-2-st-mirren-1-86908-22008271/ |title=Hibs 2 St Mirren 1 |newspaper=[[Sunday Mail (Scotland)|Sunday Mail]]|location=Scotland |first=Rob |last=Fairburn |date=31 January 2010 |access-date=31 January 2010}}</ref> At the end of the season, Hughes commented that Hanlon was a "great" footballer, but needed to become tougher and show more desire.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/John-Hughes-urges-Paul-Hanlon.6301310.jp |title=John Hughes urges Paul Hanlon to get tough with Hibs strikers |first=David |last=Hardie |newspaper=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=18 May 2010 |access-date=18 May 2010}}</ref>

Hughes again praised Hanlon before the start of the 2010–11 season, saying that he had a "real future" in the game and had the potential to play in the [[Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/hibernian/2010/08/15/paul-hanlon-could-win-move-to-english-premier-league-like-danny-wilson-if-he-keeps-learning-says-hibs-boss-john-hughes-86908-22489179/ |title=Paul Hanlon could win move to English Premier League like Danny Wilson if he keeps learning, says Hibs boss John Hughes |last=Haggerty |first=Anthony |newspaper=[[Sunday Mail (Scotland)|Sunday Mail]]|location=Scotland |date=15 August 2010 |access-date=15 August 2010}}</ref> Following the departure of [[Chris Hogg]], Hanlon [[captain (association football)|captained]] the team at times.<ref name = "captain"/> Hanlon agreed a new contract with the club in May 2011.<ref name = "captain">{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,12875_6916212,00.html|title=Hanlon secures Hibs extension |publisher=Sky Sports |date=6 May 2011|access-date=6 May 2011}}</ref>

Hibs struggled in the 2011–12 season, only securing a place in the SPL with a 4–0 win against [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]] in early May.<ref name = "ghost"/> Hanlon scored the fourth goal, which was awarded despite the fact the ball [[Ghost goal|had not crossed the goal-line]].<ref name = "ghost">{{cite web |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/hibernian/99064-paul-hanlon-i-was-shocked-when-officials-awarded-my-ghost-goal/ |title=Paul Hanlon: 'I was shocked when officials awarded my ghost goal' |publisher=STV |website=STV Sport |date=10 May 2012 |access-date=8 February 2016 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He played in Scottish Cup final defeats in [[2012 Scottish Cup final|2012]] and [[2013 Scottish Cup final|2013]].<ref name = "2016 contract"/>

He won the club's player of the year award for the 2013–14 season, awarded in March 2014.<ref name = "poty">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26791402 |title=Hibernian defender Paul Hanlon to miss rest of season |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 March 2014 |access-date=8 February 2016}}</ref> At the same time, Hanlon was ruled out of action for the rest of the season due to a knee injury.<ref name = "poty"/> Hibs were seven points ahead of the relegation play-off position at that point,<ref name = "poty"/> but a continued bad run of results led to their eventual relegation to the [[Scottish Championship]].

In the [[2015–16 Hibernian F.C. season|2015–16 season]], Hanlon scored the winning goal in a match against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34630330|title=Hibernian 2-1 Rangers|work=BBC Sport |date=31 October 2015 }}</ref> and scored an injury-time equaliser away to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in the [[2015–16 Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35453156|title=Heart of Midlothian 2-2 Hibernian|work=BBC Sport |date=5 February 2016 }}</ref> Hibs won the replay against Hearts at [[Easter Road]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35535920|title=Hibernian 1-0 Heart of Midlothian|work=BBC Sport |date=15 February 2016 }}</ref> and went on to win the competition, defeating Rangers 3–2 in the [[2016 Scottish Cup final|final]].<ref name = "cup win">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36292302|title=Scottish Cup final: Rangers 2-3 Hibernian |date=21 May 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=21 May 2016}}</ref>

Hanlon signed a three-year contract with Hibs in June 2016.<ref name = "2016 contract">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36532255 |title=Paul Hanlon: Hibernian defender signs new three-year contract |publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 June 2016 |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref> He missed much of the second half of the 2016–17 season due to a pelvic injury,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/paul-hanlon-s-hibs-season-isn-t-over-insists-neil-lennon-1-4417415 |title=Paul Hanlon's Hibs season isn't over, insists Neil Lennon |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |first=David |last=Hardie |access-date=22 April 2017}}</ref> but the team earned promotion to the Premiership.<ref name="BBC39536738"/> He was awarded a testimonial by Hibs in March 2018,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-central-defender-paul-hanlon-awarded-testimonial-1-4702631 |title=Hibs central defender Paul Hanlon awarded testimonial |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=8 March 2018 |access-date=8 March 2018 |first=David |last=Hardie}}</ref> and soon afterwards agreed a new contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43681649 |title=Paul Hanlon: Hibernian defender signs new contract to 2022 |publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 April 2018 |access-date=7 April 2018}}</ref>

Hanlon made his 400th competitive appearance for Hibs on 23 November 2019, in a 3–1 win against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50443020 |title=Hibernian 3–1 Motherwell |publisher=BBC Sport |first=Jordan |last=Elgott |date=23 November 2019 |access-date=23 November 2019}}</ref>

Following the retirement of [[David Gray (footballer, born 1988)|David Gray]], Hanlon was appointed club [[captain (association football)|captain]] in July 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/paul-hanlon-named-new-hibs-skipper-as-club-makes-call-on-vice-captain-3315348 |title=Paul Hanlon named new Hibs skipper as club makes call on vice-captain |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=20 July 2021 |access-date=20 July 2021}}</ref> On 16 November 2021, Hanlon signed a new long-term contract with Hibernian, keeping him at the club until 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/paul-hanlon-remains-a-hibee|title=Paul Hanlon Remains A Hibee|website=Hibernian|date=16 November 2021|accessdate=16 November 2021}}</ref> Hanlon made his 500th appearance for the club on 7 May 2022, in a 1–1 draw against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite tweet |user=HibernianFC |number=1522984101845905410 |title=Ron Gordon presented Paul Hanlon with a special shirt to commemorate his 500th Hibs appearance today after the game |date=7 May 2022 |accessdate=8 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-david-gray-hails-paul-hanlon-for-playing-through-pain-barrier-to-reach-milestone-3685015 |title=Hibs: David Gray hails Paul Hanlon for playing through pain barrier to reach milestone |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=8 May 2022 |accessdate=8 May 2022}}</ref>

Hibs announced in May 2024 that Hanlon and long-serving teammate [[Lewis Stevenson (Scottish footballer)|Lewis Stevenson]] would be leaving the club at the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c3ge2rn63m4o |title=Stalwarts Hanlon & Stevenson's Hibs exits 'uncomfortable' but mutual |website=BBC Sport |date=9 May 2024 |accessdate=16 May 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/clkk3dxxw27o |title=Hibernian announce retained list |website=BBC Sport |date=10 June 2024 |accessdate=10 June 2024}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
Hanlon signed a three-year deal with [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on 20 June 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Club |first1=Raith Rovers Football |last2=Fowlie |first2=Grace |date=2024-06-20 |title=WELCOME, PAUL HANLON! |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/welcome-paul-hanlon/ |access-date=2024-07-18 |website=Raith Rovers Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Following the departure of manager [[Barry Robson]] in November 2025, Hanlon was made interim player/manager until [[Dougie Imrie]] took charge later that month.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cn8vk03jzvro |title=Raith Rovers sack manager Robson after poor run |website=BBC Sport |date=11 November 2025 |accessdate=11 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cy8j7p9n9xxo |title=Dougie Imrie: Raith Rovers appoint Greenock Morton manager as new boss |website=BBC Sport |date=25 November 2025 |accessdate=25 November 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Paul Hanlon - Schottland U-21 (2).jpg|thumb|upright|Hanlon with [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] in 2009]]

Hanlon captained [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19]],<ref name = "sfa"/><ref name = "St Johnstone take Hanlon on loan"/> and made his debut for [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] in a 1–0 win against [[Albania national under-21 football team|Albania]] in March 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/7946314.stm |title=Albania U21 0–1 Scotland U21 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 March 2009}}</ref> Hanlon was a regular in central [[defender (association football)|defence]] during the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]] campaign,<ref name = "sfa 21"/> which ended in a play-off defeat by [[Iceland national under-21 football team|Iceland]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/scotland/9080443.stm |title=Scotland U21 1–2 Iceland U21 (2–4 on agg) |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 October 2010 |access-date=11 October 2010 |last=Murray |first=Keir}}</ref> Hanlon then captained an inexperienced side in November 2010 as [[head coach]] [[Billy Stark]] made initial preparations for the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]] campaign.<ref name = "u21 captain"/> He scored the second goal in a 3–1 win for Scotland in a [[friendly match]] against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland]].<ref name = "u21 captain">{{cite news |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1884&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=6832 |title=Under-21s defeat Northern Ireland |date=17 November 2010 |access-date=18 November 2010 |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |last=Irving |first=Chris}}</ref>

Hanlon received his first call-up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad in November 2017, for a friendly match with the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41796933 |title=Scotland: Interim manager Malky Mackay calls up three new faces for friendly |publisher=BBC Sport|date=30 October 2017 |access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref> He was recalled to the squad in October 2020,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54516492 |title=Scotland v Czech Republic: Hibs captain Paul Hanlon called up |publisher=BBC Sport  |date=12 October 2020 |access-date=12 October 2020}}</ref> and made his full international debut in a 1–0 win against the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54424702 |title=Scotland 1–0 Czech Republic |publisher=BBC Sport  |date=14 October 2020 |access-date=14 October 2020}}</ref>

'''Grant Gillespie''' (born 2 July 1991) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for  {{Scottish football updater|GreenocM}} club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]]. He has previously played for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]], [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] and [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].

==Career==
===Hamilton Academical===
Gillespie made his senior debut for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on 15 August 2009, in a [[Scottish Premier League]] match against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/8200792.stm|title=Kilmarnock 3 – 0 Hamilton|access-date=15 August 2009|date=15 August 2009|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> In May 2011, he signed a new two-year contract with Hamilton.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13563453|title=Grant Gillespie signs new Hamilton Accies contract|access-date=27 May 2011|date=26 May 2011|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In May 2012, Gillespie urged manager Billy Reid to make him a first-team regular for the forthcoming 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonadvertiser.co.uk/hamilton-lanarkshire-sport/hamiltonaccies/2012/05/24/accies-midfielder-aims-to-prove-he-s-ready-for-a-regular-first-team-place-51525-31033101/|title=Accies midfielder aims to prove he's ready for a regular first-team place|date=24 May 2012|author=Andrew McGilvray|publisher=Hamilton Advertiser}}</ref> In January 2012, after making an "impact" as a substitute in the previous game, Gillespie spoke publicly about his desire to start the team's next match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonadvertiser.co.uk/hamilton-lanarkshire-sport/hamiltonaccies/2013/01/17/grant-let-me-start-the-game-at-raith-51525-32615047/|title=Grant: Let me start the game at Raith|date=17 January 2013|author=Andrew McGilvray|publisher=Hamilton Advertiser}}</ref> In February 2013, he commented that he wanted a win in the upcoming derby against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonadvertiser.co.uk/hamilton-lanarkshire-sport/hamiltonaccies/2013/02/14/dump-the-diamonds-gillespie-wants-derby-win-51525-32804183/|title=Dump the Diamonds: Gillespie wants derby win|date=14 February 2013|author=Andrew McGilvray|publisher=Hamilton Advertiser}}</ref> In April 2013, Gillespie signed a new two-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?view=article&catid=44:news&id=2190:gillespie-signs-extension&format=pdf|title=Gillespie signs Extension|date=8 April 2013|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.}}</ref>

In August 2013 Gillespie stated that the team needed to "dig in and grind out results" in the season ahead.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonadvertiser.co.uk/hamilton-lanarkshire-sport/hamiltonaccies/2013/08/15/midfielder-grant-gillespie-says-accies-need-to-dig-in-this-season-for-wins-51525-33728766/|title=Midfielder Grant Gillespie says Accies need to dig in this season for wins|date=15 August 2013|access-date=16 August 2013|author=Andrew McGilvray|publisher=Hamilton Advertiser}}</ref> In October 2014 he signed a new contract with the club, to last until the summer of 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29754084|title=Hamilton's Crawford and Gillespie agree new deals|date=24 October 2014|access-date=26 October 2014|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Gillespie left the club in January 2018.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=acciesfc|number=956941436376711168|date=26 January 2018|access-date=26 January 2018|title=With almost 500 appearances between them the club has today said Goodbye to Michael Devlin, Greg Docherty and Grant Gillespie. Statement to follow on website shortly}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
Gillespie signed a short-term contract with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42894011|title=Dundee United: Stephen Thompson to step down as chairman|date=31 January 2018|access-date=31 January 2018|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was released by the club at the end of his contract in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44130428 |title=Captain Willo Flood among Dundee United departures |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=15 May 2018 |access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
Gillespie signed with [[Scottish League One|League One]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in June 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-league-1/674008/raith-new-boy-grant-gillespie-determined-to-make-this-a-season-to-remember/|title=Raith new boy Grant Gillespie determined to make this a season to remember|first=Neil|last=Robertson}}</ref>

===Derry City===
In July 2019 he signed for [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49117428|title=Grant Gillespie: Derry City sign Scottish midfielder until end of season|date=25 July 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref> After making 10 appearances, scoring 1 goal, he left in January 2020.

===Ayr United===
In January 2020 he returned to Scotland, signing for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] until the end of their season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/grant-gillespie-signs/|title=Grant Gillespie signs – Ayr United Football Club}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.ie/articles/24319/former-candystripe-grant-gillespie-joins-ayr-united-on-a-short-term-deal/|title=Former Candystripe Grant Gillespie joins Ayr United on a short-term deal|website=ExtraTime.ie}}</ref>

===Queen's Park===
In August 2020 he signed for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/grant-gillespie-signs-for-the-spiders/|title=Grant Gillespie Signs for the Spiders|first=Ian|last=Cairns|date=11 August 2020}}</ref> before leaving in 2022.

===Greenock Morton===
In June 2022 he signed for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gmfc.net/grant-gillespie-joins-on-a-one-year-deal/|title=Grant Gillespie joins on a one-year-deal|date=20 June 2022}}</ref> Gillespie was named club captain by manager Dougie Imrie, and made his first competitive appearance against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in the League Cup Group Stage. Gillespie would score 2 times in this group, against Hibernian and [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]] respectively.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hibernian v Greenock Morton |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62210115 |access-date=10 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Greenock Morton v Bonnyrigg Rose |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62210610 |access-date=10 June 2023}}</ref> Gillespie would continue his positive start to life at Morton by scoring in the first league game of the season against his former club Hamilton.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Morton and 10-man Hamilton share points |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62275205 |access-date=10 June 2023}}</ref>

Gillespie signed a contract extension on New Year's Day, keeping him at the club until summer 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 January 2023 |title=Grant Gillespie extends his stay |url=https://www.gmfc.net/grant-gillespie-extends-his-stay/ |access-date=10 June 2023 |website=Greenock Morton FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

With Gillespie's contract expiring summer 2024, Morton announced that he had signed a new one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 May 2024 |title=Grant Gillespie signs contract extension - Greenock Morton FC |url=https://gmfc.net/grant-gillespie-signs-contract-extension/|access-date=25 June 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Michael Francis O'Halloran''' (born 6 January 1991) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].

Born in [[Glasgow]], he began his professional career with English club [[Bolton Wanderers F.C|Bolton Wanderers]], but made only made two appearances in three seasons. While at Bolton he had loan spells with [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] and [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]]. After two years with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], he moved to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in January 2016.

O'Halloran returned to St Johnstone on loan in July 2017. After a short spell with Australian club [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne City]], he returned to St Johnstone for a third spell in January 2019.

O'Halloran represented Scotland at various youth levels, up to and including the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level.

==Club career==

===Bolton Wanderers===
O'Halloran started his professional career at [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], regularly playing in the reserve side. A product of the youth system, he made his début in the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] tie at home to [[Macclesfield Town F.C.|Macclesfield Town]] on 24 August 2011, coming on as a second-half substitute for [[Martin Petrov]]. His form in the reserves prompted Bolton to offer both O'Halloran and [[Joe Riley (footballer, born 1991)|Joe Riley]] new three-and-a-half-year contracts, committing them to the club until the summer of 2015.<ref name="new contracts">{{cite web|title=Riley And O'Halloran Sign New Deals|url=http://www.bwfc.co.uk/page/General/0,,1004~2620960,00.html?|publisher=Bolton Wanderers Football Club|work=Bwfc.co.uk|date=23 February 2012|access-date=24 February 2012}}{{dead link|date=October 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In March 2012, O'Halloran joined [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] on loan until the end of the season,<ref>{{cite web|title=Sheffield United sign Michael O'Halloran on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17479970|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=22 March 2012}}</ref> and made his début for the Blades on as an 81st-minute substitute against [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] in a 4–1 victory at [[Bramall Lane]].<ref name=BladesVchesterfield>{{cite news|title=Sheffield United 4–1 Chesterfield|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17455197|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=28 April 2012}}</ref> O'Halloran was in and out of the side for the remainder of his spell, with his final appearance for the Blades coming at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] for the [[2012 Football League One play-off final|League One play-off final]] in which he came on as a substitute in extra time. O'Halloran scored in the game's penalty shoot out but United slipped to defeat.<ref name="playoff">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18127853|title=Huddersfield promoted after epic shoot-out win over Sheffield United |publisher=BBC|first=Emlyn|last= Begley |work=BBC Sport|date=26 May 2012|access-date=27 May 2012}}</ref>

In August 2012, O'Halloran joined [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] on a month's loan.<ref name="carlisle loan">{{cite web|title=Carlisle United sign Bolton's Michael O'Halloran on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19438532|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=31 August 2012}}</ref> However, after playing just one game, a substitute appearance against [[MK Dons F.C.|MK Dons]], O'Halloran opted to return to Bolton, his loan only lasting 12 days.<ref>{{cite web|title=Michael O'Halloran leaves Carlisle United for Bolton early|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19563808|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=11 September 2012}}</ref> O'Halloran then joined [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] on loan on in November of the same year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20443076|title=Tranmere sign Michael O'Halloran & Donervon Daniels on loan|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=22 November 2012}}</ref> O'Halloran scored the first professional goal of his career on 8 December as he scored in a 2–2 draw against [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20564651|title=Tranmere 2–2 Portsmouth|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=8 December 2012|access-date=3 January 2014}}</ref> O'Halloran loan was extended by a further month on 7 January 2013, and then again until the end of the season on January deadline day.<ref>{{cite news|title=O'Halloran extends Rovers stay|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11065/8385065/ohalloran-extends-rovers-stay|publisher=Sky Sports|date=7 January 2013|access-date=20 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=O'Halloran extends Rovers stay|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11065/8459198/ohalloran-extends-rovers-stay|publisher=Sky Sports|date=31 January 2013|access-date=20 February 2014}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
After appearing in just two cup matches in three years at Bolton, O'Halloran made the move back to his native Scotland with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in January 2014, signing an 18-month contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=St Johnstone sign Michael O'Halloran from Bolton Wanderers |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/spfl/st-johnstone-sign-michael-o-halloran-from-bolton-wanderers-1.172215? |publisher=DC Thomson |work=The Courier |date=3 January 2014|access-date=3 January 2014}}</ref> O'Halloran made his debut, coming on as a substitute, in a 1–0 win over [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]. Then on 8 February 2014, O'Halloran scored his first goal in the fifth round of Scottish Cup, in a 4–0 win over [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Forfar Athletic 0–4 St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25995059|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=8 February 2014|access-date=20 February 2014}}</ref> He scored again in Saints' final home game of the season, to conclude a 3–3 draw with former club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/scott-brown-and-michael-ohalloran-lead-st-johnstone-fightback-to-stun-celtic-pg2nsmqd8j7 |title=Scott Brown and Michael O'Halloran lead St Johnstone fightback to stun Celtic |work=[[The Times]] |publisher=News International |first=Phil |last=Gordon |date=7 May 2014 |access-date=18 January 2016}}</ref>

O'Halloran won the Scottish Premiership player of the month award for November 2015.<ref name="December award">{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/o039halloran-voted-player-of-the-month/ |title=O'Halloran named Player of the Month |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=3 December 2015 |access-date=18 January 2016}}</ref> St Johnstone rejected two bids from [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] for O'Halloran in January 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35312038 |title=Michael O'Halloran: Rangers bids rejected by St Johnstone |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin|work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=14 January 2016 |access-date=18 January 2016}}</ref> Manager Tommy Wright then left O'Halloran out of their following league game, saying that O'Halloran was not "mentally ready" to play. O'Halloran made his final appearance for the club in a 2–1 defeat to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] semi final at [[Tynecastle Stadium|Tynecastle]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35333919 |title=Michael O'Halloran 'still a St Johnstone player' – Tommy Wright |first=Liam |last=McLeod|work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=16 January 2016 |access-date=18 January 2016}}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 1 February 2016, after much speculation, O'Halloran signed a four-and-a-half-year deal with the then [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] for a fee reported to be £500,000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/headlines/rangers-sign-michael-ohalloran/ |title=Rangers Sign Michael O'Halloran |last= Thomson |first=Nick |publisher=Rangers Football Club|work=Rangers.co.uk |date=1 February 2016 |access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Ibrox club as a substitute in a 1–0 victory against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] at [[Stark's Park]] on 2 February 2016. He scored his first goal for the club in a 1–1 draw with [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] on 13 February 2016.<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35510620 | title=Alloa Athletic 1–1 Rangers | date=13 February 2016 | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | first=Jonathan |last=Sutherland}}</ref> He picked up a winners' medal in the [[2016 Scottish Challenge Cup Final]] at [[Hampden Park]] after defeating [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] 4–0 on 10 April 2016<ref name="Rangers 4-0 Peterhead">{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35953055| publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | first=Tom |last=English | date=10 April 2016 | title=Rangers 4–0 Peterhead}}</ref> and helped Rangers win promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref name = "saints loan"/>

O'Halloran fell out of favour during the 2016–17 season, playing mainly as a substitute.<ref name = "saints loan"/> He returned to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on loan in July 2017.<ref name = "saints loan">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40763476 |title=Michael O'Halloran: St Johnstone take Rangers winger back to Perth on loan |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=29 July 2017 |access-date=29 July 2017}}</ref> On his first appearance back at the club, he scored the winning goal in a 2–1 victory away to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kilmarnock 1–2|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40761234|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Crawford|first=Kenny|date=5 August 2017|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> After scoring four goals in his first five appearances back at the club, O'Halloran won the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2017–18 season|Scottish Premiership Player of the month award]] for August.<ref name="August award">{{cite web|title=St Johnstone's Tommy Wright and Michael O'Halloran take monthly awards|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41161876|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 September 2017|access-date=4 December 2017}}</ref>

O'Halleron controversially attended a Scottish Cup Final involving Celtic while he was still a Rangers player.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/rugby-union/agent-explains-why-michael-ohalloran-watched-cup-final-in-celtic-end-1429338|title=Agent explains why Michael O'Halloran watched Cup final in Celtic end|date=21 May 2018|website=The Scotsman|access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref>  To most observers this looked like a Rangers player supporting their arch rivals Celtic. O'Halleron stated that his intention was to attend the match viewing from a neutral section of the ground.  This seems at best implausible and at worst incredible.  O'Halleron regretted his decision to attend.  It did not endear him to Rangers fans.

===Melbourne City===
O'Halloran signed a two-year contract with Australian club [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne City]] in June 2018.<ref name = "melbourne">{{cite news |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/melbourne-city-sign-glasgow-rangers-winger-20180617-p4zm19.html |title=Melbourne City sign Glasgow Rangers winger |first=Michael |last=Lynch |work=Sydney Morning Herald |date=17 June 2018 |access-date=17 June 2018}}</ref> O'Halloran had played in the same youth team as Australian international [[Aaron Mooy]], who recommended the move to him.<ref name = "melbourne"/> He stayed at the club for only six months, being released by the club on 8 January 2019 on compassionate grounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-au/news/melbourne-city-release-ohalloran-as-baccus-locked-down/18fctlwikxn2w1iwonk0k6qxu1|title=Melbourne City release O'Halloran as Baccus locked down|work=Goal.com|date=8 January 2019}}</ref>

===St Johnstone (second spell)===
O'Halloran returned to Scotland in January 2019, re-signing for St Johnstone for a second time.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/16213/11610954/st-johnstone-re-sign-michael-ohalloran-after-curtailed-spell-in-australia |title=St Johnstone re-sign Michael O'Halloran after curtailed spell in Australia |work=skysports.com |publisher=Sky Sports News |date=18 January 2019 |access-date=26 December 2021}}</ref>

==== Cove Rangers (loan) ====
On 24 February 2023, O'Halloran joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael O'Halloran heads to Cove on loan |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/ |access-date=2023-02-25 |website=St Johnstone Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

=== Dunfermline Athletic ===
Following his release from St Johnstone, O'Halloran signed for [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://dafc.co.uk/michael-ohalloran-joins-dunfermline/ | title=Michael O'Halloran joins Dunfermline | Dunfermline Athletic Football Club – | date=9 July 2023 }}</ref>

==International career==
O'Halloran represented Scotland at various age levels up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21 team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=40469&squadID=5 |title=Michael O'Halloran |work=www.scottishfa.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Football Association |access-date=26 October 2015}}</ref> He made his Scotland under-21 debut on 29 February 2012, appearing as a substitute in a 0–0 draw with the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17200423 | title=Scotland U21 0–0 Netherlands U21 | work=BBC Sport | publisher=BBC | date=29 February 2012 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
O'Halloran's father, Michael senior, is a youth coach at [[Old Firm]] rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. Although he never coached his son.<ref>{{ cite news | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/new-rangers-forward-michael-ohalloran-7367382| publisher=Trinity Mirror| work=Daily Record | location=London|first=Euan |last=McLean| date=14 February 2016 | title=New Rangers forward Michael O'Halloran thrills his Celtic coach dad after salvaging draw against Alloa}}</ref>

'''Callum Fordyce''' (born 23 June 1992) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]], and is a [[Soccer player|player]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers]]. Fordyce started his career as a youth player with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], before signing with the ''Lions'' on a permanent senior contract, before going on to play for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] and [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] then [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] as a player/coach role. Fordyce also had a loan spell at [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] whilst at the [[West Lothian]] club.

==Career==
===Livingston===
Fordyce joined [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]'s youth system from [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/team_profiles/team_fordyce.php | title=Callum Fordyce Livingston Profile | publisher=[[Livingston F.C.]] | date=2 January 2012 | accessdate=3 January 2012}}</ref> A member of the ''Lions'' under-19s,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/team_u19.php | title=Under 19 Squad 2010–11 | publisher=Livingston Fc | accessdate=20 August 2011 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213162035/http://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/team_u19.php | archivedate=13 February 2012 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> Fordyce made his senior debut on 23 April 2011, playing from the start in a 4–2 win versus [[Airdrie United F.C.|Airdrie United]] in the [[Scottish Second Division]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/9465300.stm | title=Airdrie Utd 2–4 Livingston | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=23 April 2011 | access-date=3 January 2012}}</ref> Fordyce made two more appearances that season.<ref name=CF1011>{{Soccerbase season|59345|2010|accessdate=3 January 2012}}</ref> Fordyce's next appearance was in the following season on 2 January 2011 as a substitute versus [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in the [[Scottish First Division]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/football/first/results/3408581/ | title=Livingston 1 – 2 Falkirk | publisher=Scottish Football League | date=2 January 2012 | accessdate=3 January 2012 | March 2013, Fordyce moved to [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] on a short-term loan deal <ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/fordyce-heads-for-clyde/ | title=Fordyce heads for Clyde | publisher=[[Scottish Football League]] | work=scottishfootballleague.com | date=19 March 2013 | accessdate=28 March 2013 |
