made six appearances in total.<ref name="Fordyce">{{cite web | url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=59345 | title=Callum Fordyce Stats | publisher=Soccerbase | accessdate=3 January 2012}}</ref> Fordyce extended his stay with Livingston by signing a new one-year contract in May 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/news/news_20130503_1.php | title=Dycey signs new contract | publisher=[[Livingston F.C.]] | date=3 May 2013 | accessdate=3 May 2013}}</ref>

===Dunfermline Athletic===
In June 2015, after six years with Livingston, Fordyce signed for [[Scottish League One]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Another defender signed |url=http://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Another_defender_signed&ID=8535 |work=dafc.co.uk |accessdate=15 June 2015 |date=15 June 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/dunfermline-bring-in-fordyce/ |title=Dunfermline bring in Fordyce |work=www.spfl.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=16 June 2015 |accessdate=17 June 2015 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and was appointed [[captain (association football)|first-team captain]] by manager [[Allan Johnston]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Leading_the_Way&ID=8635 |title=Leading the way |publisher=dafc.co.uk |date=6 August 2015 |accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> On 12 September 2015 in a match versus [[Scottish League One]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], Fordyce was injured in a tackle by Ayr striker [[Craig Moore (footballer, born 1994)|Craig Moore]], suffering a suspected broken leg.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://dafc.co.uk/fixture.php?SID=First%20Team&D=2015-09-12&ID=852# |title=Dunfermline 0 Ayr United 2 |publisher=dafc.co.uk |date=12 September 2015 |accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/dunfermline-0-ayr-utd-2/ |title=Dunfermline 0 Ayr United 2 |publisher=ayrunitedfc.co.uk |date=12 September 2015 |accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> Fordyce was released by the Pars at the end of the [[2016–17 in Scottish football|2016–17]] season, as his contract expired.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Fordyce_Departs&ID=9996 |title=Fordyce departs |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=18 May 2017 |accessdate=18 May 2017}}</ref>

===Queen of the South===
On 23 May 2017, Fordyce signed a one-year contract with fellow [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40068019|title=Queens sign Martin amid English interest|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 1 February 2018, Fordyce signed an extension to his contract to remain in [[Dumfries]] until May 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.qosfc.com/news-3909 |title=Callum Extends His Stay |publisher=Queen of the South FC |date=1 February 2018 |accessdate=1 February 2018}}</ref>

===Airdrieonians===
On 30 May 2019, Fordyce signed a one-year contract with [[Scottish League One]] club [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Fordyce makes Airdrie switch|url=https://www.airdriefc.com/1819-news/Fordyce-makes-Airdrie-switch|publisher=Airdrieonians F.C.|date=30 May 2019|accessdate=25 June 2019}}</ref>

On 26 May 2022, Fordyce was named as [[Player-coach|player-assistant manager]] of Airdrieonians alongside player-manager [[Rhys McCabe]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rhys McCabe named new Diamonds manager |url=https://www.airdriefc.com/2122-news/220526/rhys-mccabe-named-new-diamonds-manager |access-date=2022-05-26 |website=airdrie |language=en}}</ref>
Fordyce played a key role in helping Airdrieonians gain promotion back to the Scottish Championship via the play-offs at the end of the 2022–23 season scoring in the play-off semi-final against Falkirk.
Played in the Scottish Challenge Cup Final for Airdrieonians in their 2–1 victory over The New Saints at the Falkirk Stadium.
On 26 May 2024, it was announced that Fordyce would leave the club upon expiry of his contract after 5 years at the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Defender Fordyce moves on |url=https://www.airdriefc.com/2324-news/240526/defender-fordyce-moves-on |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=airdrie |language=en}}</ref>

=== Raith Rovers ===
On 28 May 2024, Fordyce joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Club |first1=Raith Rovers Football |last2=niallrussell |date=2024-05-28 |title=WELCOME, CALLUM FORDYCE! |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/callum-fordyce-signs/ |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=Raith Rovers Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Dylan Easton''' (born 6 April 1994) is a Scottish footballer who plays as an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] or [[Forward (association football)|second striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers]].

Easton has previously played with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]], [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] and [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]], [[Kelty Hearts]], [[Airdrieonians]], as well as [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] and [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan.

==Career==

===Livingston===
Easton signed for Livingston in July 2011<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/team_profiles/u19/team_easton.php | title=Dylan Easton Livingston Profile | publisher=[[Livingston F.C.]] | accessdate=13 February 2012}}</ref> from [[Lothian Thistle F.C.|Hutchison Vale]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.hutchisonvale.com/modules/page/Page.aspx?pc=1940&mid=21254&pmid=0 | title=EX-HUTCHISON VALE PLAYERS | publisher=Hutchison Vale | accessdate=13 February 2012 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130126001404/http://www.hutchisonvale.com/modules/page/Page.aspx?pc=1940&mid=21254&pmid=0 | archivedate=26 January 2013 }}</ref> A member of their under 19 squad,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/team_u19.php |title=Under 19's Squad 2011–12 |publisher=[[Livingston F.C.]] |accessdate=13 February 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213162035/http://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/team_u19.php |archivedate=13 February 2012 }}</ref> he made his first team debut aged 17 as a substitute against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on 11 February 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/football/first/results/3408936/ | title=Livingston 3 – 1 Partick Thistle | publisher=[[Scottish Football League]] | date=11 February 2012 | accessdate=13 February 2012 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120523072056/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/football/first/results/3408936/ | archivedate=23 May 2012 }}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
In 2013, Easton signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Scottish Premier League]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. Easton left the club by mutual consent in August 2015.

====Dumbarton (loan)====
He joined Dumbarton on loan in January 2015<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=1686|title=Dumbarton Football Club - LOAN SIGNING - DYLAN JOINS FROM SAINTS}}</ref> and made his debut in a 5–1 defeat to Livingston.

===Elgin City===
In October 2015, Easton signed a contract agreement until the summer 2016 after he left St Johnstone by mutual consent in August 2015. Easton's attacking instincts produced many goal assists during his short time with the club. He was a fans favourite with several his fine displays, and was one of the star players of the season. Easton helped to lead the club to a 2nd-place finish and the promotion the play-offs. He was also named in the Ladbrokes Scottish League Two Team of the Season for 2015–16.

===Clyde===
On 28 May 2016, it was announced that Easton had signed for [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2016/05/28/5195/#.V0lOjmP3ekg |title=Dylan Easton Signs for Clyde |publisher=Clyde FC |date=28 May 2016 |accessdate=28 May 2016}}</ref> After a positive start to his career at Clyde, Easton was ruled out for an extended period after rupturing his cruciate ligament in Clyde's 3–2 win over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://m.clydefc.co.uk/news/2016/09/13/5284/#.V9gg7jR4WnM | title =Easton Ruled Out for Season| publisher=[[Clyde F.C.]] | accessdate=13 September 2016}}</ref>
However, Easton still managed to win Clyde FC Goal of the Season 2016–17. The midfielder's excellent strike against Montrose in August was the most popular from a shortlist of six, in an online vote. The goal was also included in the shortlist for the PFA Scotland Goal of the Season. He left Clyde in June 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2017/06/11/5512/#.WT6ahmjyiUk |title=Dylan Easton Moves On |publisher=Clyde FC |date=11 June 2017 |accessdate=12 June 2017}}</ref>

===Forfar Athletic===
He signed a two-year contract with [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on 20 June 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.forfarathletic.co.uk/index.php?option=com_flexicontent&view=items&cid=6%3Anews&id=2832%3Adylan-easton-joins-the-loons&Itemid=27 |title=Dylan Easton joins the 'Loons' |publisher=Forfar Athletic FC |date=20 June 2017 |accessdate=24 June 2017 |archive-date=17 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180717213032/http://www.forfarathletic.co.uk/index.php?option=com_flexicontent&view=items&cid=6%3Anews&id=2832%3Adylan-easton-joins-the-loons&Itemid=27 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Kelty Hearts===
Easton joined [[Lowland Football League|Lowland League]] club [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] in June 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kelty Hearts signal ambition after signing Championship striker|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/kelty-hearts-signal-ambition-after-signing-championship-striker-1-4930138|access-date=2019-06-21|website=www.scotsman.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Airdrieonians===
On 11 June 2021, Easton signed for [[Scottish League One]] side [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.airdriefc.com/2122-news/210611/diamond-dylan-on-board |title=Diamond Dylan on board |publisher=Airdrieonians FC |date=11 June 2021 |accessdate=8 November 2021}}</ref>

Easton helped the side to the Championship play offs scoring 8 goals and 12 assists, making him the highest assister in League 1.
He won Airdrieonians Player of the Season and the Scottish PFA League 1 player of the year as well as being named in Scotlands PFA League 1 Team of the Year.

===Raith Rovers===

On 26 May 2022, Easton joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a 2-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/54819/dylan-easton-checks-in-to-starks-park.htm|title=Dylan Easton checks in to Stark's Park|publisher=Raith Rovers FC|date=26 May 2022|accessdate=26 May 2022}}</ref>

In March 2013, he stated that the club was no longer in a relegation fight, and was aiming to get as high in the table as possible.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonadvertiser.co.uk/hamilton-lanarkshire-sport/hamiltonaccies/2013/03/28/louis-targets-raith-51525-33071705/|title=Louis targets Raith|date=28 March 2013|author=Andrew McGilvray|publisher=Hamilton Advertiser}}</ref> In March 2014 he signed a new two-year contract extension with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?view=article&catid=44:news&id=2567:longridge-signs-extension&format=pdf|title=Longridge signs extension|date=2 April 2014|accessdate=2 April 2014|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in January 2016, until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/he-s-young-fit-quick-raith-boss-delighted-with-new-loan-signing-1-3997765|title="He's young, fit & quick!" - Raith boss delighted with new loan signing|date=11 January 2016|accessdate=11 January 2016|publisher=Fife Today}}</ref>

===Falkirk===
In October 2017, he signed for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on an emergency loan deal until the start of January 2018,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/15630550.Hamilton_Accies_striker_Louis_Longridge_joins_Falkirk_on_emergency_loan_deal/ |title=Hamilton Accies striker Louis Longridge joins Falkirk on emergency loan deal |first=Alasdair |last=Mackenzie |work=The Herald|location=Glasgow |publisher=Herald & Times Group |date=31 October 2017 |accessdate=31 October 2017}}</ref> whereupon he signed a permanent deal until the end of the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/louis-longridge-signs-permanent-deal/ |title=Louis Longridge signs permanent deal |publisher=Falkirk FC |date=5 January 2018 |accessdate=5 January 2018}}</ref> Longridge left Falkirk at the end of this contract, as the player and the club were unable to agree a new deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/longridge-welsh-depart/ |title=Longridge & Welsh Depart |publisher=Falkirk FC |date=16 May 2018 |accessdate=16 May 2018}}</ref>

===Dunfermline===
In June 2018, Longridge signed for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref name = "dunfermline"/> He joined the club at the same time as his brother [[Jackson Longridge|Jackson]].<ref name = "dunfermline">{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Longridge_Brothers_Sign&ID=10644 |title=LONGRIDGE BROTHERS SIGN |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=1 June 2018 |accessdate=1 June 2018}}</ref> After a year with the side, Longridge departed the club in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Player_Update_&ID=11225 |title=Player update |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=6 May 2019 |accessdate=6 May 2019}}</ref>

===Return to Falkirk===
Longridge returned to Falkirk in August 2019, signing a short-term contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/louis-longridge-falkirk-sign-former-dunfermline-striker-1-4977619 |title=Louis Longridge: Falkirk sign former Dunfermline striker |work=Falkirk Herald |date=6 August 2019 |accessdate=7 August 2019 |first=Craig |last=Turnbull}}</ref> He left Falkirk at the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/pictures-nine-players-departing-falkirk-summer-2884516|title=IN PICTURES: The nine players departing Falkirk this summer|website=falkirkherald.co.uk}}</ref>

===Queen's Park===
In August 2020, Longridge signed for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/new-signing-louis-longridge/|title=New Signing – Louis Longridge | Queen's Park Football Club}}</ref>

'''Jackson Longridge''' (born 12 April 1995) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].

Longridge previously played for [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], [[Torquay United F.C.|Torquay United]], [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]], Livingston and [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Career==
Longridge made his debut for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in a [[Scottish Football League First Division|First Division]] match against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], that Ayr won 3–2, winning the 'Man of the Match' award.<ref name="audtjlgcthd">{{Cite web |date=4 May 2012 |title=Ayr United Debut Teenager Jackson Longridge Gives Champagne To His Dad |url=http://www.ayrshirepost.net/ayrshire-sport/ayrshire-football/ayr-utd-fc/2012/05/04/ayr-united-debut-teenager-jackson-longridge-gives-champagne-to-his-dad-102545-30884604/ |access-date=18 July 2012 |publisher=[[Ayrshire Post]]}}</ref> In the play-off semi-final match, against [[Airdrie United F.C.|Airdrie United]] on 12 May 2012, he was sent off by referee [[Steven McLean (referee)|Steven McLean]] for an over the ball challenge on Ricki Lamie.<ref name="au13au">{{Cite web |date=12 May 2012 |title=Ayr United 1-3 Airdrie United |url=http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/news.asp?int_news_id=2962&bln_archive=yes&int_month=5&int_year=2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130419160207/http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/news.asp?int_news_id=2962&bln_archive=yes&int_month=5&int_year=2012 |archive-date=19 April 2013 |access-date=18 July 2012 |publisher=[[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]]}}</ref>

On 18 June 2014, he signed for [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]]. Longridge scored his first senior goal in a 4–2 victory over [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on 10 January 2015. Longridge signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in June 2015. He helped them win successive promotions in 2016–17 and 2017–18.

In June 2018, Longridge signed for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a two-year contract.<ref name="dunfermline" /> He signed for the club at the same time as his brother [[Louis Longridge|Louis]].<ref name="dunfermline">{{Cite web |date=1 June 2018 |title=Longridge brothers sign |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Longridge_Brothers_Sign&ID=10644 |access-date=1 June 2018 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC}}</ref> After one season with Dunfermline, he signed a two-year contract with [[EFL League Two]] club [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 June 2019 |title=Jackson Longridge: Bradford City sign defender from Dunfermline Athletic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48624654 |access-date=13 June 2019 |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Torquay United F.C.|Torquay United]] in January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bantams defender goes on loan to Torquay United |url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/18152699.bantams-defender-jackson-longridge-goes-loan-torquay-united/ |website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus |date=10 January 2020 }}</ref>

On 19 January 2021, Longridge left [[Bradford City F.C.|Bradford City]] by mutual consent,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2021/january/longridge-leaves-utilita-energy-stadium/ |title=Longridge leaves Utilita Energy Stadium |publisher=Bradford City AFC |date=19 January 2021 |access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref> and returned to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55725040|title=Longridge returns to Livingston|work=BBC Sport|date=19 January 2021}}</ref> Longridge was loaned to [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] in March 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cx9q12xw4zqo |title=Longridge departs on loan |website=BBC Sport |date=1 March 2023 |accessdate=1 March 2023}}</ref>

Longridge signed for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on 19 June 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/former-livingston-defender-joins-hamilton-30267124|title=Former Livingston defender joins Hamilton Accies|website=Daily Record|date=19 June 2023}}</ref>

'''Scott David Brown''' (born 25 November 1994) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] as a [[midfielder]].<ref name="soccerway">{{soccerway|scott-brown/257986|Scott Brown}}</ref>

==Career==
Following a trial in June 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13939127|title=Bradford City take five players on pre-season trials|date=28 June 2011|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Brown moved from [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] to [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] in July 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14041906|title=Bradford City sign Scottish midfielder Scott Brown|date=6 July 2011|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his senior debut for them in a 1–1 draw against [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] in the [[FA Cup]] on 3 November 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20107719|title=Northampton 1 – 1 Bradford|date=3 November 2012|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was offered a professional contract by the club on 11 April 2013, alongside Louie Swain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/article/duo-awarded-pro-deals-766273.aspx|title=Duo awarded pro deals|date=11 April 2013|publisher=Bradford City A.F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/sportbcfc/10349720.Bradford_City_duo_offered_pro_deals/|title=Bradford City duo offered pro deals|date=11 April 2013|author=Simon Parker|publisher=Telegraph & Argus}}</ref> In July 2013, it was announced that Brown was close to transferring to Scottish club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/sportbcfc/10563903.Bantams_teenager_Brown_set_to_sign_for_St_Johnstone/|title=Bantams teenager Scott Brown set to sign for St Johnstone|date=22 July 2013|author=Simon Parker|publisher=Telegraph & Argus}}</ref> and Bradford City's official website confirmed he would not be given a 2013–14 squad number because of the proposed move.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/article/shirt-numbers-confirmed-947326.aspx|title=Squad numbers confirmed|date=27 July 2013|publisher=Bradford City A.F.C.}}</ref> The deal was completed later that month.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/st-johnstone/st-johnstone-sign-newcastle-starlet-1.120886|title=St Johnstone sign Newcastle starlet|date=16 August 2013|accessdate=22 November 2013|author=James Mason|work=Evening Telegraph}}</ref>

Brown made his St Johnstone debut on 5 October 2013 against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in the Premiership, coming on as a substitute for [[David Wotherspoon (footballer, born 1990)|David Wotherspoon]] in the 86th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24349649|title=St Johnstone 4–0 Inverness CT|work=BBC Sport|date=5 October 2013|access-date=18 November 2013}}</ref> He scored his first senior goal on 7 May 2014 in St Johnstone's 3–3 draw at home to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27216459|title=St Johnstone 3 – 3 Celtic|date=7 May 2014|access-date=9 May 2014|author=Cheri Burns|work=BBC Sport|quote=...youngster Scott Brown scored his first goal in senior football...}}</ref>

He signed for [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan on 20 August 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=2031|title=Dumbarton Football Club - SIGNING NEWS: ON-LOAN MIDFIELDER ARRIVES}}</ref> He left at the end of his loan deal in January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=2217|title=Dumbarton Football Club - LOAN UPDATE}}</ref>

He moved to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/54883/scott-brown-becomes-ian-murrays-second-arrival.htm|title=Scott Brown Joins Rovers | Raith Rovers FC|website=www.raithrovers.net}}</ref>

'''Eamonn Brophy''' (born 10 March 1996) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].

Brophy has previously played for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], and made his senior international debut for Scotland in 2019.

==Club career==
Brophy is a product of the [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] youth systems, but both considered him too short at the time.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-heartbreak-spurred-on-kilmarnock-13254636 | title='Celts exit fuelled me' Eamonn Brophy defying doubters who said he was too small | date=16 September 2018 }}</ref> He turned professional with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in July 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1884:new-signings&catid=44:news&Itemid=140|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130706195115/http://www.acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1884:new-signings&catid=44:news&Itemid=140|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 July 2013|title=New Signings|date=15 July 2012|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 9 April 2013, scoring a goal in the process.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=2192:accies-5-airdrie-united-0&catid=79:season-2012-13|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130706201222/http://acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=2192:accies-5-airdrie-united-0&catid=79:season-2012-13|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 July 2013|title=Accies 5 Airdrie United 0|date=9 April 2013|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22088504|title=Hamilton Academical 5–0 Airdrie Utd|date=9 April 2013|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonadvertiser.co.uk/hamilton-lanarkshire-sport/hamiltonaccies/2013/04/11/five-star-show-from-hamilton-puts-diamonds-closer-to-drop-51525-33152104/|title=Five-star show from Hamilton puts Diamonds closer to drop|date=11 April 2013|author=Andrew McGilvray|publisher=Hamilton Advertiser}}</ref>

On 6 March 2014, Brophy signed for [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on loan until the end of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brophy goes out on loan|url=http://www.acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=2533:brophy-goes-out-on-loan&catid=44:news&Itemid=140|publisher=acciesfc.co.uk|date=6 March 2014|access-date=6 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306184754/http://www.acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=2533:brophy-goes-out-on-loan&catid=44:news&Itemid=140|archive-date=6 March 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 8 March 2014, scoring in a 3–1 defeat against [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Queen's Park 1–3 Clyde|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26396773|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 March 2014|access-date=10 March 2014}}</ref>

He joined [[Scottish Championship]] outfit [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan in September 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=2074|title=Dumbarton Football Club – LOAN SIGNING: BROPHY JOINS FROM ACCIES|website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref>

On 18 August 2017, Brophy signed for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], on a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kilmarnock sign Eamonn Brophy and Brad Spencer|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40981144|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 August 2017|access-date=18 August 2017}}</ref> On the last day of the 2018–19 season, Brophy's 89th-minute penalty saw Kilmarnock beat [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] 2–1 to seal a place in the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League]] – the first time the club had qualified for a European competition since the [[2001–02 UEFA Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kilmarnock 2–1 Rangers: Steve Clarke's side finish third to qualify for Europe |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48242023 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2019 |access-date=20 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/late-eamonn-brophy-penalty-seals-kilmarnocks-place-in-europe-v2rmz8x7n|title=Late Eamonn Brophy penalty seals Kilmarnock's place in Europe|first=Graham|last=Spiers|date=20 May 2019|website=[[The Times]]|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref>

Brophy signed a pre-contract agreement with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in January 2021 to transfer in the summer, although St Mirren were hoping to sign him that month instead.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3876-st-mirren-delighted-to-confirm-signing-of-eamonn-brophy-on-pre-contract|title=St Mirren delighted to confirm signing of Eamonn Brophy on pre-contract|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/news/st-mirren-confirm-eamonn-brophy-capture-as-jim-goodwin-hails-saints-bound-striker/|title=St Mirren confirm Eamonn Brophy capture as Jim Goodwin hails Saints-bound striker|date=6 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/st-mirren-aiming-to-sign-brophy-in-january-transfer-window?top |title=St Mirren aiming to sign Eamonn Brophy in January window |website=STV News |date=5 January 2021 |access-date=5 January 2021}}</ref> Kilmarnock manager [[Alex Dyer (footballer, born 1965)|Alex Dyer]] said that he "probably" wouldn't select Brophy again, as the player wanted to leave the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55543614 |title=Eamonn Brophy: Striker played last game for Kilmarnock, says Alex Dyer |website=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2021 |access-date=8 January 2021}}</ref> Brophy was loaned to St Mirren for the rest of the 2020–21 season, filling the period before his permanent move.<ref>{{cite web |title=St Mirren sign Kilmarnock's Eamonn Brophy on loan after securing Collin Quaner |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55596234 |date=8 January 2021 |access-date=8 January 2021}}</ref>

In January 2023, he moved on loan to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64403829|title=Brophy switches to County from St Mirren on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=25 January 2023 }}</ref> The transfer was made permanent in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66054567|title=St Mirren sell Brophy to County and sign Nahmani|work=BBC Sport |date=29 June 2023 }}</ref> In January 2025, after falling out-of-favour at Ross County, he signed on loan for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/eamonn-brophy-joins-falkirk-on-loan|title=Eamonn Brophy joins Falkirk on loan|website=RCFC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/eamonn-brophy-out-of-favour-ross-county-forward-joins-falkirk-on-loan-4936792|title=Eamonn Brophy: Out-of-favour Ross County forward joins Falkirk on loan|date=9 January 2025|website=Falkirk Herald}}</ref>

In August 2025 he left Ross County by mutual consent,<ref>{{cite web | title=Eamonn Brophy Departs Ross County | url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/eamonn-brophy-departs-ross-county }}</ref> in order to sign for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Imrie lays down marker to Ton rivals with statement signing of ex-Scotland striker | work=Greenock Telegraph | date=August 2025 | url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/news/25360003.morton-gauntlet-signing-forward-eamonn-brophy-announced/ }}</ref>

==International career==
Brophy has played for Scotland at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=114420&lid=9|title=Eamonn Brophy – Scotland – Scottish FA|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref> He was selected for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad for the first time in October 2016, for a friendly match against [[Slovakia national under-21 football team|Slovakia]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37821662 |title=Scotland Under-21s: Morton winger Jai Quitongo given first call-up |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=31 October 2016 |access-date=31 October 2016}}</ref> in which he made his debut as Scotland lost 4–0 on 9 November 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=International friendly: Slovakia U21 4–0 Scotland U21|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37930204|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 November 2016|access-date=16 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=114420&lid=5|title=Eamonn Brophy – Scotland – Scottish FA|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref>

He received his first call-up to the Scotland senior national team for [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] fixtures in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48430589|title=Scotland squad: Steve Clarke selects five uncapped players|date=28 May 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 8 June 2019 in a 2–1 victory against [[Cyprus national football team|Cyprus]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref>[https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/eamonn-brophy-shows-qualities-which-led-to-scotland-debut-cap-1-4943833 Eamonn Brophy shows qualities which led to Scotland debut cap], The Scotsman, 8 June 2019</ref>

'''Scott Cameron McMann''' (born 9 July 1996) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|AyrUnite}} club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].

==Club career==
Raised in [[Torrance, East Dunbartonshire]],<ref>[https://www.glasgowworld.com/sport/football/bishopbriggs-club-helping-to-nurture-the-stars-of-tomorrow-2747624?amp Bishopbriggs club helping to nurture the stars of tomorrow], Glasgow World, 28 June 2012</ref> McMann turned professional with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in July 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1884:new-signings&catid=44:news&Itemid=140|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130706195115/http://www.acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1884:new-signings&catid=44:news&Itemid=140|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 July 2013|title=New Signings|date=15 July 2012|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 16 April 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22178262|title=Livingston 0-0 Hamilton Academical|date=16 April 2013|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In February 2016, McMann moved on loan to [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] for the remainder of the [[2015–16 in Scottish football|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/mcmann-goes-on-loan-to-clyde/ |title=McMann goes on loan to Clyde |publisher=hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk |date=1 February 2016 |access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref> In October 2019, he signed a new contract with Hamilton until 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/scott-mcmann-signs-new-deal/|title=Scott McMann Signs New Deal|date=4 October 2019|website=Hamilton Academical Website}}</ref>

He signed for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on 31 August 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6991/WELCOME-TO-TANNADICE-SCOTT-MCMANN.html|title=WELCOME TO TANNADICE SCOTT MCMANN|website=Dundee United Football Club}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58403623|title=Dundee Utd sign McMann after Robson exit|work=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2021 }}</ref>

On 16 June 2024, McMann signed for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] upon his release from Dundee United.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scott McMann Joins The Honest Men|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/scott-mcmann-joins-the-honest-men|access-date=2024-07-16|website=Ayr United FC|language=en-gb}}</ref>

==International career==
He has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] international levels.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=138649&squadID=17|title=Scotland U16 profile|publisher=Scottish FA}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=138649&squadID=13|title=Scotland U17 profile|publisher=Scottish FA}}</ref>

'''Euan Murray''' (born 20 January 1994) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen’s Park]].

He began his career at [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and has also played for [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]], [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] and [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], as well as English clubs [[Barrow A.F.C.|Barrow]], [[Southport F.C.|Southport]], and [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]] and in the [[Solomon Islands]] for [[Western United FC (Solomon Islands)|Western United]].

==Career==
Murray is a product of the [[Motherwell F.C. Reserve and Youth squads|Motherwell Academy]], regularly turning out for their under-20 squad. On 9 November 2013, Murray made his debut for Motherwell as a substitute in a 4–0 defeat against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24783006|title=Motherwell 0–4 Dundee United|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=9 November 2013|access-date=9 November 2013}}</ref>

Having left Motherwell at the end of the 2013–14 season, Murray played as a trialist for [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] against [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]] on 9 August 2014<ref>{{cite web|title=Berwick 1–2 Arbroath|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28647632|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 August 2014|access-date=19 September 2014}}</ref><ref name="clyde">{{cite web|title=Murray joins Clyde|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/murray-joins-clyde/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=19 September 2014|accessdate=19 September 2014|archive-date=29 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029065923/https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/murray-joins-clyde/|url-status=dead}}</ref> before signing for [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] on 19 September 2014.<ref name="clyde"/> On 23 December 2014, he was released by Clyde.<ref>{{cite web|title=Players Moving On|url=http://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2014/12/23/4804/#.VLcbe6-zWUk|publisher=Clyde F.C.|date=23 December 2014|accessdate=15 January 2015}}</ref> In 2015, Murray signed for [[Western United FC (Solomon Islands)|Western United]] in the [[Solomon Islands]] ahead of their [[2014–15 OFC Champions League|OFC Champions League]] campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Euan aims to star in Western role|url=http://www.motherwelltimes.co.uk/sport/local-sport/euan-aims-to-star-in-western-role-1-3720544|work=Motherwell Times|date=19 March 2015|accessdate=8 July 2015}}</ref>

Having returned to Scotland, Murray signed for [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on 8 July 2015,<ref>{{cite web|title=Player New – Latest Update|url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2015/07/07/1266/|last=Bulloch|first=Terry|date=8 July 2015|accessdate=8 July 2015|archive-date=29 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029012801/http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2015/07/07/1266/|url-status=dead}}</ref> however, he left the club in May 2016 after declining the offer of a new contract to pursue a full-time offer from an English club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2016/05/20/1404/|title=May 2016 {{!}} Interview with the Manager: updated! {{!}} News {{!}} Stenhousemuir Football Club|website=www.stenhousemuirfc.com|accessdate=28 June 2016}}</ref> On 22 July 2016, Murray signed for English [[National League (division)|National League]] club [[Barrow A.F.C.|Barrow]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Coxy Makes Double Swoop|url=http://barrowafc.com/coxy-makes-double-swoop/|publisher=Barrow A.F.C.|date=22 July 2016|accessdate=4 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822140725/http://barrowafc.com/coxy-makes-double-swoop/|archive-date=22 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He subsequently signed for [[Southport F.C.|Southport]], before once again returning to Scotland, this time to sign with [[Scottish League One]] team [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in June 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.raithrovers.net/30132/triple-signing-coup-for-smith.htm |title=Triple Signing Coup for Smith |publisher=Raith Rovers FC |date=9 June 2017 |accessdate=9 June 2017}}</ref>

After two seasons with the Rovers, Murray signed with [[Fife derby|Fife rivals]] [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in June 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Euan_Murray_joins_DAFC&ID=11271 |title=Euan Murray joins DAFC |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=13 June 2019 |accessdate=15 June 2019}}</ref> Murray spent two season with Dunfermline before leaving the club at the end of his contract in May 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Player_Update_&ID=13149 |title=Player update |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=31 May 2021 |accessdate=31 May 2021}}</ref> He subsequently joined recently relegated [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/euan-murray-joins-killie/ |title=Euan Murray joins Killie |publisher=Kilmarnock FC |date=1 June 2021 |accessdate=1 June 2021}}</ref> He made 38 appearances in all competitions as the club won the [[Scottish Championship]] title.

On 24 June 2022, his contract with Kilmarnock had been cancelled by mutual consent. Later on the same day, it was announced that Murray had signed for [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/2022/june/pools-sign-euan-murray/ |title=Pools sign Euan Murray |publisher=Hartlepool United FC |date=24 June 2022 |accessdate=24 June 2022 |archive-date=3 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221103124540/https://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/2022/june/pools-sign-euan-murray/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 17 July 2023, Murray's contract was terminated by mutual consent.<ref name="HpoolJul">{{cite news|url=https://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/2023/july/euan-murray-departs/ |title=Euan Murray departs |publisher=Hartlepool United FC |date=17 July 2023 |access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref> Murray made 36 appearances for Hartlepool.<ref name="HpoolJul"/>

On 18 July 2023, Murray signed a two-year deal to return to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/4567801/euan-murray-returns-to-raith-rovers-on-a-two-year-deal/ |title=Euan Murray returns to Raith Rovers on a two-year deal |publisher=Raith Rovers FC |date=18 July 2023 |accessdate=18 July 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Murray played one match for [[Scotland national under-18 football team|Scotland Under-18s]] against [[Serbia national under-18 football team|Serbia]] in April 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international-matches/?mid=119030|title=Serba 1 v 4 Scotland|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |date=19 April 2012|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref>

[[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. Connolly began his career with [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] before joining [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in 2013, and also played for [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] on [[Loan (sports)|loan]]. He has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] level. ==Early life== Connolly was born in [[Dundee]] on 15 August 1995, when his father [[Paddy Connolly]] was playing for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22762888 |title=Dundee Utd sign Queen's Park's Robertson and Connolly |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 June 2013 |accessdate=2 July 2016}} He attended [[Williamwood High School]] in [[Clarkston, East Renfrewshire]].{{cite news |title=Queen's Park youngster Aidan Connolly's big test is to be like his dad |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/queens-park-youngster-aidan-connollys-1544645 |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=19 January 2013 |accessdate=12 February 2018}} ==Club career== Connolly started his career at [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], progressing through the club's youth system. '''Ross Millen''' (born 28 September 1994) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who most recently played as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right-back]] for Scottish Championship club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

Millen has previously played for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], and [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]].

He is the son of former [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], Kilmarnock, [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] and [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] defender [[Andy Millen]].

==Career==
Millen made his Dunfermline debut against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton]] on 2 February 2013,<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross Millen on his debut|url=http://www.dafc.co.uk/articles/20130209/ross-millen-on-his-debut_2207955_3070263|publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC|accessdate=20 May 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520220753/http://www.dafc.co.uk/articles/20130209/ross-millen-on-his-debut_2207955_3070263|archivedate=20 May 2014}}</ref> having played for the Dunfermline U20s team alongside team-mate [[Shaun Byrne (footballer born 1993)|Shaun Byrne]]. After the Pars went into administration, Millen featured regularly in the first-team, and scored his first goal for the club, a penalty, against [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar]] in the [[2012–13 Scottish First Division#First Division Play-offs|First Division play-offs]] on 11 May 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross ready for role|url=http://www.dafc.co.uk/articles/20140215/ross-ready-for-role_2207955_3668756|publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC|accessdate=20 May 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520220814/http://www.dafc.co.uk/articles/20140215/ross-ready-for-role_2207955_3668756|archivedate=20 May 2014}}</ref> Millen scored the winner in a 1–0 victory over rivals [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith]] in a Scottish League Cup match on Tuesday 5 August 2014. His other three goals all came from the penalty spot against [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin]], [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar]] & [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock]].

After leaving Dunfermline at the end of the [[2014–15 in Scottish football|2014–15 season]], Millen signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in July 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Defensive duo jump aboard |date=2 July 2015 |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/defensive-duo-jump-aboard/ |publisher=livingstonfc.co.uk |accessdate=2 July 2015}}</ref> Millen stayed with the side for only six months, leaving in January 2016 in order to seek regular first-team football.<ref>{{cite web|title=McCallum returns as Millen departs |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/mccallum-returns-as-millen-departs/ |publisher=livingstonfc.co.uk |date=12 January 2016 |accessdate=12 January 2016}}</ref> Shortly after leaving Livingston, Millen signed a six-month contract with [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] who he previously played for as a youth player.<ref>{{cite web|title=Millen In, Mitchell Out |url=http://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2016/01/27/5072/#.Vqkb2iqLSUl |publisher=clydefc.co.uk |date=27 January 2016 |accessdate=27 January 2016}}</ref> At the end of his contract, Millen was released by the [[Cumbernauld]] side.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2016/06/29/5214/#.V3TZ-LgrKUl |title=Players Moving On |publisher=Clyde FC |date=29 June 2016 |accessdate=29 June 2016}}</ref> At the beginning of July 2016, Millen was signed by [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], with whom his father [[Andy Millen]] finished his playing career with.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.queensparkfc.co.uk/?p=15120 |title=Signing news |publisher=Queen's Park FC |date=2 July 2016 |accessdate=2 July 2016 }}{{dead link|date=February 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Millen signed a six-month deal with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in July 2018. He stayed at the club for just under 3 years before letting his contract expire in June 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/Article?id=7435&ShowCat= |title=Ross Millen joins Killie on six-month contract |publisher=Kilmarnock FC |date=13 July 2018 |accessdate=13 July 2018}}</ref>

On 6 July 2021, Millen joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]], signing a two-year deal following his release from Kilmarnock.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scunthorpe-united.co.uk/news/2021/july/ross-millen-joins-the-iron/|title=Ross Millen joins the Iron|website=www.scunthorpe-united.co.uk|date=6 July 2021}}</ref>

Millen signed for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a two-year deal on 14 June 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Club |first1=Raith Rovers Football |last2=media |date=2022-06-14 |title=Ross Millen Signs |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/ross-millen-signs/ |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=Raith Rovers Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 7 March 2024 it was confirmed that Millen was training on his own and would no longer be selected to play for the club due to an 'internal matter'. Manager [[Ian Murray (footballer)|Ian Murray]] confirmed that he would remain contracted to the club until his contract expires<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldthorp |first=Craig |date=7 March 2024 |title=Raith Rovers boss Ian Murray praises his squad's adaptability since defender Ross Millen has been frozen out and made to train in isolation due to 'internal matter' |url=https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/international/raith-rovers-boss-ian-murray-praises-his-squads-adaptability-since-defender-ross-millen-has-been-frozen-out-and-made-to-train-in-isolation-due-to-internal-matter-4547049 |access-date=15 March 2024 |website=Fife Today}}</ref> and was not to be loaned to another team.

MIllen was one of 15 free agents that signed for [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] on 12 July 2024, after the club's embargo on registering new players was lifted.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-12 |title=Morecambe: League Two side make 15 signings after embargo lifted |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c3gr4nyjj84o |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 19 June 2025, Millen left Morecambe and signed for Scottish League One side, Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

On 25 May 2026 it was announced that Millen was one of 9 players who would be leaving Inverness upon the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-25 |title=Caley Jags confirm release of nine players at the end of their contracts |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-jags-confirm-release-of-nine-players-at-the-end-of-the-435941/ |access-date=2026-05-31 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

'''Charlie Telfer''' (born 4 July 1995) is a Scottish [[midfielder]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Airdrieonians}} side [[ Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]]

==Early life==
Telfer was born in [[Carluke]] and grew up supporting [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref name="Charlie Telfer 1">{{cite news|title=Ally McCoist: Dundee United have captured a gem in Charlie Telfer|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-united/ally-mccoist-dundee-united-have-captured-a-gem-in-charlie-telfer-1.414543|publisher=Dundee Evening Telegraph|date=11 June 2014|accessdate=11 August 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104014925/http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-united/ally-mccoist-dundee-united-have-captured-a-gem-in-charlie-telfer-1.414543|archivedate=4 November 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref> He joined the club as a youth player after being spotted at a Football in the Community course at [[Bell College]], Hamilton, when he was eight.<ref name="Record" />

==Club career==
===Rangers===
After progressing through the [[Rangers F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Rangers academy]], Telfer signed his first professional contract with the club in November 2011.<ref name="Record">{{cite news|title=Rangers starlet Charlie Telfer set to become first player to graduate from community scheme to the first team|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/rangers-starlet-charlie-telfer-on-verge-1546334|publisher=Daily Record|date=20 January 2013|accessdate=11 August 2014}}</ref> He would make one competitive first team appearance for the club against [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] in April 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26999413|title=Stenhousemuir 0-4 Rangers|publisher=BBC Sport|work=BBC|date=19 April 2014}}</ref> On 13 May 2014, he was in the Rangers side that won the [[2013–14 Scottish Youth Cup|Scottish Youth Cup]] beating [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] 8–7 on penalties following a 2–2 draw, at [[St Mirren Park]].<ref>{{cite web|title=U20: Rangers 2–2 Hearts (Rangers win 8–7 on pens)|url=http://www.rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/item/6958-u20-rangers-2-2-hearts-rangers-win-8-7-on-pens|publisher=Rangers F.C.|last=Dickson|first=Andrew|date=13 May 2014|accessdate=10 August 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104023744/http://www.rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/item/6958-u20-rangers-2-2-hearts-rangers-win-8-7-on-pens|archivedate=4 November 2014|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Telfer later describe playing in the Scottish Youth Cup Final as his biggest game of his life.<ref>{{cite news|title=Moving from Rangers to Dundee United was the best thing I could have done says Terrors kid Charlie Telfer|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/moving-rangers-dundee-united-best-5329767|publisher=Daily Record|date=14 March 2015|accessdate=27 June 2015}}</ref>

At the end of the 2013–14 season, Telfer's future at Rangers appeared to be in doubt when [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] were reported to be keen to sign him.<ref>{{cite news|title=Is Charlie Telfer on verge of signing with Dundee United?|url=http://therangersreport.com/2014/05/05/is-charlie-telfer-on-verge-of-signing-with-dundee-united/|publisher=The Rangers Report|date=5 May 2014|accessdate=11 August 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720002203/http://therangersreport.com/2014/05/05/is-charlie-telfer-on-verge-of-signing-with-dundee-united/|archivedate=20 July 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Dundee United then made a £50,000 bid to sign Telfer, which was rejected by Rangers, who offered him a new contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United confident of getting Rangers starlet|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-united/dundee-united-confident-of-getting-rangers-starlet-1.384734|publisher=Dundee Evening Telegraph|date=23 May 2014|accessdate=11 August 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141102230014/http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-united/dundee-united-confident-of-getting-rangers-starlet-1.384734|archivedate=2 November 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Rangers youngster Charlie Telfer in the dark over future as Gers and Dundee United battle for his signature|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/rangers-youngster-charlie-telfer-dark-3629622|publisher=Daily Record|date=31 May 2014|accessdate=11 August 2014}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
After rejecting the offer of a new contract with Rangers, Telfer signed for Dundee United in June 2014, with a compensation payment still to be agreed between the clubs.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United sign Rangers midfielder Charlie Telfer|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27672711|access-date=10 August 2014|work=BBC Sport website|publisher=BBC|date=2 June 2014}}</ref> Telfer's departure from Rangers was commented on by the club's manager [[Ally McCoist]], who described him as a "great prospect" and said that the club had wanted to keep him but it had been Telfer's decision to leave.<ref name="Charlie Telfer 1"/> The level of compensation to be paid was set by an independent tribunal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-united/decision-reached-in-telfer-tribunal-1.728186|title=Decision reached in Telfer tribunal|publisher=Evening Telegraph|date=9 December 2014|accessdate=27 June 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150324042309/http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-united/decision-reached-in-telfer-tribunal-1.728186|archivedate=24 March 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> with Dundee United paying £200,000 to Rangers in January 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rangers: Dundee United pay Charlie Telfer cash to Ibrox club|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30700561|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 January 2015|access-date=27 June 2015}}</ref>

He made his Dundee United debut as a substitute against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the opening match of the [[2014–15 in Scottish football|2014–15 season]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Aberdeen 0 – 3 Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28647039|access-date=10 August 2014|work=BBC Sport Website|publisher=BBC|date=10 August 2014}}</ref> and scored his first goal for the club in a 3–0 win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 1 November 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee Utd 3-0 St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29767943|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Campbell|first=Andy|date=1 November 2014|access-date=2 November 2014}}</ref> Telfer was named as [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2014–15 season|SPFL Young Player of the Month]] for November 2014.<ref name="award">{{cite web|title=SPFL: Dundee United's Charlie Telfer takes young player award|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30330356|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 December 2014|access-date=4 December 2014}}</ref> On 1 January 2015 he scored United's sixth goal in a 6–2 [[Dundee derby]] victory over local rivals [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30600732|title=Dundee United thrashed Dundee in the New Year's Day city derby.|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Campbell|first=Andy|date=1 January 2015|access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref> This was followed by two goals against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] later that month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30860821|title=Dundee United consigned Motherwell to their fifth Scottish Premiership defeat in the month of January.|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Spence|first=Jim|date=24 January 2015|access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref> Telfer was a substitute for the [[2015 Scottish League Cup Final]], but was unused as Dundee United lost 2–0 to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Wilson|first=Richard|title=Dundee Utd 0 - 2 Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31785677|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=16 March 2015|date=27 June 2015}}</ref> He made 25 appearances and scored 4 times in his first season at the club.

Having been unable to gain a regular place in the Dundee United team, Telfer moved on loan to [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in January 2016 until the end of the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Roache |first=Ian |title=Dundee United's Charlie Telfer off to Livingston on loan |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united/dundee-united-s-charlie-telfer-off-to-livingston-on-loan-1.921826 |publisher=The Courier |accessdate=28 January 2016 |date=28 January 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160131221151/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united/dundee-united-s-charlie-telfer-off-to-livingston-on-loan-1.921826 |archivedate=31 January 2016 |df=dmy }}</ref>

Telfer was released by United on 5 June 2017.

===Almere City===
Telfer signed for Dutch club [[Almere City FC|Almere City]] in August 2017 on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/ex-dundee-united-midfielder-turn-bolton-netherlands/|title = Ex-Dundee United midfielder to turn down Bolton for Netherlands| date=7 August 2017 }}</ref>

He had been training with [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] and [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]]; rejecting a contract at the [[Macron Stadium]] to move to the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/ex-dundee-united-midfielder-turn-bolton-netherlands/|title=Ex-Dundee United midfielder to turn down Bolton for Netherlands|publisher=Evening Telegraph|date=7 August 2017|accessdate=4 July 2018|first=Tom|last=Duthie}}</ref>

===Greenock Morton===
Telfer signed a one-year contract with Scottish Championship club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in June 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gmfc.net/2018/06/12/breaking-charlie-telfer-signs-for-morton/|title=Charlie Telfer signs for Morton|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.|accessdate=13 June 2018|date=12 June 2018|first=Jonathan|last=Mitchell|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612162125/https://gmfc.net/2018/06/12/breaking-charlie-telfer-signs-for-morton/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went on to make 29 league appearances, 24 of them in the starting line-up. Morton manager [[Jonatan Johansson (footballer)|Jonatan Johansson]] and his assistant [[Peter Houston]] walked out on the club before the final game of the season in May 2019, claiming that chairman Crawford Rae had told them not to select Telfer, as one further appearance would trigger an automatic contract extension. Rae subsequently suggested that Telfer could still be offered a new contract once a replacement manager was appointed.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=Aadm |title=Contract wrangle a bitter blow to Morton midfielder Telfer |url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/17621769.contract-wrangle-bitter-blow-morton-midfielder-telfer/ |access-date=6 June 2021 |work=Greenock Telegraph |date=6 May 2019}}</ref>

===Falkirk===
On 18 June 2019, Telfer signed for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Long term thinking helps Falkirk land Charlie Telfer|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/long-term-thinking-helps-falkirk-land-charlie-telfer-1-4949470|publisher=The Falkirk Herald|last=Oliver|first=David|date=18 June 2019|accessdate=18 June 2019}}</ref> At the end an injury-hit 2020–21 season, Telfer signed a further one-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Simpson |first1=Martyn |title=Ben Hall and Charlie Telfer signs new Falkirk deals |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/ben-hall-and-charlie-telfer-signs-new-falkirk-deals-3262539 |access-date=6 June 2021 |work=Falkirk Herald |date=5 June 2021}}</ref> After three years at Falkirk, he left at the end of his contract in May 2022.

===Airdrieonians===
Following a trial spell with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], Telfer signed a contract with the club in September 2022.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/former-rangers-midfielder-joins-airdrieonians-27957906 |title=Former Rangers midfielder joins Airdrieonians |newspaper=Daily Record |first=Paul |last=Thomson |date=10 September 2022 |accessdate=10 September 2022}}</ref>
Telfer played a key role in helping Airdrieonians gain promotion back to the Scottish Championship via the play-offs at the end of season 2022-23.

===Ross County===
Telfer signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in July 2024 on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 July 2024|title=Ross County complete signing of former Rangers, Dundee United and Airdrieonians midfielder Charlie Telfter|url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/ross-county-bring-in-rangers-academy-product-354923/|website=ross-shirejournal.co.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref>

====Hamilton Academical (loan)====
He signed for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on loan in February 2025 for the remainder of the 2024-25 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 February 2025|title=Charlie Telfer joins Hamilton Academical on loan|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/charlie-telfer-joins-hamilton-academical-on-loan|website=rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==
Telfer has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/item/3637-kids-aim-for-scotland-spot |title=Kids Aim For Scotland Spot |publisher=[[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] |accessdate=14 August 2014 |date=28 March 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814141505/http://www.rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/item/3637-kids-aim-for-scotland-spot |archivedate=14 August 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Barrie turns to dark side for Scotland|url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/rangers/barrie-turns-to-dark-side-for-scotland-118806n.20538710|publisher=Glasgow Evening Times|date=19 March 2013|accessdate=14 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Charlie Telfer profile|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=69371&squadID=9|publisher=Scottish FA|accessdate=10 August 2014}}</ref>

'''George Oakley''' (born 18 November 1995) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

==Playing career==

===AFC Wimbledon===
Oakley joined [[AFC Wimbledon]] at the age of eleven, and progressed through the youth ranks.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/under-18s-oakley-694092.aspx|author=Chris Slavin|title=Young striker was "immense"|publisher=AFC Wimbledon|date=4 March 2013|access-date=4 November 2014}}</ref> On 15 February 2014, he was named as a substitute in a 1–0 league defeat at [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Portsmouth 1–0 Wimbledon|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26094949|access-date=4 November 2014|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=15 February 2014}}</ref> He signed a professional contract in May 2014, and scored just days later in the 2014 [[London Senior Cup]] final win over [[Metropolitan Police F.C.|Metropolitan Police]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Young Dons clinch glory|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/young-dons-clinch-glory-1539714.aspx|access-date=8 September 2014|author=Chris Slavin|publisher=AFC Wimbledon|date=6 May 2014}}</ref>

Oakley was ruled out of the opening two months of the [[2014–15 AFC Wimbledon season|2014–15 season]] with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/oakley-player-interview-2002946.aspx|author=Chris Slavin|title=Oakley relishes cup tie|publisher=AFC Wimbledon|date=7 October 2014|access-date=4 November 2014}}</ref> On 7 October 2014, he marked his return in a 4–0 defeat to [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] in the [[Premier League Cup (football)|U21 Premier League Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/dons-v-charlton-under-21s-2005890.aspx|author=Laurence Lowner|title=Dons suffer cup knock-out|publisher=AFC Wimbledon|date=8 October 2014|access-date=4 November 2014}}</ref> On 1 November 2014, he made his [[English Football League|Football League]] debut as a late substitute in a 2–0 loss at [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Northampton 2–0 Wimbledon|date=31 October 2014 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29767756|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=4 November 2014}}</ref>

On 30 October 2015, Oakley joined affiliate [[Isthmian League|Isthmian Premier Division]] side [[Kingstonian F.C.|Kingstonian]] on a one-month loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/oakley-goes-out-on-loan-2773301.aspx|title=Oakley goes out on loan|last=Slavin|first=Chris|website=www.afcwimbledon.co.uk|access-date=2016-12-17}}</ref> He made his debut the following day, scoring in a 5–1 [[FA Trophy]] win at [[Leatherhead F.C.|Leatherhead]].<ref name=":0" /> He managed just 12 minutes in his second appearance – a 1–0 victory over [[Enfield Town F.C.|Enfield Town]] – before suffering from injury.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.kingstonian.com/teams/72292/player/george-oakley-1611034/32404|title=George Oakley – First Team – Kingstonian FC|website=www.kingstonian.com|access-date=2016-12-17}}</ref> A grade two hamstring tear ruled him out for eight weeks and his loan spell was ended prematurely.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/update-on-george-oakley-2786717.aspx|title=Update on George Oakley|last=Slavin|first=Chris|website=www.afcwimbledon.co.uk|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref>

In January 2016, Oakley suffered a broken ankle during a training session, ruling him out for the remainder of the [[2015–16 AFC Wimbledon season|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/staff-rally-around-oakley-2926229.aspx|title=Staff rally around Oakley|last=Cornell|first=Rob|website=www.afcwimbledon.co.uk|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref> On 19 July 2016, he made his first appearance after the injury in a pre-season outing at [[Raynes Park Vale F.C.|Raynes Park Vale]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/vale-return-for-george-3193851.aspx|title=Vale return for George|access-date=2016-12-17}}</ref> On 8 November 2016, he made his first appearance of the season for the senior squad in a 2–0 [[EFL Trophy]] defeat at [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]].<ref name=":1" />

On 18 November 2016, Now plays for woking  his 21st birthday, Oakley joined [[National League South]] club [[Welling United F.C.|Welling United]] on a one-month loan.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/oakley-goes-out-on-loan-3423323.aspx|title=Oakley goes out on loan|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref> Making his debut in a 3–1 defeat at [[Hampton & Richmond Borough F.C.|Hampton & Richmond Borough]], he scored his first goal for the club a week later in a 1–0 [[FA Trophy]] win at [[Concord Rangers F.C.|Concord Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wellingunited.com/wp/event/concord-rangers-vs-welling-united-2/|title=Concord Rangers vs Welling United|website=www.wellingunited.com|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref> He added his second of the season in the next round of the cup, completing the scoring in an 8–1 win over [[Hythe Town F.C.|Hythe Town]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wellingunited.com/wp/event/welling-united-vs-hythe-town/|title=Welling United vs Hythe Town|website=www.wellingunited.com|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref> On 16 December 2016, Oakley's loan at Welling was extended by a further month.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/egli-goes-out-on-loan-3473061.aspx|title=Egli goes out on loan|access-date=19 December 2016}}</ref>

On 17 March 2017, Oakley joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[Maidstone United F.C.|Maidstone United]] on a one-month loan deal.<ref>{{Cite news |title=George Oakley: AFC Wimbledon forward makes Maidstone United loan switch |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39307778 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 March 2017 |access-date=21 March 2017}}</ref>

===Inverness Caledonian Thistle===
Oakley signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in July 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40478534 |title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle sign George Oakley and Mark Ridgers |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=3 July 2017 |access-date=3 July 2017}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 4–1 friendly win at [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://brorarangers.football/2017/07/04/ict-home-report/| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170730075825/http://brorarangers.football/2017/07/04/ict-home-report/| archive-date = 2017-07-30| title = Brora Rangers Football Club {{!}} Ict Home Report}}</ref> He then scored his first competitive goal in Inverness's first game of the season, the opening game of the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stages, a 3–0 home win against [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Inverness CT 3–0 Brechin|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40619957|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 July 2017|access-date=21 August 2017}}</ref> He started in the following match, a 0–0 draw away at [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] which resulted in a 2–0 penalty shootout a win for ICT, the lowest scoring penalty shootout in Scottish football.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pars and ICT among penalty winners|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/pars-and-ict-among-penalty-winners/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=19 July 2017|access-date=21 August 2017|archive-date=21 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170821044833/https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/pars-and-ict-among-penalty-winners/|url-status=dead}}</ref> His second competitive goal for Inverness came in a 2–1 win away to [[Forfar Athletic]], although this wasn't enough to prevent them exiting the League Cup.<ref>{{cite web|title=Forfar 1–2 Inverness CT|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40760186|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 July 2017|access-date=21 August 2017}}</ref>

On 30 December 2017, with Inverness down to ten men and losing 2–1 against bottom of the table [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]], Oakley came on as a substitute and netted twice to give Inverness the win. On his [[2017–18 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] debut, he scored a late goal in a 2–2 draw v [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], earning Inverness a replay at home.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42672291|title=Dundee 2-2 Inverness Caledonian Thistle|date=20 January 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=20 January 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Hamilton Academical===
In January 2019, Oakley moved to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New signing: George Oakley|url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/new-signing-george-oakley/|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.|date=31 January 2019}}</ref> On 27 February 2019, he scored the opening goal as Hamilton won 2–0 away to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], with the goal drawing comparisons to [[Marco van Basten]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aberdeen 0–2 Hamilton Academical|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47301046|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Elgott|first=Jordan|date=27 February 2019|access-date=20 June 2019}}</ref>

===Pirin Blagoevgrad===
In June 2020, he signed a two-year contract with Bulgarian club [[OFC Pirin Blagoevgrad|Pirin Blagoevgrad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Английски нападател е десетият нов в Пирин|url=https://topsport.bg/pirin/angliyski-napadatel-e-desetiyat-nov-v-pirin.html|publisher=topsport.bg|language=bg|date=15 June 2020|access-date=15 June 2020}}</ref> In January 2021, he was training with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] after leaving Pirin.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/rangers/rangers-announce-signing-celtic-ace-lined-ps35m-deal-ibrox-winger-exit-rafa-benitez-replace-neil-lennon-latest-scottish-premiership-rumour-mill-3111313|title=Rangers to announce signing, Celtic ace lined up in £35m deal, Ibrox winger to exit, Rafa Benitez to replace Neil Lennon latest - Scottish Premiership Rumour Mill|website=edinburghnews.scotsman.com|date=25 January 2021|access-date=25 January 2021}}</ref>

=== Kilmarnock ===
On 26 January 2021, after a trial period, Oakley returned to the Scottish Premiership with Kilmarnock after signing a deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=26 January 2021|title=Nine is fine as Oakley joins Killie|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/nine-is-fine-as-oakley-joins-killie/|access-date=26 January 2021|website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk}}</ref> He left Kilmarnock at the end of the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/squad-update-following-2020-21-season/|title=Squad update following 2020/21 season|date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

===Woking===
On 22 June 2021, it was announced that Oakley would join National League side, [[Woking F.C.|Woking]] following his release from Kilmarnock.<ref>{{Cite news |title=George Oakley Signs |url=https://www.wokingfc.co.uk/news/article/7537/george-oakley-signs/ |publisher=[[Woking F.C.]] |first=Daniel |last=O'Sullivan |date=22 June 2021 |accessdate=24 June 2021}}</ref> He went on to feature seventeen times, scoring once before leaving The Cards in July 2022 at the end of his contract.<ref>{{Cite news |title=2021/22 Retained and Released List |url=https://www.wokingfc.co.uk/news/article/7862/2021-22-retained-and-released-list/ |publisher=[[Woking F.C.]] |first=Daniel |last=O'Sullivan |date=18 May 2022 |accessdate=18 May 2022}}</ref>

=== Return to Inverness Caledonian Thistle ===
On 2 July 2022, Oakley returned to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], 3 years after leaving initially.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-06 |title=George Oakley signs for ICTFC |url=https://ictfc.com/george-oakley-signs-for-ictfc |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref> A week later, Oakley scored on his second debut in a 1–0 away win over [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] in the League Cup. On 20 January 2023, Oakley left ''Caley'' by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=ICTFC |date=2023-01-20 |title=George Oakley leaves ICTFC |url=https://ictfc.com/george-oakley-leaves-ictfc |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Greenock Morton ===
On 24 January 2023, Oakley signed an 18-month contract with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]]. He scored his first Morton goal 4 minutes into his debut.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-24 |title=George Oakley becomes our third January signing |url=https://www.gmfc.net/george-oakley-becomes-our-third-january-signing/ |access-date=2023-01-24 |website=Greenock Morton FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> Oakley would finish the season with 6 goals in 13 appearances, an average of roughly 1 goal every 2 games.

=== Ayr United ===
In 2024, Oakley joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on a two-year deal after previously signing a pre-contract agreement while at Morton.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-24 |title=Ayr United make first summer signing as top Championship marksman joins |url=https://www.ayradvertiser.com/sport/24344715.ayr-united-george-oakley-signs-pre-contract-agreement/ |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=Ayr Advertiser |language=en}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
On 4 May 2026, Oakley agreed to join fellow Scottish Championship club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a two-year deal from the expiry of his contract with Ayr United.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/welcome-george-oakley/|title=Welcome, George Oakley!|website=www.raithrovers.net|date=4 May 2026|accessdate=11 May 2026}}</ref>
