'''Jack Baird''' (born 7 February 1996) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. He has previously played for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] (two spells) and [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].

==Career==
Baird made his first team debut for St Mirren on 22 November 2014, in a 3–0 defeat to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Hamilton Accies 3–0 St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30065657|access-date=14 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=22 November 2014}}</ref> On 14 May 2015, Baird signed a two–year extension to his contract, tying him to the club until the summer of 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=New Deals for Jack, Lewis and Barry|url=http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=43404|access-date=14 May 2015|work=Official St Mirren website|date=14 May 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150522212028/http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=43404|archive-date=22 May 2015}}</ref>

After establishing himself as a first team regular over the past few years, Baird signed a new one-year deal in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/880-jack-baird-signs-contract-extension|title=Jack Baird signs contract extension|publisher=St Mirren Official website|accessdate=22 May 2017|archive-date=3 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180203005706/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/880-jack-baird-signs-contract-extension|url-status=dead}}</ref> Baird signed a further one-year extension to his contract in January 2018, tying him to the club until the summer of 2019 after showing impressive form.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1554-delight-for-saints-as-jack-baird-signs-contract-extension |title=Delight for Saints as Jack Baird signs contract extension |work=stmirren.com |date=1 February 2018 |accessdate=1 February 2018 |archive-date=2 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202071728/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1554-delight-for-saints-as-jack-baird-signs-contract-extension |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In January 2019, Baird signed a further two-year contract extension meaning that he will be at the club until the summer of 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/2553-jack-baird-signs-contract-extension-2 |title=Jack Baird signs contract extension |work=stmirren.com |date=1 February 2019 |accessdate=1 February 2019 |archive-date=2 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202042309/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/2553-jack-baird-signs-contract-extension-2 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He moved on loan to [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in September 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gmfc.net/2019/09/02/jack-baird-joins-morton-on-loan/|title=Jack Baird Joins Morton On Loan – Greenock Morton|access-date=3 September 2019|archive-date=3 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903082741/https://gmfc.net/2019/09/02/jack-baird-joins-morton-on-loan/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The loan agreement was originally due to expire in January 2020, but it was later extended to the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51021616 |title=St Mirren: Centre-back Conor McCarthy signs from Cork City |website=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2020 |accessdate=7 January 2020}}</ref>

On 3 September 2020 Baird left St Mirren club by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jack Baird leaves by mutual consent|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3755-jack-baird-leaves-by-mutual-consent|access-date=3 September 2020|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref> The next day he signed for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/jack-baird-signs-for-the-honest-men/|title=Jack Baird signs for the Honest Men – Ayr United Football Club|access-date=4 September 2020|archive-date=13 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200913055842/https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/jack-baird-signs-for-the-honest-men/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In May 2022, Baird signed a pre-contract agreement with fellow [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2022 |title=Jack Baird signs pre-contract agreement with the club. |url=https://www.gmfc.net/jack-baird-signs-pre-contract-agreement-with-the-club/ |access-date=7 July 2022 |website=Greenock Morton FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 26 May 2025 Baird signed a two-year contract with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 May 2025 |title=Jack Baird signs for Saints! |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/jack-baird-signs-for-saints |access-date=26 May 2025 |website=St Johnstone FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''David Mitchell''' (born 4 April 1990) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|PartickT}} club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. Mitchell has previously played for [[Ayr United F.C.| Ayr United]], [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]

==Career==

===Stranraer===
After beginning his career at [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] without featuring in the first team, Mitchell joined [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] on loan in July 2009,<ref>{{cite web|title=Stranraer bring in two new faces|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/stranraer/8153648.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 July 2009|access-date=29 April 2016}}</ref> then made the move permanent in June 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stranraer sign Ayr Utd goalkeeper David Mitchell|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/stranraer/8724164.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 June 2010|access-date=29 April 2016}}</ref> He stated that his decision to make the initial loan move was to achieve his ambition of first team football which he felt he wouldn't get at Ayr.<ref name="spfl interview">{{cite web|title=Mitchell is old head on young shoulders|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/mitchell-is-old-head-on-young-shoulders/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=5 April 2013|accessdate=29 April 2016|archive-date=9 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170109010732/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/mitchell-is-old-head-on-young-shoulders/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Mitchell was part of the club's successful promotion campaign in 2012, when having initially lost against [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] in the play-offs, Stranraer were promoted to the [[Scottish Football League Second Division|Scottish Second Division]] due to the demise of [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref name="spfl interview"/> During the 2014–15 season, [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] were reported to be interested in signing Mitchell.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stranraer duo are in Hibs' sights|url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/stranraer-duo-are-in-hibs-sights-1-3629172|work=The Scotsman|date=9 December 2014|access-date=10 June 2015|archive-date=11 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611024913/http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/stranraer-duo-are-in-hibs-sights-1-3629172|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Dundee===
In June 2015, Mitchell agreed a pre-contract with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee sign Stranraer keeper David Mitchell|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/dundee-sign-stranraer-keeper-david-mitchell-1.880335|publisher=DC Thomson|date=1 June 2015}}</ref> He made his debut on 20 March 2016 in the [[Dundee derby]] against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], coming on as a substitute following a red card for [[Scott Bain]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United 2–2 Dundee|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35796734|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Young|first=Chick|date= 20 March 2016|accessdate=29 April 2016}}</ref> He left Dundee at the end of the 2016–17 season.

===Falkirk===
On 1 June 2017, Mitchell agreed a contract with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/bairns-confirm-david-mitchell-signing/ |title=Bairns Confirm David Mitchell Signing |publisher=Falkirk FC |date=1 June 2017 |accessdate=1 June 2017 |archive-date=29 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029020041/http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/bairns-confirm-david-mitchell-signing/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Clyde===
On 24 May 2019, Mitchell signed for [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] on a one-year contract,<ref>{{cite web|title=NEW SIGNING:David Mitchell|url=http://clydefc.co.uk/news/2019/05/24/6127/#.XSURfjfTUwA|publisher=Clyde F.C.|date=24 May 2019|accessdate=9 July 2019}}</ref> and on 16 January 2020 signed a two-and-a-half-year contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 January 2020 |title=Mitchell Extends Clyde Contract |url=https://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2020/01/mitchell-extends-clyde-contract/ |access-date=13 December 2024 |website=Clyde FC}}</ref> 

===Hibernian===
He moved to Premiership club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in August 2021,<ref>{{cite web |title=Hibernian: Late Jamie McGrath bid fails but Nathan Wood joins from Middlesbrough |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58400014 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2021 |access-date=1 September 2021}}</ref> and left them in June 2022 without having played a first-team game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/david-mitchell-departs |title=David Mitchell Departs |website=www.hibernianfc.co.uk |date=23 June 2022 |accessdate=23 June 2022}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
After leaving Hibs Mitchell joined Scottish Championship club Partick Thistle in June 2022, on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-david-mitchell-signs-two-year-deal/ | title=Signing News: David Mitchell signs two-year deal }}</ref>

After making 50 appearances in all competitions over two seasons with the club, Mitchell signed a one-year contract extension with Thistle in May 2024, extending his deal until June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 May 2024 |title=David Mitchell Signs New One-Year Deal |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/david-mitchell-signs-new-one-year-deal/ |access-date=13 December 2024 |website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
On June 3rd 2025 Mitchell rejoins the team he started his career with, signing a 2 year contract with Scottish Championship club, Scott Brown's Ayr United.

===Queen's Park===
In summer 2026 Mitchell moved to Queen's Park after the departure of Spiders no.1 goalkeeper Calum Ferrie to [[Kilmarnock F.C.| Kilmarnock]].

'''Scott Anthony Martin''' (born 1 April 1997) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]], who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. Martin has previously played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] and [[Partick Thistle F.C. |Partick Thistle]], and on loan for [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] and [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].

==Club career==
===Hibernian===
Raised in [[Cambuslang]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/6257 |title=Under 20s gain Modern Apprenticeship |publisher=Hibernian F.C. |date=4 March 2016  |accessdate=14 February 2018}}</ref> and a pupil at [[Trinity High School (Rutherglen)|Trinity High School]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.youthfootballscotland.co.uk/live/item/7151-cardinal-see-off-trinity-to-clinch-silverware.html |title=Cardinal see off Trinity to clinch silverware |publisher=Youth Football Scotland |date=15 May 2013 |accessdate=14 February 2018 }}</ref> Martin trained with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] as a young boy but was released. His mother corresponded with several professional clubs on his behalf, and he joined the youth setup at [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in 2007, following a successful trial.<ref name=pride>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/mother-s-pride-key-to-scott-martin-s-hibs-rise-1-3832878|title=Mother's pride key to Scott Martin's Hibs rise |publisher=Edinburgh Evening News |date=17 July 2015 |accessdate=14 February 2018 }}</ref>

Having signed a professional contract with the [[Edinburgh]] side in February 2014, Martin made his first team debut for Hibs in December of the same year,<ref name = "profile">{{cite web|url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/team/80 |title=Scott Martin|publisher=Hibernian FC |accessdate=17 September 2017}}</ref> and made three appearances from the bench in the [[2014–15 Hibernian F.C. season|2014–15 season]]. He scored his first goal for the club on 1 August 2015, in a [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] game against [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]].<ref name = "profile"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/hibernian/1325754-hibernian-3-0-montrose-alan-stubbs-bounce-back-with-league-cup-win/ |title=Hibernian 3-0 Montrose: Alan Stubbs bounce back with League Cup win |work=STV Sport |publisher=STV |date=1 August 2015 |accessdate=2 August 2015}}</ref>

Martin moved on loan to [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] in October 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/spfl-lower-divisions/hibs-youngster-scott-martin-joins-forfar-on-loan-1-3926101#axzz3pPrSHmmz |title=Hibs youngster Scott Martin joins Forfar on loan |first=Craig |last=Fowler |work=The Scotsman |date=23 October 2015 |accessdate=23 October 2015}}</ref> On returning to his parent club for the [[2016–17 Hibernian F.C. season|2016–17 season]] and made four league appearances as Hibernian [[2016–17 Scottish Championship|won promotion as champions]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/hibs/player.php?playerid=6751 |title=Hibernian player Scott Martin profile |publisher=Fitbastats  |accessdate=14 February 2018 }}</ref>

Early in his career, he was compared to the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] captain [[Scott Brown (footballer, born June 1985)|Scott Brown]], due to similarities in their style of play and the fact that both players came through the Hibernian youth system.<ref name=pride/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/next-scott-brown-glasgows-rising-11415466|title=The next Scott Brown and Glasgow's other rising youth stars  |publisher=Glasgow Live |date=1 June 2016 |accessdate=14 February 2018 }}</ref>

In November 2017, Martin was loaned to a third-tier club again, this time to [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/8073 |title=Martin joins Arbroath on loan |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=2 November 2017 |accessdate=2 November 2017}}</ref> The Arbroath fans voted Martin as their young player of the year for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-youngster-scott-martin-voted-arbroath-s-young-player-of-the-year-1-4729288 |title=Hibs youngster Scott Martin voted Arbroath's Young Player of the Year |first=David |last=Gunn |work=Edinburgh Evening News |date=24 April 2018 |accessdate=24 April 2018}}</ref>

===Hamilton Academical===
On 31 August 2018, Martin signed for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/new-signing-scott-martin/|title=New Signing: Scott Martin |publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C. |date=31 August 2018 |accessdate=31 August 2018 }}</ref> On 3 August 2020, he signed a new three-year deal at Hamilton, keeping him at the club until 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Deals For Martin & Want|url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/new-deals-for-martin-want/|website=hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
After spending six and a half years with Hamilton Academical, on 3 February 2025 Martin joined fellow Scottish Championship club [[Partick Thistle]] on an 18 month deal, with the option of a further year, with Thistle midfielder [[Scott Robinson (footballer)|Scott Robinson]] heading the other way as part of a swap deal for the two players.<ref>[https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/scott-martin-joins-the-club-as-scott-robinson-moves-to-hamilton-accies/ Scott Martin joins the club as Scott Robinson moves to Hamilton Accies], Partick Thistle FC, 3 February 2025</ref>

Just five games into his Thistle career, Martin suffered a knee injury in a 2–0 away win against Queens Park, which ruled him out for 12 months.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/injury-update-scott-martin-27th-march-2025/ | title=Injury Update: Scott Martin – 27th March 2025 }}</ref>

In February 2026, Martin joined fellow [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/scott-martin-heads-to-queens-park-on-loan/</ref>

===Queen's Park===
Following his loan spell, Martin joined Queen's Park permanently following the expiry of Partick Thistle contract.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/scott-martin-departs-to-join-queens-park/</ref>

==International career==
Martin has played for Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] international levels.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/hibernian/303920-fifteen-for-15-all-action-midfielder-scott-martin-is-climbing-hibs-ranks/ |title=Fifteen for '15: All-action midfielder Scott Martin is climbing Hibs' ranks |work=STV Sport |publisher=STV |date=18 December 2014 |accessdate=2 August 2015}}</ref>

'''Ricki Lamie''' (born 20 June 1993) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] professional [[association football|footballer]], who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].

He has previously played for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]], [[East Stirlingshire F.C.|East Stirlingshire]], [[Bathgate Thistle]], [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] and [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].

==Career==
Lamie started his senior career when he moved to [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] (then called Airdrie United) in 2011 from his youth team Whitburn Boys Club. In his first season with Airdrie's youth team, he won the club's U19 Player of the Year award.<ref name="afc">{{cite news|url=http://www.airdriefc.com/squadprofiles/rickilamie.html|title=Ricki Lamie|publisher=Airdrieonians F.C.|accessdate=2 August 2015|website=airdriefc.com}}</ref>

Whilst at Airdrie he had three loan spells at [[Bathgate Thistle]],<ref name="afc"/> [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2012/11/23/4241/#.Vb35kPlViko|title=Loan Deal for Lamie|publisher=Clyde F.C.|date=23 November 2012|accessdate=2 August 2015|website=clydefc.co.uk}}</ref> and [[East Stirlingshire F.C.|East Stirlingshire]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eaststirlingshirefc.com/2014/03/28/ricki-joins-shire-on-loan/|title=Ricki joins Shire on loan|publisher=East Stirlingshire F.C.|date=28 March 2014|accessdate=2 August 2015|website=eaststirlingshirefc.com}}{{dead link|date=February 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

In the summer of 2014, Lamie signed up with Morton on a short-term contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/morton/articles/2014/07/18/504568-morton-snap-up-three-trialists/|title=Morton snap up three trialists|work=[[Greenock Telegraph]]|first=Jonathan|last=Mitchell|date=18 July 2014|accessdate=2 August 2015|publisher=[[Newsquest]]}}</ref> This was extended in January, and he signed on again for the 2015–16 season in May 2015.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://gmfc.net/News/&action=fullnews&id=1415|title=Ricki Lamie Re-signs|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.|date=19 May 2015|accessdate=20 May 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150522132352/http://gmfc.net/News/%26action%3Dfullnews%26id%3D1415|archivedate=22 May 2015|df=dmy-all|website=gmfc.net}}</ref>

His contract was again extended in May 2016, this time for one year.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://gmfc.net/News/&action=fullnews&id=1615|title=Player news - three confirmed|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.|date=3 May 2016|accessdate=4 May 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324174226/http://gmfc.net/News/|archivedate=24 March 2016|df=dmy-all|website=gmfc.net}}</ref> After a successful campaign in 2016–17, Lamie signed up for another season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://gmfc.net/2017/05/26/ricki-lamie-signs-new-one-year-deal/|title=Ricki Lamie signs new one-year deal|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.|date=26 May 2017|accessdate=26 May 2017|first=Jonathan|last=Mitchell|website=gmfc.net}}</ref>

In June 2018, Lamie signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44433608 |title=Livingston sign defender Ricki Lamie from Greenock Morton |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=10 June 2018 |accessdate=10 June 2018}}</ref>

On 10 June 2020, [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of Lamie on a contract until the summer of 2022.<ref name="Ricki Lamie 2022">{{cite web |title=RICKI LAMIE SIGNS FOR MOTHERWELL |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2020/06/10/ricki-lamie-signs-for-motherwell/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |accessdate=10 June 2020 |date=10 June 2020}}</ref>

On 28 January 2022, Lamie signed a pre-contract agreement with fellow [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |title=Dundee agree pre-contract deal with Motherwell defender Ricki Lamie - and Dark Blues hope to get him in before window shuts |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/2956620/dundee-agree-pre-contract-deal-with-motherwell-defender-ricki-lamie-and-the-dark-blues-hope-to-get-him-in-before-the-window-shuts/ |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 9 April, Lamie would score a last-minute goal against former team [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] to secure a top-six spot for Motherwell.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Motherwell salvage top-six spot with dramatic draw |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60903122 |access-date=2022-05-09}}</ref> Lamie would score another key goal for Motherwell the next month, netting a winning goal against [[Hearts F.C.|Hearts]] which guaranteed the ''Steelmen'' European football the next season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Banks |first=Ben |date=2022-05-11 |title=Motherwell boss provides Lamie update with Europa Conference League spot booked |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/motherwell-boss-provides-ricki-lamie-26941555 |access-date=2022-05-16 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> The big goals for Motherwell created questions whether Lamie would join Dundee next season, and Lamie confirmed there was a relegation clause in his pre-contract agreement and stated that things were "still up in the air".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricki Lamie opens up on Dundee-Motherwell future as other clubs wait in wings |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/ricki-lamie-opens-up-on-dundee-motherwell-future-as-other-clubs-wait-in-wings-3691822 |access-date=2022-05-16 |website=www.scotsman.com |language=en}}</ref> On 24 May, Lamie officially signed a new two-year extension with Motherwell.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pilcher |first=Ross |date=2022-05-24 |title=Ricki Lamie in Motherwell transfer u-turn as defender dumps Dundee |url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/ricki-lamie-motherwell-transfer-u-24046201 |access-date=2022-05-24 |website=footballscotland |language=en}}</ref>

On 26 August 2023, Lamie joined [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-26 |title=Lamie signs for The Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/lamie-signs/ |access-date=2023-08-26 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Lamie made his debut on 2 September and scored his first goal for the club in the same game.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kucheriavyi nets late double in Dundee draw |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66625125 |access-date=2023-09-02}}</ref> On 23 February 2024, Lamie signed a pre-contract agreement with Dundee for a second time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-23 |title=Lamie signs pre-contract with The Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/lamie-signs-pre-contract/ |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> However, the agreement would fall apart once again and Dundee announced that Lamie would depart the club in June 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-28 |title=Ricki Lamie Departs |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/ricki-lamie-departs/ |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 1 July 2024, Lamie joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricki Lamie joins the Staggies |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/ricki-lamie-joins-the-staggies |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref> Lamie made his debut for the ''Staggies'' on 13 July in a win over [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stranraer vs Ross County: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cl7y8rjdxk2t |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 23 January 2025, Lamie joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricki Lamie joins Hamilton Accies on loan |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/ricki-lamie-joins-hamilton-accies-on-loan |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomson |first=Paul |date=2025-01-23 |title=Former Motherwell defender Ricki Lamie completes Hamilton Accies loan move |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/ross-county-defender-joins-hamilton-34540813 |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for the ''Accies'' two days later, starting in an away league defeat to his former club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Livingston vs Hamilton Academical: Scottish Championship stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz0l1xl9340t |access-date=2025-01-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 15 February, Lamie scored his first goal for Hamilton in an away victory at [[Hampden Park|Hampden]] over [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Queen's Park 1-2 Hamilton Academical: Cup heroes suffer sobering defeat |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cglyj34kee2t |access-date=2025-02-15 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 27 June 2025, Lamie departed Ross County.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 June 2025 |title=@RossCounty on X |url=https://x.com/RossCounty/status/1938507620286878006 |access-date=12 July 2025 |website=x.com}}</ref>

After an attempt to sign permanently with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] failed after 5 months amid the club's stint in [[Administration (British football)|administration]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burns |first=Scott |date=2025-12-02 |title=Rickie Lamie opens up on hunt for new club after five months hanging on for Hamilton |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/rickie-lamie-opens-up-hunt-36338176 |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> in January 2026 Lamie joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on a short-term deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=David |date=2026-01-06 |title=Welcome back to Queen's Park, Ricki Lamie |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/sean-crighton-queens-park-ricki-lamie-transfer-window/ |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> On 28 May 2026, Lamie signed a new deal with the ''Spiders'' to stay with the club for the next season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=David |date=2026-05-28 |title=Ricki Lamie Returns To Queen's Park |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/ricki-lamie-returns-to-queens-park/ |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Paul James McMullan''' (born 25 February 1996) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a winger for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]]. McMullan started his career with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and has also had loan spells at [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]], [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]], [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] and [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. He then signed for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] before joining their city rivals [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], winning the [[Scottish Championship]] with both clubs. After leaving Dundee, McMullan spent the next couple of years with [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] side [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]].

==Career==
===Celtic===
Born in [[Stirling]], McMullan began his career in the under-19 team at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

===Stenhousemuir (loan)===
On 23 January 2015, he joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stenhousemuir sign Craig Sutherland and Paul McMullan ahead of Ayr clash|url=http://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/local-sport/football/stenhousemuir-sign-craig-sutherland-and-paul-mcmullan-ahead-of-ayr-clash-1-3669924|access-date=19 August 2015|work=Falkirk Herald|date=23 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311162623/http://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/local-sport/football/stenhousemuir-sign-craig-sutherland-and-paul-mcmullan-ahead-of-ayr-clash-1-3669924|archive-date=11 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his senior debut the following day, playing the full 90 minutes of a 1–1 draw with [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] at [[Ochilview Park]], scoring his team's goal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stenhousemuir 1–1 Ayr|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30861104|access-date=19 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 January 2015}}</ref> On 14 February, he opened the scoring away to [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], who came from behind to defeat Stenhousemuir 3–2.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dunfermline 3-2 Stenhousemuir|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31375517|access-date=19 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 February 2015}}</ref> McMullan's only other goal of 14 league appearances came on 11 April in a defeat by the same score at [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Morton 3-2 Stenhousemuir|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32088903|access-date=19 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 April 2015}}</ref> Stenhousemuir finished in the relegation play-off places, but stayed up with a 2–1 aggregate victory over [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]: McMullan's free-kick set up [[Jamie McCormack]] to head the only goal of the first leg on 13 May,<ref>{{cite news|last1=Crawford|first1=Kenny|title=Queen's Park 0-1 Stenhousemuir|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32679094|access-date=19 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2015}}</ref> and he also assisted [[Colin McMenamin]] in the second leg three days later.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lamont|first1=Alasdair|title=Stenhousemuir 1–1 Queen's Park|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32679093|access-date=19 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 May 2015}}</ref>

===St Mirren (loan)===
On 13 July 2015, McMullan was loaned to [[Scottish Championship]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] for the [[2015–16 Scottish Championship|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=St Mirren take Paul McMullan on loan from Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33386567|access-date=19 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 July 2015}}</ref> He made his debut 12 days later, playing the full 90 minutes of a 3–1 home win over [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]] in the first round of the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Haggerty|first1=Anthony|title=St Mirren 3 Berwick Rangers 1: Winning start to Ian Murray's reign in Paisley as Buddies see off Borderers|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/st-mirren-3-berwick-rangers-6138174|access-date=19 August 2015|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|date=25 July 2015}}</ref> On 7 August, he made his league debut for the team in a defeat by the same score to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at [[Ibrox Park|Ibrox]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rangers 3-1 St Mirren |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33729044 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2015 |access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref> Twenty-two days later, he scored his only goal for the team from [[Paisley, Renfrewshire|Paisley]], taking four minutes to open a 1–1 draw against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] at [[St. Mirren Park]]; the result meant his team had not won yet in four league games of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=St Mirren 1-1 Livingston|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34025543|access-date=13 April 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 August 2015}}</ref>

In January 2016, McMullan's loan was ended by Saints, and he returned to Celtic. In total, he played 22 games for the club, scoring once.<ref>{{cite news|title=Paul McMullan|url=http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=51796|access-date=1 February 2016|publisher=St Mirren F.C.|date=1 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208122415/http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=51796|archive-date=8 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Greenock Morton (loan)===
McMullan was loaned to [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on 24 February 2016, making his debut in a 3–0 Championship win at [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on the same day.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/14299148.Morton_swoop_to_sign_Celtic_man_on_loan/|title=Morton swoop to sign Celtic man on loan|publisher=Greenock Telegraph|date=24 February 2016|access-date=24 February 2016|first=Russell|last=Steele}}</ref> On 15 March at [[Cappielow]], he scored his first goal for the Ton, putting them 3–0 up at half time in an eventual 3–2 win over [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Greenock Morton 3-2 Queen of the South|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35751155|access-date=13 April 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 March 2016}}</ref>

===Dunfermline Athletic (loan)===
On 4 July 2016, McMullan was loaned to newly promoted Championship team [[Dunfermline Athletic]], as [[PJ Crossan]] made the move in the other direction on a permanent basis.<ref>{{cite news|title=Celtic: PJ Crossan signs as Paul McMullan joins Dunfermline on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36707176|access-date=4 July 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 23 June 2017, McMullan signed a two-year contract with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://dufc.co/news/united-sign-mcmullen/|title=United sign McMullan|publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]|date=23 June 2017|access-date=23 June 2017}}{{Dead link|date=May 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 7 January 2021, McMullan signed a pre-contract with United's [[Dundee derby|crosstown rivals]] [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], which would see him begin a two-year deal at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=7 January 2021|title=McMullan signs a pre-contract|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/mcmullan-signs-a-pre-contract/|access-date=7 January 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> On 26 January, McMullan joined Dundee on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=26 January 2021|title=Paul joins on loan|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/paul-joins-on-loan/|access-date=26 January 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> Despite only joining in January, McMullan would sit atop the league assist charts by the end of the season, and would play a key role in helping the club win the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-offs]] and gaining promotion back to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scottish Championship Top Assists|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/scottish-championship/top-scorers#TopAssists|access-date=27 May 2021|website=BBC}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=24 May 2021|title=Dundee promoted as Kilmarnock drop down for first time in 28 years|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/57089947|access-date=24 May 2021|website=BBC}}</ref> At the end of the season, McMullan was named in the [[SPFL]]'s Championship Team of the Season.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=9 June 2021|title=Championship Team of the Season 2020/21|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/championship-team-of-the-season-202021|access-date=9 June 2021|website=SPFL.co.uk}}</ref>

McMullan officially joined Dundee on his two-year deal in June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=11 June 2021|title=Paul signs permanent deal with club|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/paul-signs-permanent-deal-with-club/|access-date=11 June 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> He would score his first competitive goals for the club in the [[Scottish League Cup]], netting a brace against [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 July 2021|title=Dundee v Brora Rangers|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57825426|access-date=14 July 2021|website=BBC}}</ref> On 5 March 2022, McMullan would finally score his first league goal for the club since he joined over a year prior in a draw away to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee 'would take play-off place now' |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60534423 |access-date=2022-03-05}}</ref>

After returning to the [[Scottish Championship]] the following season, McMullan would have a very strong start in both goals and assists, and would be named the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|Championship Player of the Month]] in November 2022.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Championship award for McMullan {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/championship-award-for-mcmullan |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> At the end of the season McMullan would be nominated for [[PFA Scotland]]'s Championship Player of the Year,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |title=Dundee star Paul McMullan in the running for PFA Player of the Year |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4359466/dundee-paul-mcmullan-pfa-player-of-the-year/ |access-date=2023-05-05 |website=The Courier |date=3 May 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref> and would win the [[Scottish Championship]] with Dundee.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref> On 31 May 2023, Dundee announced McMullan had not been offered a new contract and would leave the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-31 |title=Squad update |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/squad-update/ |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Derry City ===
On 25 June 2023, McMullan signed with [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] club [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]], and would start playing for the side on 1 July.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Collins |first=Simon |date=25 June 2023 |title=Former Dundee winger excited for new challenge with Derry City in Ireland |url=https://www.derryjournal.com/sport/football/former-dundee-winger-paul-mcmullan-excited-for-new-challenge-with-derry-city-in-ireland-4196190 |access-date=25 June 2023}}</ref> He would make his first start and appearance in a home win over [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Patching scores injury-time winner against Sligo |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66140284 |access-date=2023-07-07}}</ref> McMullan scored his first goal for the ''Candystripes'' on 6 May 2024 in a league draw against [[Shelbourne F.C.|Shelbourne]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-06 |title=Candystripes denied by leaders Shelbourne at Brandywell |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cxx81pz77zjo |access-date=2024-05-06 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 30 June 2025, it was reported that McMullan had left Derry in favour of a move back to Scotland.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ferry |first=Gary |date=2025-06-30 |title=Winger McMullan departs Derry City |url=https://www.derrynow.com/news/derry-sport/1837955/winger-mcmullan-departs-derry-city.html |access-date=2025-06-30 |website=www.derrynow.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Raith Rovers ===
On 1 July 2025, McMullan returned to Scotland and joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Club |first1=Raith Rovers Football |last2=Fowlie |first2=Grace |date=2025-07-01 |title=WELCOME PAUL MCMULLAN! |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/welcome-paul-mcmullan/ |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=Raith Rovers Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===International===
McMullan represented Scotland at the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=101353&squadID=17 |title=Paul McMullan |publisher=Scottish Football Association |access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref> [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=101353&squadID=13 |title=Paul McMullan |publisher=Scottish Football Association |access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref> [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=101353&squadID=9 |title=Paul McMullan |publisher=Scottish Football Association |access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref> and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels. He made his debut for the under-21 team in March 2017, appearing in a goalless draw against [[Estonia national under-21 football team|Estonia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39425846 |title=Scotland Under-21 0-0 Estonia Under-21 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=28 March 2017 |access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref>

'''Cameron Ballantyne''' (born 13 April 1997) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|GreenocM}} club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]]. Ballantyne previously played for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], and had three loan spells with [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]]. Most recently, Ballantyne played for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]]

==Early life==
Cammy Ballantyne was born in [[Glasgow]] on 13 April 1997. He attended [[Duncanrig Secondary School]] in [[East Kilbride]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Thomson|first1=Paul|title=Cammy's delight as he pens three-year pro contract with Dundee Utd|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/cammys-delight-pens-three-year-pro-2403261#GtFi5L0ZFCCrvejb.97|accessdate=11 May 2016|work=Daily Record|date=15 October 2013|location=Glasgow}}</ref> After joining [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] as a youth player in 2007, he signed for the club as a professional in 2013.<ref name="DUFC">{{cite web|title=Development squad - Cammy Ballantyne|url=http://dufc.co/the-teams/development-squad/6875/|publisher=Dundee United F.C.|accessdate=11 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305151535/http://dufc.co/the-teams/development-squad/6875/|archive-date=5 March 2016|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Club===
Ballantyne made his first team debut against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in a [[Scottish Premiership]] match on 10 May 2016.<ref>[https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36189161 Scottish Premiership], [[BBC News]], 11 May 2016</ref> He joined [[Scottish League Two|League Two]] team [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on loan in August 2016,<ref>{{cite news|title=Tony Andreu: Norwich City midfielder joins Dundee United on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37239024|accessdate=2 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=31 August 2016}}</ref> with the loan being extended in January 2017 for the rest of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Duthie|first1=Tom|title=Ray McKinnon: Dundee United must use ball better - Evening Telegraph|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/ray-mckinnon-dundee-united-must-use-ball-better/|accessdate=2 March 2017|work=Evening Telegraph|location=Dundee}}</ref> In March 2017, Ballantyne extended his Dundee United contract to 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United's Cammy Ballantyne signs contract extension - The Courier|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/380135/dundee-uniteds-cammy-ballantyne-signs-contract-extension/|accessdate=2 March 2017|work=The Courier|date=2 March 2017|location=Dundee|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303045428/https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/380135/dundee-uniteds-cammy-ballantyne-signs-contract-extension/|archive-date=3 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He rejoined Montrose on a season-long loan in August 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cammy Ballantyne Loaned To Montrose|url=http://dufc.co/news/cammy-ballantyne-loaned-montrose/|accessdate=10 August 2017|publisher=Dundee United F.C.|date=9 August 2017|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810140544/http://dufc.co/news/cammy-ballantyne-loaned-montrose/|archive-date=10 August 2017|url-status=usurped}}</ref> His spell with Montrose was, however, cut short, and he was recalled at the start of January 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/5471/BALLANTYNE-RETURNS-TO-TANNADICE-AS-HORNBY-DEPARTS.html |title=Ballantyne returns as Hornby departs |publisher=Dundee United FC |date=1 January 2018 |accessdate=1 January 2018}}</ref> He then rejoined Montrose on an emergency loan for the remainder of the season in March 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cammy Ballantyne on emergency loan to Montrose|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/5564/CAMMY-BALLANTYNE-ON-EMERGENCY-LOAN-TO-MONTROSE.html|accessdate=16 March 2018|publisher=Dundee United F.C.|date=16 March 2018}}</ref> Following the end of his contract, he was released by United in May 2018<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44130428 |title=Captain Willo Flood among Dundee United departures |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=15 May 2018 |accessdate=15 May 2018}}</ref> and joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] in June 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=3663|title=SIGNING NEWS: CAMMY BALLANTYNE CHECKS IN|last=Galloway|first=Andy|date=26 June 2018|website=Dumbarton Football Club|access-date=}}</ref> After making 32 appearances for Dumbarton, he joined Montrose on a two year permanent deal in May 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.montrosefc.co.uk/index.php/latest-news-mma|title=LEAGUE WINNING DEFENDER RETURNS TO GABLE ENDIES|last=|first=|date=4 May 2019|website=Montrose Football Club|access-date=|archive-date=5 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505075001/https://www.montrosefc.co.uk/index.php/latest-news-mma|url-status=dead}}</ref>
In May 2022 Ballantyne signed for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], where he ended up getting him and the club promoted to the Scottish Championship, beating [[Hamilton Accies]] on penalties, with Ballantyne himself scoring Airdries' sixth.

On 14 June 2024, Ballantyne joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-14 |title=Cammy Ballantyne signs for the Ton - Greenock Morton FC |url=https://gmfc.net/cammy-ballantyne-signs-for-the-ton/,%20https://gmfc.net/cammy-ballantyne-signs-for-the-ton/ |access-date=2024-08-03 |language=en-US}}</ref>

===International===
Ballantyne was given his first call up for the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland under-17]] squad in March 2014.<ref name="DUFC" /> He was added to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad in March 2017, after [[Zak Jules]] withdrew.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39410290 |title=Dundee United's Cammy Ballantyne replaces Motherwell's Zack Jules for Scotland Under-21s |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=27 March 2017 |accessdate=27 March 2017}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle=== After a successful loan spell at the club, Tiffoney joined [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a two-year contract in June 2021 ahead of the upcoming [[2021–22 Scottish Championship]] season after Partick Thistle's title-winning [[Scottish League One]] campaign in [[2020–21 Scottish League One|2020–21]]. Tiffoney scored the winner on the opening day of the 2021–22 league season in a 3–2 home win over Queen of The South.{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57951141 | title=Partick Thistle 3-2 Queen of the South: Scott Tiffoney late goal gives hosts three points | work=BBC Sport | date=31 July 2021 }} During his first full season with Thistle; Tiffoney scored five goals and registered seven assists in all competitions, as Partick Thistle finished 4th in the Scottish Championship. Tiffoney suffered injury problems during spells of his second full season with Thistle, however, managed to register 12 goals and eight assists in all competitions during the 2022–23 campaign. '''Iain Wilson''' (born 15 December 1998) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|GreenocM}} club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]]. Wilson has previously played for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], and [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]]. Wilson also had two previous loan spells at the ''Doonhamers'' and has also represented Scotland from under-17 to under-21 levels.

==Club career==
On 6 December 2016, Wilson debuted for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] as a half-time in a match versus [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in a 5-1 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/14950876.aberdeen-5-kilmarnock-1-killie-hit-for-five-by-rampant-dons/ |title=Aberdeen 5, Kilmarnock 1: Killie hit for five by rampant Dons |work=Glasgow Times |publisher=Newsquest |date=7 December 2016 |accessdate=16 July 2020}}</ref> On 29 January 2019, Wilson was loaned out to [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] for the remainder of the [[2018-19 in Scottish football|2018-19]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-4327 |title=Scotland U21 Midfielder Joins |publisher=Queen of the South FC |date=29 January 2019 |accessdate=16 July 2020}}</ref> In January 2020, Wilson returned to the [[Dumfries]] club for a second loan spell.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-4914 |title=QosFC: Iain Returns |publisher=Queen of the South FC |date=31 January 2020 |accessdate=3 February 2020}}</ref>

In July 2020, Wilson departed ''Killie'' and signed for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Iain_Wilson_signs_for_Dunfermline&ID=12485 |title=Iain Wilson signs for Dunfermline |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=16 July 2020 |accessdate=16 July 2020}}</ref> On 30 January 2022, Wilson departed the ''Pars'' by mutual consent <ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Player_Update_&ID=13600 |title=Player Update |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=30 January 2022 |accessdate=31 January 2022}}</ref> and the following day signed for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] until the end of the [[2021-22 in Scottish football|2021-22]] season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Temple |first1=Alan |title=Released Dunfermline midfielder Iain Wilson joins relegation rivals |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/2964120/released-dunfermline-midfielder-iain-wilson-joins-morton/ |access-date=23 February 2022 |work=The Courier |date=31 January 2022}}</ref>

On 2 June 2022, Wilson signed a two-year contract for [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]], having previously had two loan spells at [[Palmerston Park|Palmerston]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://qosfc.com/news-5777 | title=QosFC: Return of the 'Shug' }}</ref>

On 16 August 2023, Wilson rejoined [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on a season-long loan from the [[Dumfries]] club.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/23726603.iain-wilson-rejoins-morton-dougie-imrie-adds-squad/ |title=Iain Wilson rejoins Morton as Dougie Imrie adds to squad |newspaper=Greenock Telegraph |first=Russell |last=Steele |date=16 August 2023 |accessdate=16 August 2023}}</ref>

==International career==

Selected for the [[Scotland national under-20 football team|Scotland under-20]] squad in the [[2017 Toulon Tournament]],<ref>{{ cite web | title = Scotland squad for Toulon announced | url = http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1957&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16955 | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association|Scottish FA]] | date = 17 May 2017 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> Wilson played as Scotland beat [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil under-20]]s 1–0, which was the nations first ever win against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] at any level.<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.largsandmillportnews.com/news/15336718.the-west-kilbride-teen-who-helped-scotland-beat-brazil-at-football/ | title = The West Kilbride teen who helped Scotland beat Brazil at football | newspaper = Largs & Millport Weekly News | date = 8 June 2017 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> The team went on to claim the bronze medal.<ref>{{ cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-third-at-toulon-tournament-with-3-0-win/ | title = Scotland finish third at Toulon Tournament with 3-0 win | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association|Scottish FA]] | date = 10 June 2017 |access-date = 1 July 2022}}</ref> It was the nations first ever medal at the competition.<ref>{{ cite web | title = JULES AND HOLSGROVE TAKE BRONZE WITH SCOTLAND IN TOULON | url = https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2017/june/jules-and-holsgrove-take-bronze-with-scotland-in-toulon/ | publisher = Reading FC | date = 11 June 2017 | access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref>

Selected for the [[2018 Toulon Tournament squads#Group B|under-21]] squad in the [[2018 Toulon Tournament]].<ref>{{ cite web | title=Scotland Under-21 squad announced for Toulon tournament | url = https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-21-squad-announced-for-toulon-tournament/ | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association|Scottish FA]] | date = 3 May 2018 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> They lost to [[Turkey national under-21 football team|Turkey under-21]]s in a penalty-out and finished fourth.<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-fourth-at-the-toulon-tournament-after-shoot-out-defeat-to-turkey/ | title = Scotland finish fourth at the Toulon tournament after shoot-out defeat to Turkey | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association|Scottish FA]] | date = 10 June 2018 |access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref>

'''Harry Cochrane''' (born 24 April 2001) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Arbroath F.C.|Greenock Morton]]. Cochrane has previously played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]], and Arbroath, as well as loan spells with [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] and [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]].

==Career==
===Youth football===
Cochrane attended Kirklandpark Primary in [[Strathaven]]<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/harry-cochrane-offers-glimpse-of-brighter-future-for-scotland-tz6c8ldjj | title=Harry Cochrane offers glimpse of brighter future for Scotland| work=[[The Times]]|date=20 December 2017|access-date=20 December 2017| last1=Campbell| first1=Jordan}}</ref> and later studied at [[Grange Academy, Kilmarnock]] where he was part of the [[Scottish Football Association]] Performance School.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/performance-school-graduate-stars-for-hearts/ | title=Performance School graduate stars for Hearts| work=scottishfa.co.uk| publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]]|date=3 October 2017|accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref> Cochrane began his football career with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], before transferring to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] at under-13 level.<ref name = "EEN">{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-academy-laying-local-foundations-for-the-future-1-4405916|title=Hearts academy laying local foundations for the future|date=29 March 2017|accessdate=15 July 2018|author=Barry Anderson|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715210533/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-academy-laying-local-foundations-for-the-future-1-4405916|archive-date=15 July 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
In June 2017 Cochrane signed a professional contract with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], which committed him to the club until 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hearts' Harry Cochrane sets out to beef himself up |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts-harry-cochrane-sets-out-beef-himself-1430383 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729122424/https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts-harry-cochrane-sets-out-beef-himself-1430383 |archive-date=2020-07-29 |access-date=2026-04-12 |language=en-GB}}</ref> The following month he played in all four of the first team's pre season friendlies,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.deadlinenews.co.uk/2017/07/09/ian-cathro-insists-age-no-barrier-harry-cochrane-hearts-16-year-old-stars-linfield/ | title=Ian Cathro insists age is no barrier at Hearts as 16-year-old Harry Cochrane stars against Linfield | work=deadlinenews.co.uk  | publisher =Capital City Press|date=9 July 2017 |accessdate=21 October 2017 }}</ref> netting in a 4–1 win against [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-post-match-harry-cochrane-shines-as-jambos-click-into-gear-1-4499094 | title=Harry Cochrane shines as Jambos click into gear | work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com | publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] | date=10 July 2017 | accessdate=21 October 2017 | archive-date=22 October 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171022032902/http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-post-match-harry-cochrane-shines-as-jambos-click-into-gear-1-4499094 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/linfield-1-4-hearts-16-year-old-harry-cochrane-nets-in-win-1-4498608 | title=16-year-old Harry Cochrane nets in win | work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com| publisher = [[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=8 July 2017 |accessdate=21 October 2017 }}</ref> On 15 August 2017, Cochrane played for Hearts [[Heart of Midlothian F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Under-20s]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] against [[Formartine United F.C.|Formartine United]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://spfl.co.uk/challenge-cup/fixture/3639989/ | title=Formartine 2 – 3 Hearts U20 | work=spfl.co.uk| publisher = [[Scottish Professional Football League]]|date=15 August 2017 |accessdate=20 December 2017 }}</ref> He made his first team debut<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/harry-cochrane-won-t-be-only-kid-to-break-through-at-hearts-1-4579455 | title=Harry Cochrane won't be only kid to break through at Hearts | work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com| publisher = [[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=6 October 2017 |accessdate=21 October 2017 }}</ref> for Hearts, aged 16,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hearts-name-16-year-old-11263877 | title=Hearts name 16 year old Harry Cochrane in starting line up for Dundee clash | work=dailyrecord.co.uk| publisher = [[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|date=30 September 2017 |accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref> on 30 September 2017, playing from the start in a 2–1 defeat against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] at [[Dens Park]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41370227 | title=Kerr Waddell scored twice to overcome Hearts' resistance and earn Dundee's second league win of the season.| work=bbc.co.uk/sport/| publisher = [[BBC Sport]]|date=30 September 2017 |accessdate=21 October 2017 }}</ref> In doing so he became the first [[Scottish Football Association]] Performance School graduate to start a [[Scottish Premiership]] game.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=2986&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=17262 | title=Performance School graduate stars for Hearts | work=scottishfa.co.uk| publisher = [[Scottish Football Association|SFA]]|date=3 October 2017 |accessdate=21 October 2017 }}</ref>

Cochrane scored the opening goal in Hearts' 4–0 win over [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 17 December 2017,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/absolutely-buzzing-16-year-old-11712262 | title='Absolutely buzzing' 16-year-old Harry Cochrane celebrates Celtic win | work=dailyrecord.co.uk| publisher = [[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|date=17 December 2017 |accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref> a result that ended Celtic's 69-game unbeaten run in domestic matches.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42297312 | title=Celtic's 69-game unbeaten domestic run was ended in emphatic style as they were stunned 4–0 by Hearts in the Scottish Premiership| work=bbc.co.uk/sport/| publisher = [[BBC Sport]]|date=17 December 2017|accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref> In doing so he became the club's youngest league goalscorer.<ref>https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/underwear-sink-confirmed-harry-cochrane-hearts-first-team-player-547266 {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref> The following week he was sent off in a match against [[St. Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] for a second bookable offence.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/st-johnstone-0-0-hearts-harry-cochrane-off-in-bore-draw-1-4646416| title=Harry Cochrane off in bore draw| work=scotsman.com| publisher =[[The Scotsman]]|date=23 December 2017 |accessdate=26 December 2017}}</ref> In April 2018, Cochrane signed a new contract with Hearts, which ran until 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43821036 |title=Hearts secure Harry Cochrane on new three-year deal after fine debut season |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=19 April 2018 |accessdate=19 April 2018}}</ref>

==== Dunfermline loan ====
Cochrane, along with Hearts teammate [[Anthony McDonald (Scottish footballer)|Anthony McDonald]], moved on a season-long loan to [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on 30 August 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-pair-harry-cochrane-and-anthony-mcdonald-join-dunfermline-1-4994438 |title=Hearts pair Harry Cochrane and Anthony McDonald join Dunfermline |first=Craig |last=Fowler |work=Scotsman |publisher=JPI Media |date=30 August 2019 |accessdate=30 August 2019}}</ref>

==== Montrose loan ====
On 30 October 2020, Cochrane joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on loan until January 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-league-1/1693060/harry-cochrane-hearts-montrose-fc-transfer-news/ |title=Montrose have snapped up Hearts youngster Harry Cochrane on loan |first=Marc |last=Deanie |date=30 October 2020 |accessdate=22 November 2020 |newspaper=The Courier }}</ref> The loan agreement was later extended to the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/harry-extends-montrose-loan|title = Harry extends Montrose loan | Heart of Midlothian Football Club}}</ref>

In April 2021, it was announced that Cochrane was set to leave Hearts at the end of the season following the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/cochrane-to-leave-hearts-at-end-of-season|title=Cochrane set to leave Hearts at end of season|website=heartsfc.co.uk|date=16 April 2021|access-date=9 July 2021}}</ref>

===Queen of the South===
On 24 July 2021, Cochrane signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] after a successful trial period.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-confirm-harry-cochrane-development-fee-after-midfielder-joins-new-club-3322598 |title=Hearts confirm Harry Cochrane development fee after midfielder joins new club |first=Mark |last=Atkinson |date=24 July 2021 |accessdate=25 July 2021 |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-5483|title=QosFC: Welcome – Harry Cochrane}}</ref>

On 24 May 2023, Cochrane signed a contract extension with the ''Doonhamers'' until 31 May 2025.<ref>{{cite web | title=QosFC: Harry's Back for Another Two Years | url=https://www.qosfc.com/news-6087 }}</ref>

During September 2023, Cochrane was appointed Queens new club captain, after [[Josh Todd (footballer)|Josh Todd]] decided to concentrate more on his own playing performances.

===Arbroath===
After spending four years with the Doonhamers, Cochrane joined Scottish Championship club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in July 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/football/ex-hearts-ace-seals-transfer-to-scottish-club-as-hes-handed-fresh-opportunity-after-high-level-experience/ar-AA1INsOR |access-date=2026-04-12 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref>

'''<big>Greenock Morton</big>'''

On 25 June, 2026, Cochrane was announced as a new signing for Championship side Greenock Morton, where he signed a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-06-25 |title=Greenock Morton (@Morton_FC) on X |url=https://x.com/Morton_FC/status/2070167635359330655 |access-date=2026-07-17 |work=X (formerly Twitter) |language=en-US}}</ref>

==International career==
He was a member of the Scotland under-16 Victory Shield squad.<ref name = "EEN"/> He was called up to represent [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland at under-17]] level in October 2017,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/15-performance-school-pupils-named-for-u17-qualifiers/ | title=15 Performance School pupils named for U17 qualifiers| work=scottishfa.co.uk| publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]]|date=9 October 2017|accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref> however was withdrawn from the squad by Hearts manager [[Craig Levein]], as he felt the "experience of being involved and perhaps playing in the first team at this minute in his career is more valuable than playing an international game."<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/harry-cochrane-will-benefit-more-with-hearts-than-scotland-1-4591437| title=Harry Cochrane 'will benefit more with Hearts than Scotland'| work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com| publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]| date=20 October 2017| accessdate=20 December 2017| archive-date=22 December 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222053003/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/harry-cochrane-will-benefit-more-with-hearts-than-scotland-1-4591437| url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''John Robertson''' (born 26 August 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

==Career==
Born in [[Edinburgh]],<ref name="auto"/> Robertson moved from [[Tynecastle F.C.|Tynecastle]] to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in June 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/team/john-robertson|title=Profile|accessdate=8 May 2018|publisher=St Johnstone F.C.}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 21 April 2018,<ref name = "2017-18"/> and was praised by manager [[Tommy Wright (footballer, born 1963)|Tommy Wright]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/641689/st-johnstone-boss-tommy-wright-has-high-hopes-for-john-robertson/|title=St Johnstone boss Tommy Wright has 'high hopes' for John Robertson|date=25 April 2018|accessdate=8 May 2018|author=Eric Nicolson|publisher=The Courier}}</ref> He was loaned to [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] in August 2019<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/cove-rangers/1809596/cove-rangers-sign-teenager-john-robertson-on-loan-deal-from-st-johnstone/ |title=Cove Rangers sign teenager John Robertson on loan deal from St Johnstone |work=Press & Journal |first=Jamie |last=Durent |date=1 August 2019 |accessdate=5 August 2019}}</ref> and [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] in October 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/1628167/tanto-olaofe-leaves-st-johnstone-and-john-robertson-goes-on-loan-to-forfar/|title=Tanto Olaofe leaves St Johnstone and John Robertson goes on loan to Forfar|first=Eric|last=Nicolson}}</ref>

Robertson was released by St Johnstone after the 2020–21 season and he then signed with [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghcityfc.com/2021/07/30/john-robertson-signs/|title=John Robertson Signs}}</ref> In June 2023 he moved to Northern Irish club [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65761512|title=Scottish striker Robertson to join Linfield|via=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref> Robertson had his contract terminated in October 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linfieldfc.com/latestnews.aspx?id=29098|title=Statement from Linfield Football Club|via=Linfield FC.com}}</ref>

In May 2026 it was announced that he would join [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] after signing a pre-contract agreement with them, on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Robbo the Rover!|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/robbo-the-rover/|website=Raith Rovers|date=7 May 2026|access-date=7 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Jack Hamilton''' (born 30 June 2000) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

==Career==
===Livingston===
Hamilton started his career with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] and spent time on loan at [[Penicuik Athletic F.C.|Penicuik Athletic]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/livingston-striker-jack-hamilton-loving-11412779|title=Livingston striker Jack Hamilton loving life on loan at Penicuik Athletic|first=Callum|last=Carson|date=26 October 2017|website=Daily Record}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.midlothianadvertiser.co.uk/sport/football/penicuik-parkhead-hamilton-line-face-celtic-2046905 |title=From Penicuik to Parkhead: Hamilton in line to face Celtic |publisher=Midlothian Advertiser |date=2 August 2018 |access-date=20 January 2021 |archive-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128015038/https://www.midlothianadvertiser.co.uk/sport/football/penicuik-parkhead-hamilton-line-face-celtic-2046905 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]] in 2018.<ref>{{soccerbase|104533}}</ref> During the January 2019 transfer window, Hamilton was then moved out on loan to [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.alloaathletic.co.uk/BlogView.aspx?pageid=2&ItemID=1894&mid=2|title=Jack Hamilton joins on loan|date=24 January 2019|access-date=25 January 2019|publisher=Alloa Athletic F.C.}}{{Dead link|date=September 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On 1 July 2019, Hamilton was sent out to [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] on a season long loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-4610|title=QosFC: Jack Hamilton|website=www.qosfc.com}}</ref> In March 2020 he signed a new contract with Livingson.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-hamilton-contract-extension/|title=Jack Hamilton – contract extension|date=9 March 2020}}</ref> In September 2020 he moved on loan to [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/east-fife-take-livingston-striker-jack-hamilton-loan-2967492|title=East Fife take Livingston striker Jack Hamilton on loan|website=www.fifetoday.co.uk}}</ref> After scoring seven goals from nine league games for the Fifers, Hamilton was named SPFL League 1 Player of the Month for December.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/hamilton-named-player-of-the-month|title=Hamilton named Player of the Month | SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref>  He was recalled by his parent club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on 8 January 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-is-back/ |title=Jack is back |publisher=Livingston FC |date=8 January 2021}}</ref> On 29 January, he headed out on loan once again, this time joining [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/jack-hamilton/|title=Jack Hamilton|publisher=[[Arbroath F.C.]]|date=29 January 2021|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref> where he scored eight goals in fourteen games<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/thank-you-jack-hamilton-2/|title=Thank you Jack Hamilton|date=6 June 2022}}</ref> and earned Scottish Championship Player of the Month for April.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/hamilton-earns-april-award|title=Hamilton earns April award | SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Thus, he collected two SPFL Player of the Month awards on two different teams for the 2020–2021 season.<ref name="auto"/>

In January 2022, Hamilton re-joined Arbroath on loan for the remainder for the [[2021–22 in Scottish football|2021–22]] season,<ref>{{Cite web|date=1 January 2022|title=Welcome back Jack Hamilton|url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/welcome-back-jack/|access-date=1 January 2022|website=Arbroath FC|language=en-GB}}</ref> where he scored ten goals in twenty appearances.<ref name="auto1"/>  He was twice named SPFL Team of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/team-of-the-week-48196|title=Team of the Week | SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/team-of-the-week-48396|title=Team of the Week | SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Between his two loan spells, he scored eighteen goals in thirty four games for Arbroath.<ref name="auto1"/>

On 1 July 2022, Hamilton signed a new two-year deal at Livingston.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-hamilton-signs-contract-extension/|title=Hamilton signs contract extension|website=livingstongc.co.uk|date=July 2022 }}</ref>

On 20 July 2022, Hamilton signed for [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]] on a season-long loan with a view to a permanent deal for the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62244036 |title=Jack Hamilton: Hartlepool United sign Livingston striker on initial loan deal |website=BBC Sport |date=20 July 2022 |access-date=22 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/2022/july/pools-sign-hamilton/|title=Pools sign Hamilton|website=HartlepoolUnited.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62244036|title=Hartlepool sign Livingston striker Hamilton|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> He was named in the League Two Team of the Week for back to back weeks on 31 December 2022,<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Sky Bet League Two |author-link=Sky Bet League Two |user=SkyBetLeagueTwo |number=1609158804104437760 |date=31 December 2022 |title=Your final #SkyBetLeagueTwo Team of the Week of 2022 💪 #EFL {{!}} @CazooUK https://t.co/k99Q5tNa55 |language=en |access-date=16 January 2023}}</ref> and 3 January 2023.<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Sky Bet League Two |author-link=Sky Bet League Two |user=SkyBetLeagueTwo |number=1610252912508436485 |date=3 January 2023 |title=The first #SkyBetLeagueTwo Team of the Week of 2023 🙌 🔋 Powered by @WhoScored ratings. #EFL {{!}} @CazooUK https://t.co/9DacKyRFtZ |language=en |access-date=16 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230103225735/https://twitter.com/skybetleaguetwo/status/1610252912508436485 |archive-date=3 January 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
On 29 May 2023, Hamilton moved to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] for a nominal transfer fee.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/61839/jack-hamilton-signs-up.htm |title=Jack Hamilton Signs Up |website=Raith Rovers FC |date=29 May 2023 |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-hamilton-departs/ |title=Jack Hamilton departs for Raith Rovers |publisher=Livingston FC |date=29 May 2023 |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref>
