'''Glenn Ethan Walker''' (born 28 July 2002) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2021-09-17 |title=Ethan Walker Joins The Coasters On Loan |url=https://www.afcfylde.co.uk/ethan-walker-joins-the-coasters-on-loan/ |access-date=2024-01-02 |website=AFC Fylde |language=en-GB}}</ref> for {{Scottish football updater|AyrUnite}} club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/-/528663/|title=England - E. Walker - Profile with news, career statistics and history - Soccerway}}</ref>

==Club career==

===Preston North End===

Walker signed his first professional contract in October 2018 and in December 2018, he became the youngest player to appear in a league game for [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] when he came on a substitute in a 1–1 draw against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] at the age of 16 years and 156 days.

On 12 December 2019, Walker joined [[Altrincham F.C.]] on loan for the rest of the 2019–20 season.<ref>[https://www.pnefc.net/news/2019/december/ethan-walker-joins-altrincham-on-youth-loan/ Ethan Walker Joins Altrincham On Youth Loan], pnefc.net, 12 December 2019</ref> He was still available to play for Preston's youth team's during his loan spell at [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]]. However, he was recalled on 14 January 2020<ref>[https://www.altrinchamfc.com/news/ethan-walker-recalled-by-preston-north-end Ethan Walker Recalled by Preston North End]{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}, altrinchamfc.com, 14 January 2020</ref> and later on the same month, he joined [[Stalybridge Celtic F.C.|Stalybridge Celtic]] on loan instead, until the end of the season along with fellow Preston teammate [[Adam O'Reilly]].<ref>{{cite web |title=PNE Duo Join Stalybridge Celtic |url=https://www.pnefc.net/news/2020/january/pne-duo-join-stalybridge-celtic/ |publisher=Preston North End FC |accessdate=11 February 2020}}</ref>

On 12 September 2020, Walker joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ethan Walker: Preston North End loan forward to Carlisle United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54131565 |publisher=BBC Sport |accessdate=12 September 2020}}</ref> After appearing in four league games for the Cumbrians, Walker was recalled by his parent club [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] on 8 January 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.carlisleunited.co.uk/news/2021/january/loan-preston-forward-recalled/ |title=Preston forward recalled |publisher=Carlisle United FC |date=8 January 2021}}</ref>

In September 2021, he joined [[National League North]] side [[AFC Fylde]] on loan for a month.<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.pnefc.net/news/2021/september/walker-joins-afc-fylde-on-loan/ |title=Walker Joins AFC Fylde On Loan |publisher=Preston North End FC |date=17 September 2021}}</ref> He returned to Preston after only two games due to injury, but re-joined the Coasters in November until January 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.pnefc.net/news/2021/november/walker-rejoins-afc-fylde-on-loan/ |title=Walker Rejoins AFC Fylde On Loan |publisher=Preston North End FC |date=19 November 2021}}</ref> Walker was released at the end of the [[2021–22 Preston North End F.C. season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pnefc.net/news/2022/may/preston-north-end-retained-list-confirmed/|title=Preston North End Retained List Confirmed|website=www.pnefc.net|date=9 May 2022}}</ref>

===Blackburn Rovers===

On 30 May 2022, it was announced that Walker had signed for [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rovers.co.uk/news/2022/may/30/ethan-arrives-/ | title=Rovers recruit exciting Ethan! | date=30 May 2022 }}</ref>

Playing for Rovers' youth team as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]], in his first twelve months at Ewood Park he scored seven goals in 19 appearances.

On 1 September 2023, it was announced that Walker had joined [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] on loan for the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66691356 | title=Morecambe take Rovers striker Walker on loan | work=BBC Sport }}</ref> On 2 January 2024, it was announced Walker had been recalled from his spell at [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] & had joined [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ethan joins Latics on loan|url=https://www.rovers.co.uk/news/2024/january/02/ethan-joins-latics-on-loan/ |access-date=2 January 2024 |publisher=Blackburn Rovers Official Site|date=2 January 2023}}</ref>

On 18 May 2024, it was confirmed Walker will be leaving the club at the end of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rovers.co.uk/news/2024/may/18/retain-list-confirmed/|title=Retain List confirmed|date=18 May 2024|website=Blackburn Rovers}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
On 18 June 2024, it was announced Walker will join [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on 1 July when his contract at Blackburn Rovers expires.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=AyrUnitedFC |author-link=Ayr United F.C. |number=1803148189039464627 |title=The Club are delighted to announce the signing of winger, Ethan Walker on a pre-contract agreement. |date=18 June 2024 |url=https://x.com/AyrUnitedFC/status/1803148189039464627?t=v_j23uvUp9zyur9Vy-uKug&s=19 |access-date=18 June 2024}}</ref>

'''Kyle Turner''' (born 10 November 1997) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]]. Turner began his career with [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]], where he made 138 appearances over a four-year period, and has also played for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], and has also had a loan with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].

==Club career==

===Stranraer===
Turner began his career playing with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] and [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] youth teams, before signing with [[Scottish League One]] side [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/people.php?SID=First%20Team&ID=136 |title=First Team Squad: Kyle Turner |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |accessdate=30 July 2019}}</ref> His first appearance for the [[Stair Park]] club came as a final-minute substitution against [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on 12 September 2015,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34161005 |title=Stenhousemuir 1 – 0 Stranraer |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=12 September 2015 |accessdate=7 July 2019}}</ref> with his first full start coming a week later against [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34230553 |title=Stranraer 0 – 1 Albion Rovers |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=19 September 2015 |accessdate=7 July 2019}}</ref>

===Dunfermline Athletic===
Turner spent four years with Stranraer, before signing a two-year contract with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on 28 May 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Kyle_Turner_joins_DAFC&ID=11249 |title=Kyle Turner joins DAFC |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=28 May 2019 |accessdate=7 July 2019}}</ref> In March 2021, Turner moved on loan to Scottish League One club [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Player_News&ID=13020 |title=Player News |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=16 March 2021 |accessdate=16 March 2021}}</ref> Turner left Dunfermline following the end of his contract in May 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Player_Update_&ID=13149 |title=Player update |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=31 May 2021 |accessdate=31 May 2021}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle (1st spell)===
Turner signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club Partick Thistle, who he previously played with as a youth player.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-kyle-turner-is-a-jag/ |title=Kyle Turner is a Jag |publisher=Partick Thistle F.C. |date=31 May 2021 |accessdate=31 May 2021}}</ref>

Turner scored his first goal for Thistle, scoring a 96th minute winner in a 1-0 home win against Raith Rovers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59618522|title=Turner late goal downs Raith Rovers|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

During his second season with Thistle, Turner was part of the squad that made it to the Scottish Premiership promotion play off final, which Thistle eventually lost on penalties to Ross County, meaning the club remained in the Scottish Championship. Following this Turner left the club.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/trio-leave-partick-thistle/ | title=Trio leave Partick Thistle }}</ref>

===Ross County===
Turner signed a two-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in June 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cpe9zl7z3d3o | title=Turner joins County on two-year deal |website=BBC Sport | date=21 June 2023 | accessdate=21 June 2023}}</ref>

==== Raith Rovers (loan) ====
Turner joined Raith Rovers on loan until the end of the 23/24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kyle Turner joins Raith Rovers on loan |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/kyle-turner-joins-raith-rovers-on-loan |access-date=2024-01-10 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref>

=== Partick Thistle (2nd spell) ===
In June 2024, Turner returned to [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kyle returns to Firhill Road on two-year deal |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/kyle-returns-to-firhill-road-on-two-year-deal/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

Turner scored on his second Thistle debut in a 3–2 Scottish League Cup group stage win over Montrose,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Partick Thistle v Montrose – 13th July 2024 |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-fixture/partick-thistle-v-montrose-13th-july-2024/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> before scoring his first league goal in his second spell through a late penalty in a 1–0 home win over [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Partick Thistle vs Ayr United: Championship stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cp3z9q0x060t |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

He departed the club at the end of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Squad Update – 29th May 2026 |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/squad-update-29th-may-2026/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

=== Raith Rovers ===
Kyle Turner re-signed for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in June 2026 on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |date=2026-06-04 |title=Kyle Turner is Back |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/kyle-turner-is-back/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=Raith Rovers Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his return debut as a substitute in a league cup tie against [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Raith Rovers vs Elgin City: Scottish League Cup score updates & stats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c6211277vjrt |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Turner is the son of former [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Morton]], [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] and [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] midfielder [[Tommy Turner (footballer)|Tommy Turner]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/17669438.stranraer-midfielder-kyle-turner-signs-for-dunfermline/?ref=twtrec |title=Stranraer midfielder Kyle Turner signs for Dunfermline as Myles Hipployte quits |first=Ross |last=Hart |work=Dunfermline Press |publisher=Newsquest |date=28 May 2019 |accessdate=28 May 2019}}</ref>

'''Zachary Scott Robinson''' (born 11 June 2002) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]], most recently for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. He came through the academy of [[AFC Wimbledon]] and made a number of first team appearances, as well as playing on loan for a number of lower league English sides before joining Scottish side [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a season-long loan during which Robinson finished as the team's top league goalscorer and won the [[Scottish Championship]]. Robinson returned to Dundee, then in the [[Scottish Premiership]], for another season-long loan before departing AFC Wimbledon.

==Career==
===AFC Wimbledon===
On 9 September 2019, whilst still a second year scholar at [[AFC Wimbledon]], Robinson joined [[Basingstoke Town F.C.|Basingstoke Town]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2019/september/young-dons-pair-go-out-on-loan/|title=Young Dons pair go out on loan|publisher=AFC Wimbledon|date=9 September 2019|access-date=15 December 2019}}</ref> On 13 November 2019, Robinson made his debut for the club in a 3–1 [[EFL Trophy]] loss against [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/11/13/england/football-league-trophy/southend-united-fc/afc-wimbledon/3110337/|title=Southend United vs. AFC Wimbledon 3–1|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=15 December 2019}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Wimbledon in an [[EFL Trophy]] tie against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C. Reserves and Academy|Brighton & Hove Albion U21s]] on 22 September 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/sport/18740235.albion-u21s-suffer-defeat-afc-wimbledon-efl-trophy/ |title=Albion U21's suffer defeat to AFC Wimbledon in EFL Trophy |date=22 September 2020 |work=The Argus |access-date=23 September 2020}}</ref> He made his league debut on 26 December 2020 in a 2–0 defeat to [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]], coming off of the bench to replace [[Ethan Chislett]] in the 87th minute of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55373547|title=Oxford United 2–0 AFC Wimbledon|work=BBC Sport|date=26 December 2020|accessdate=15 April 2021}}</ref>

On 12 April 2021, Robinson joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[Woking F.C.|Woking]] on loan until the end of the season,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2021/april/young-forward-joins-woking-on-loan/|title=Young Forward joins Woking on loan|publisher=AFC Wimbledon|date=12 April 2021|accessdate=15 April 2021}}</ref> making his debut the following day as he played the entirety of an incredible 4–3 defeat at home to [[Bromley F.C.|Bromley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56645366|title=Woking 3–4 Bromley|work=BBC Sport|date=13 April 2021|accessdate=15 April 2021}}</ref>

In August 2021, Robinson joined [[National League South]] side, [[Hemel Hempstead Town F.C.|Hemel Hempstead Town]] on a one-month loan and went onto net on his debut during a 4–2 defeat to [[Maidstone United F.C.|Maidstone United]], giving the Tudors an early lead in the 36th minute.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Zach is quick off the mark! |url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2021/august/zach-is-quick-off-the-mark/ |publisher=AFC Wimbledon |date=16 August 2021 |access-date=23 August 2021}}</ref>

On 8 January 2022, Robinson joined [[National League South]] side [[Hampton & Richmond Borough F.C.|Hampton & Richmond Borough]] on a one-month loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2022/january/young-dons-go-out-on-loan/ |title=Young Dons go out on loan |publisher=AFC Wimbledon |date=8 January 2022 |access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref> He went onto feature ten times, scoring three goals before being recalled by Wimbledon in March 2022.

====Loans to Dundee====
On 30 July 2022, after signing a two-year contract extension with Wimbledon,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zach loaned to Scottish club |url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2022/july/zach-loaned-to-scottish-club/ |access-date=31 July 2022 |publisher=AFC Wimbledon |language=en-gb}}</ref> Robinson joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 July 2022 |title=Zach joins |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/zach-joins/ |access-date=30 July 2022 |publisher=Dundee F.C. |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |title=Dundee seal loan deal for AFC Wimbledon striker Zach Robinson |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/3546532/dundee-seal-loan-deal-for-afc-wimbledon-striker-zach-robinson/ |access-date=31 July 2022 |website=The Courier |date=30 July 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his debut for Dundee on the same day against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Thistle hold on for win in five-goal thriller |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62275202 |access-date=30 July 2022}}</ref> On 12 August, Robinson scored his first goal for Dundee, in a home win over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee end Arbroath run in six-goal thriller |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62431314 |access-date=12 August 2022}}</ref> After a very successful first half of the season with Dundee, scoring 8 goals in 19 appearances, Robinson was recalled early by Wimbledon in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 January 2023 |title=Zach recalled |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/zach-recalled/ |access-date=6 January 2023 |publisher=Dundee F.C. |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 31 January 2023, Robinson returned on loan to Dundee until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 February 2023 |title=Zach's back |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/zachs-back/ |access-date=1 February 2023 |publisher=Dundee F.C. |language=en-US}}</ref> He marked his league return with the ''Dark Blues'' by scoring the opening goal in a 3–0 victory over [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee v Cove Rangers |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63896823 |access-date=12 February 2023}}</ref> Upon his return he formed a successful striking partnership with [[Alex Jakubiak]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |title=Dundee loan star Zach Robinson opens up on 'older brother' relationship with strike partner Alex Jakubiak and targets more goals |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4298380/dundee-zach-robinson-older-brother-alex-jakubiak/ |access-date=5 May 2023 |website=The Courier |date=13 April 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Robinson finished off his excellent loan spell with the ''Dark Blues'' in style, scoring his team-leading 12th league goal in a win over [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] which clinched the [[Scottish Championship]] title for Dundee.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=5 May 2023}}</ref>

On 30 June 2023, Robinson re-joined Dundee, now a [[Scottish Premiership]] side, on a season-long loan from Wimbledon.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2023 |title=Zach is back! |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/zach-is-back/ |access-date=30 June 2023 |publisher=Dundee F.C. |language=en-US}}</ref> He netted a brace against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] to open his scoring account in his second spell.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee v Dumbarton |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66193767 |access-date=26 July 2023}}</ref> Robinson would score his first Premiership goal on 11 November in a 4–0 win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite news |title='Outstanding' Dundee hammer St Mirren to go fifth |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67318545 |access-date=11 November 2023}}</ref>

In April 2024, AFC Wimbledon confirmed that Robinson would leave the club upon the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Retained List 2023/24 |url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2024/april/retained-list-202324/ |access-date=31 May 2024 |publisher=AFC Wimbledon |language=en-gb}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 20 June 2024, Robinson joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gibson |first=Scott |date=20 June 2024 |title=Zach Robinson signs two-year deal |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/06/20/zach-robinson-signs-two-year-deal/ |access-date=20 June 2024 |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |language=en}}</ref> He made his competitive debut in a win over [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Motherwell vs Edinburgh City: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crgenrvw24jt |access-date=13 July 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 20 September, Robinson scored his first goal for the ''Steelmen'' in a [[Scottish League Cup]] quarter-final victory over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] which saw Motherwell return to [[Hampden Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Motherwell vs Dundee United: Scottish League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c62rrpegv5yt |access-date=2024-09-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 3 December, Motherwell confirmed that Robinson had ruptured his [[achilles tendon]] during a training session and would miss the remainder of the season as well as the full season after it.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-03 |title=Motherwell striker Zach Robinson to miss rest of season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cj0r4m157ggo |access-date=2024-12-04 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2024 |title=Zach Robinson sustains significant injury |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/12/03/zach-robinson-sustains-significant-injury/ |access-date=4 December 2024 |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=[[Motherwell FC]]}}</ref>

On 20 May 2026, Motherwell confirmed that Robinson would leave the club when his contract expired that summer.<ref>{{cite web |title=2025/26 end of season squad update |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/05/20/2025-26-end-of-season-squad-update-2/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=20 May 2026 |date=20 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Jai Tyler Rowe''' (born 8 August 2001) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

==Career==
Jai made his [[EFL League Two|League Two]] debut for [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]] on 3 March 2020 in an away fixture against [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]]. Jai started the game, but was substituted on the 73rd minute for [[Yasin Ben El-Mhanni]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Swindon Town 2-0 Scunthorpe United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51712464 |accessdate=3 March 2020|publisher=bbc.co.uk|date=3 March 2020}}</ref> Following relegation to the [[National League (division)|National League]] at the end of the [[2021–22 Scunthorpe United F.C. season|2021–22 season]], Rowe signed a new two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scunthorpe-united.co.uk/news/2022/june/jai-rowe-signs-new-contract/|title=Jai Rowe signs new contract|website=www.scunthorpe-united.co.uk|date=14 June 2022|accessdate=14 June 2022}}</ref> On 23 March 2023, he left Scunthorpe United by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scunthorpe-united.co.uk/news/2023/march/jai-rowe-leaves-the-iron/|title=Jai Rowe leaves the Iron|website=www.scunthorpe-united.co.uk|date=23 March 2023|accessdate=23 March 2023}}</ref>

Following his departure from Scunthorpe United, Rowe signed for [[Aldershot Town F.C.|Aldershot Town]] on a short-term deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theshots.co.uk/new-signing-jai-rowe/|title=NEW SIGNING: Jai Rowe|website=www.theshots.co.uk|date=23 March 2023|accessdate=23 March 2023}}</ref> He was released at the end of this deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theshots.co.uk/2023-retained-list/|title=2023 RETAINED LIST|website=www.theshots.co.uk|date=7 May 2023|accessdate=9 May 2023}}</ref>

On 6 October 2023, he signed for [[National League North]] club [[Boston United F.C.|Boston United]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bostonunited.co.uk/news/united-recruit-defender-rowe-2808678.html |title=United recruit defender Rowe |publisher=Boston United |date=6 October 2023 |accessdate=7 October 2023}}</ref>

On 7 June 2025, Rowe joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Club |first=Raith Rovers Football |last2=Fowlie |first2=Grace |date=2025-06-07 |title=WELCOME, JAI ROWE! |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/welcome-jai-rowe/ |access-date=2025-06-07 |website=Raith Rovers Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Carlo Pignatiello''' (born 16 January 2000) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].

==Career==
Pignatiello began his career at youth level with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and later played for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] before joining [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/team/playing-squad/carlo-pignatiello/|title=Carlo Pignatiello}}</ref> He had loan spells with [[BSC Glasgow F.C.|BSC Glasgow]] in the [[Lowland League]], where he was voted the club's Young Player of the Season,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-02-24 |title=Carlo Pignatiello |url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/carlo-pignatiello/ |access-date=2024-10-08 |website=Arbroath FC |language=en}}</ref> and [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in [[Scottish League One]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/carlo-pignatiello-hoping-stand-out-21299017|title=Livi youngster looking to shine against Rangers in Scottish Cup|first=Callum|last=Carson|date=January 17, 2020|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

He made his professional debut as a late substitute in a [[Scottish Premiership]] 3–2 defeat against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in September 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/livingston-youngster-carlo-pignatiello-reflects-22730660|title=Livingston youngster Carlo Pignatiello reflects on 'pretty special' debut|first=Callum|last=Carson|date=September 23, 2020|website=Daily Record}}</ref> Pignatiello was loaned to [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in February 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Black|first=Dave|date=2021-02-24|title=Carlo Pignatiello joins Arbroath on loan|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/carlo-pignatiello-joins-arbroath-on-loan/|access-date=2021-07-28|website=Livingston FC|language=en-GB}}</ref> He then joined [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on a season long loan in July 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dumbarton Football Club - CARLO PIGNATIELLO JOINS DUMBARTON ON LOAN|url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=4995|access-date=2021-07-03|website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the Sons in a 3–1 victory against [[Sauchie Juniors F.C.|Sauchie Juniors]] in November 2021<ref>{{Cite web|last=Clarke|first=Fraser|date=2021-11-27|title=Dumbarton 3-1 Sauchie Juniors - Sons leave it late to avoid a Scottish Cup shock|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/dumbarton-3-1-sauchie-juniors-25562470|access-date=2021-11-27|website=Daily Record|language=en}}</ref> and was named the club's Young Player of the Year and Players' Player of the Year at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dumbarton Football Club - CONNER IS PLAYER OF THE YEAR |url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=5314 |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref>

On 23 May 2022, it was announced, via the club's website, that he would join [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on a pre-contract deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gmfc.net/carlo-pignatiello-signs-pre-contract-agreement/|title=Carlo Pignatiello signs pre-contract agreement|work=Greenock Morton FC|publisher=gmfc.net|date=23 May 2022|accessdate=29 June 2022}}</ref> He made his first appearance for the club in a pre-season friendly draw against [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] at [[Raydale Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/Morton_FC/status/1540679772275183616|title=Today's team to face Annan|publisher=[[Twitter]]|work=Greenock Morton FC|date=25 June 2022|accessdate=29 June 2022}}</ref> Pignatiello left Morton by mutual consent at the end of the 2022–23 season, with the club saying he wished to pursue an opportunity outside of football.<ref>{{cite web |title=2022/23 End of Season Squad Update |publisher=Greenock Morton FC |website=www.gmfc.net |url=https://www.gmfc.net/2022-23-end-of-season-squad-update/ |date=11 May 2023 |access-date=11 May 2023}}</ref> He returned to Dumbarton on a two-year deal in May 2023<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Jack |date=2023-05-29 |title=CARLO IS BACK AT THE ROCK |url=https://dumbartonfootballclub.com/carlo-is-back-at-the-rock/ |access-date=2023-05-29 |website=Dumbarton Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> and was named in the PFA League Two Team of the Year for the [[2023–24 Scottish League Two|2023–24]] season<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kearney |first=Ben |date=19 April 2024 |title=Five Stenhousemuir title-winning stars included in PFA Scotland League Two team of the year |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/five-stenhousemuir-title-winning-stars-included-in-pfa-scotland-league-two-team-of-the-year-4598498 |access-date=3 May 2024 |website=Falkirk Herald}}</ref> as he helped the Sons to promotion to [[Scottish League One]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Fraser |date=2024-05-20 |title=Spartans 2-2 Dumbarton - Sons win promotion on Friday night to remember |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/spartans-2-2-dumbarton-sons-32851518 |access-date=2024-05-23 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> He scored the club's first goal back in [[2024–25 Scottish League One|League One]], a volleyed equaliser in a 1-1 draw with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web '''Michael James Ruth''' (born 8 January 2002) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. Ruth has previously played for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] and [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], as well as loan spells with [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] and [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

==Early and personal life==
Ruth was born in [[Glasgow]].<ref name="soccerway">{{soccerway|michael-ruth/544134|accessdate=14 October 2020}}</ref>

==Career==
After progressing through their youth academy, Ruth debuted for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on 31 March 2018 versus [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 September 2020 |title=Michael Ruth |url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/michael-ruth/ |access-date=14 October 2020 |website=arbroathfc.co.uk |publisher=Arbroath F.C.}}</ref> and made ten league appearances for the Spiders, scoring one goal.<ref name="soccerway" />

Ruth signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a two-year contract in June 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cryle |first=Ryan |date=18 June 2019 |title=Aberdeen land striker Ruth, 17, from Queen's Park |url=https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/donsnews/aberdeen-land-striker-ruth-17-from-queens-park/ |access-date=14 October 2020 |website=Evening Express}}</ref> Ruth signed a one-year contract extension with the Dons in September 2020 and joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 September 2020 |title=Dons striker signs new deal |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2020/09/05/dons-striker-signs-new-deal/ |access-date=14 October 2020 |website=afc.co.uk |publisher=Aberdeen F.C.}}</ref> The loan was curtailed on 1 February 2021, as the Dons made several squad changes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bryce |first=Liam |date=1 February 2021 |title=Derek McInnes admits Aberdeen were 'vigorous' in Florian Kamberi chase |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/florian-kamberi-vigorous-aberdeen-transfer-23425641 |access-date=2 February 2021 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

Ruth was loaned to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in September 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/3447302/aberdeen-youngster-michael-ruth-loaned-out-to-league-one-falkirk/ |title=Aberdeen youngster Michael Ruth loaned out to League One Falkirk |first=Ryan |last=Cryle |newspaper=Press & Journal |date=6 September 2021 |accessdate=6 September 2021}}</ref>

On 14 June 2022, after his contract expired at the Dons, Ruth signed a one-year contract for [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-5784 | title=QosFC: Michael Ruth Next in }}</ref>

Ruth was released by the ''Doonhamers'' at the end of the [[2022-23 in Scottish football|2022-23]] season.<ref>https://qosfc.com/news-6077</ref>

Ruth signed for [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Jack |date=2023-06-15 |title=MICHAEL RUTH SIGNS FOR DUMBARTON |url=https://dumbartonfootballclub.com/michael-ruth-signs-for-dumbarton/ |access-date=2023-06-15 |website=Dumbarton Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> He scored 15 goals for the Sons in the [[2023–24 Dumbarton F.C. season|2023–24 season]], including a double in the playoff final against [[The Spartans F.C.|The Spartans]], as the club won promotion to [[Scottish League One]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Watch: Spartans v Dumbarton (agg 1-2) in Scottish League 1 play-off final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4n11qq33v1t |access-date=2024-05-18 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He signed a new season long deal with the club in May 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Jack |date=2024-05-29 |title=RUTHY SIGNS NEW DEAL |url=https://dumbartonfootballclub.com/ruthy-signs-new-deal/ |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=Dumbarton Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 12 June 2025, Ruth returned to his first club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] and signed a permanent deal with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=David |date=2025-06-12 |title=Queen's Park add former Aberdeen striker to First team squad |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/queens-park-michael-ruth-aberdeen-falkirk-striker/ |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Mark McKenzie''' (born 17 August 2000) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|AyrUnite}} club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref name="soccerbase">{{soccerbase|121859}}</ref>

==Career==
McKenzie progressed through the youth academy at [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]],<ref name="forfar">{{Cite web |last=Coutts |first=Christopher |date=25 February 2020 |title='Loons' sign Ayr United striker |url=https://www.forfarathletic.co.uk/item/4115-loons-sign-ayr-united-striker |access-date=18 October 2020 |website=forfarathletic.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> and made his debut for the club on 7 September 2019 against [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]], before making his league debut later that month in a 4–1 [[Scottish Championship]] victory over [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].<ref name="soccerbase" />

He joined [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on loan on 25 February 2020.<ref name="forfar" />

McKenzie scored his first senior goals on 16 March 2021 with a brace in a 3–1 win over [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref name="soccerway" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Stuart |date=17 March 2021 |title=Ayr United star McKenzie: I've waited for my chance – now I'll take it |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/ayr-united-kid-mark-mckenzie-23743092 |access-date=20 March 2021 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

'''Matthew Shiels''' (born 13 September 2000) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|left back]] for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].

==Early and personal life==
Shiels was born in [[Glasgow]].<ref name="auto"/> His paternal grandparents were from Donegal in Ireland,<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.donegaldaily.com/2017/11/06/rangers-man-with-strong-donegal-connections-gets-irish-call-up/|title=Rangers man with strong Donegal connections gets Irish call-up – Donegal Daily|first=Chris|last=McNulty|website=www.donegaldaily.com|date=6 November 2017 }}</ref> and he grew supporting [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dumbarton's Matty Shiels set for Cove Rangers switch after Scottish Cup goal – Daily Record |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/dumbartons-matty-shiels-set-cove-31941627 |access-date=25 June 2024 |website=www.dailyrecord.co.uk |date=22 January 2024 }}</ref>

==Club career==
After playing youth football for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], and spending loan spells at [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]], [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] and [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]],<ref>{{soccerbase|93410}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/matthew-shiels-joins-clyde-on-loan/6e4uo0xw60RI5S3qQOKBwd|title=Matthew Shiels Joins Clyde On Loan|website=www.rangers.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.donegaldaily.com/2020/09/01/rangers-player-with-donegal-links-goes-out-on-loan/|title=Rangers player with Donegal links goes out on loan – Donegal Daily|first=Chris|last=McNulty|website=www.donegaldaily.com|date=September 2020 }}</ref> as well as in the United States with [[Orange County SC]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://orangeandblacksoccercast.com/news-1/rangers-fc-orange-county-sc-francis-jacobs-cammy-palmer-danny-finlayson-matthew-shiels|title=Rangers Players Head to Orange County SC, Francis 4–0 victory against [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]] in November 2023,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Fraser |date=10 November 2023 |title=Dumbarton's Matty Shiels says confidence is key to sparkling recent showings |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/former-rangers-defender-matty-shiels-31407494 |access-date=10 November 2023 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> in He signed for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in June 2025,<ref>{{cite web | title=Matthew Shiels is a Spider | date=17 June 2025 | url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/matthew-shiels-joins-queens-park/ }}</ref> and renewed his contract with the club in May 2026.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/matthew-shiels-signs-up-for-next-season/|title=Matthew Shiels Signs Up for next season|first=David|last=Oliver|date=26 May 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Having previously been called up for Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] level, in November 2017 he was called up to the [[Republic of Ireland national under-18 football team|Republic of Ireland under-18]] squad,<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/rangers-striker-matthew-shiels-handed-11476413|title=Rangers striker Matthew Shiels handed shock Republic of Ireland call-up|first=Mark|last=McDougall|date=6 November 2017|website=Daily Record}}</ref> making his debut on 9 November.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.donegaldaily.com/2017/11/10/rangers-striker-shiels-makes-irish-debut-in-spain-thanks-to-donegal-roots/|title=Rangers striker Shiels makes Irish debut in Spain thanks to… – Donegal Daily|first=Chris|last=McNulty|website=www.donegaldaily.com|date=10 November 2017 }}</ref>

He also played with the [[Republic of Ireland national under-19 football team|Republic of Ireland under-19s]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derryjournal.com/news/coveted-rangers-starlet-matthew-shiels-enjoys-debut-victory-tom-mohans-ireland-709337|title=Coveted Rangers starlet Matthew Shiels enjoys debut victory with Tom Mohan's Ireland | Derry Journal |date=13 February 2018 }}</ref> before later reverting his international allegiance back to Scotland,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/why-scottish-irish-footballing-relations-have-been-at-a-low-ebb-for-20-years-41742090.html|title=Why Scottish-Irish footballing relations have been at a low ebb for 20 years|website=independent|date=11 June 2022 }}</ref> playing ten games for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19]] team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=214791&lid=9|title=Matthew Shiels | Scotland | Scottish FA|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref>

==Playing style==
Shiels plays primarily as a [[Defender (association football)|left back]], but also played as a [[Midfielder#Winger|left winger]] and [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for Rangers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/rangers-striker-left-winger-can-25005600|title=Rangers had me as striker and left winger, I can be Accies' utility man – Shiels|first=Paul|last=Thomson|date=18 September 2021|website=Daily Record}}</ref> On signing for [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] in August 2023 he said he preferred playing in a more attacking role.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Fraser |date=9 August 2023 |title=Returning Son Matty Shiels says title ambitions convinced him on Dumbarton move |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/returning-son-matty-shiels-says-30666474 |access-date=9 August 2023 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> During his time with Queens Park, he was described by the club as a " dependable utility man [...] playing a variety of positions".<ref name="auto2"/>

'''Zak Delaney''' (born 10 January 2002) is an Irish professional footballer, who plays for {{Scottish football updater|GreenocM}} club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zak Delaney {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Greenock Morton {{!}} Age 22 {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=116555 |access-date=2024-08-05 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

== Club career ==
Delaney spent his early youth career playing for Dublin sides, [[St Francis F.C.|St Francis]] and [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]] before securing himself a move to [[EFL Championship]] side [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]].

Delaney never made an appearance for the first team at ''West Brom'', as he spent his season out on loan to [[Bath City F.C.|Bath City]] in the [[National League South]], making his debut against [[Welling United F.C.|Welling United]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=03 Zak Delaney |url=https://www.bathcityfc.com/player/anthony-straker/ |access-date=2022-07-05 |website=Bath City FC |language=en-GB |archive-date=2022-05-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220522010157/https://www.bathcityfc.com/player/anthony-straker/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In July 2022, Delaney went on trial at [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], featuring in their 10–0 and 1–0 friendly wins over [[Clachnacuddin F.C.|Clachnacuddin]] and [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]] respectively, before signing for the club on 4 July.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ray |first=James |date=2022-07-05 |title=Defender completes move to new club after West Brom release |url=https://the72.co.uk/2022/07/05/defender-completes-move-to-new-club-after-west-brom-release/ |access-date=2022-07-05 |website=The72 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 12 January 2024, Delaney was released by Inverness and joined Championship rivals, Arbroath, making his debut the following day.

On 3 July 2024, Delaney joined Scottish Championship side [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gmfc.net/zak-delaney-signs-a-two-year-deal/|title=Zak Delany signs a two-year deal|website=gmfc.net|date=3 July 2024|accessdate=3 July 2024}}</ref>

'''Ben Summers''' (born 16 June 2004) is a Scottish professional [[Association footballer|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] for [[Ayr United]] on loan from [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/ben-summers-leaves-celtic-after-36566048|title=Ben Summers joins Scott Brown and his Ayr United promotion bid |date=16 January 2026 }}</ref>

==Club career==
Summers joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at the age of seven. He signed his first professional contract with the club in June 2020,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/18215/ | title=Birthday Bhoy Ben signs first professional contract with Celtic | publisher=Celtic FC | date=16 June 2020 | access-date=17 April 2023}}</ref> which was extended in September 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2022/september/30/ben-summers-extends-his-stay-at-celtic/ | title=Ben Summers extends his stay at Celtic | publisher=Celtic FC | date=30 September 2022 | access-date=17 April 2023}}</ref> On 18 March 2023, Summers was named on the bench for Celtic's 3–1 win against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64923678|title=Celtic 3–1 Hibernian|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 March 2023|accessdate=17 April 2023}}</ref> He made his Celtic debut on 16 April 2023, substituted on in the 88th minute, in a 4–1 win away to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65223924|title=Kilmarnock 1–4 Celtic|website=BBC Sport|date=16 April 2023|accessdate=17 April 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Summers was included in the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad for the first time in March 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64901700 |title=Scotland Under-21 squad: Josh Doig, Leon King & Ben Doak selected for friendlies |website=BBC Sport |date=9 March 2023 |accessdate=17 April 2023}}</ref> He made his debut on 23 March 2023 in a [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] match against [[Sweden national under-21 football team|Sweden]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65059879 |title=Manchester City duo score but Scotland U21s lose 3-2 to Sweden in friendly |website=BBC Sport |date=23 March 2023 |accessdate=17 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=237821&lid=5|title=Ben Summers|publisher=Scottish Football Association|accessdate=17 April 2023}}</ref>

'''Arron John Lyall'''<ref name="Inverness">{{Soccerway|id=arron-lyall/622309|accessdate=}}</ref> (born 27 September 2003) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|GreenocM}} club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on loan from [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]]. He previously played for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], on loan from [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

== Career ==
Lyall played through the [[Rangers F.C. B Team and Academy|Rangers Academy]], signed a three-year contract with the club on 9 September 2020.<ref name="trio new">{{ Cite news | url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/academy-trio-pen-new-contracts/widZEQiS6d0VeCZflGHhr| work=Rangers.co.uk | publisher=Rangers Football Club| date=29 September 2020| title=ACADEMY TRIO PEN NEW CONTRACTS}}</ref> On 22 March 2022, he was loaned out to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 March 2021  |title=Caley Thistle sign Rangers teenager on loan |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-sign-rangers-teenager-on-loan-232309/ |access-date=4 January 2023 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=ICTFC |date=22 March 2021 |title=Arron Lyall signs for ICTFC on loan |url=https://ictfc.com/aaron-lyall-signs-for-ictfc-on-loan |access-date=4 January 2023 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://twitter.com/RFC_Youth/status/1374064225182740480| title=RangersFC can today confirm that Arron Lyall has joined @ICTFC on loan for the remainder of the season.  |publisher=Twitter, Inc. |date=22 March 2021|accessdate=22 March 2021}}</ref> He made his career debut on 23 March 2021, in the [[Scottish Cup]], away to [[Buckie Thistle F.C.|Buckie Thistle]]. Lyall made a further three appearances for Inverness, including two in the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref name="Inverness"/>

On 21 May 2023, he made his professional Rangers debut in a [[Scottish Premiership]] match away to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], as a 89th minute substitute for [[Ryan Jack]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hibernian 1-3 Rangers |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65586920 |date=21 May 2023}}</ref> Three days later, Lyall signed a one-year contract extension with Rangers which kept him at the club until the summer of 2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/RFC_Youth/status/1661295986050736128|title=Rangers FC are delighted to announce that Arron Lyall has signed a contract extension until summer 2024.|work=Rangers FC|publisher=Twitter, Inc|date=24 May 2023}}</ref>

Lyall signed a loan deal with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] on the 19th of January 2024. The midfielder made his debut as a second-half substitute in a 1-0 victory versus [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in the Scottish Cup on 20 January 2024.

On 21 June 2024, Lyall joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-21 |title=Arron Lyall Signs - Greenock Morton FC |url=https://gmfc.net/arron-lyall-signs/ |access-date=2024-08-03 |language=en-US}}</ref>

on 21 June 2025, Lyall joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/arron-lyall-joins-the-staggies |title=Arron Lyall joins the Staggies |website=Ross County FC |date=21 June 2025 |accessdate=21 June 2025}}</ref> On 26 September 2025, Lyall re-joined [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lyall Joins Greenock Morton on Loan |website=Ross County FC |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/lyall-joins-greenock-morton-on-loan |date=26 September 2025 |access-date=30 September 2025}}</ref>

'''Luke McBeth''' (born 9 September 1999) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre back]] or [[defensive midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|PartickT}} club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]]. Born in [[Glasgow]], McBeth developed his game in the US College system before returning to [[Scotland]] for his professional playing career.

== Career ==

===College career===
Following coming through the youth ranks at St Cadocs Youth Club in Glasgow's Southside, McBeth continued his footballing career in the [[College soccer#United States|US college football scholarship system]]. Between 2018 and 2022 he played for two universities during his time in the US, [[Lindenwood University]] in [[Missouri]] and [[Monmouth University]] in [[New Jersey]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-luke-mcbeth-signs-an-18-month-contract/ | title=Signing News: Luke McBeth signs an 18 month contract }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://monmouthhawks.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/luke-mcbeth/14977 | title=Luke McBeth - Men's Soccer }}</ref>

===Return to Scotland===
After leaving the US, McBeth signed for Scottish [[Lowland Football League]] side [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]] in late 2022. Following a short spell with East Kilbride, McBeth moved to [[West of Scotland Football League]] club [[Glenafton Athletic F.C.|Glenafton Athletic]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-luke-mcbeth-signs-an-18-month-contract/ | title=Signing News: Luke McBeth signs an 18 month contract }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://glenaftonfc.com/former-players/squad-luke-mcbeth/ | title=Squad: Luke McBeth | date=12 June 2023 }}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
On 1 January 2024, following a successful trial period, McBeth signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] for an undisclosed fee, signing an 18-month contract, with the option of a further year, with the Glasgow club.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-luke-mcbeth-signs-an-18-month-contract/ | title=Signing News: Luke McBeth signs an 18 month contract }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ayrshire-today.co.uk/news/24025347.partick-thistle-sign-luke-mcbeth-glenafton-athletic/ | title=Glens star departs and makes debut for Scottish Championship side | date=3 January 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24086921.shrewd-mcbeth-deal-looks-solved-partick-thistle-problem-area/ | title=Shrewd Luke McBeth signing looks to have solved Partick Thistle problem area | date=February 2024 }}</ref>

McBeth made his Thistle debut, coming off the bench as a substitute in a 3–2 home victory over Queen's Park in the Scottish Championship in January 2024.<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67821091</ref>

McBeth made his first start for Thistle, playing the full 90 minutes in a 3–3 away draw with Inverness in February 2024.<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68144690</ref>

McBeth scored his first goal for Thistle in the first leg of the Scottish Premiership play off quarter final against Airdrie in May 2024, curling in a stunning strike from over 25 yards.<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c72pr5envn8t</ref>

McBeth signed a contract extension with Partick Thistle in May 2024, adding an extra two years to his deal, extending it until summer 2027.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/luke-mcbeth-signs-up-until-2027/</ref>

McBeth scored his first league goal for Thistle with a volley, in a 2–0 home win over Ayr United in March 2025.<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwydwl9998dt</ref>

=== Ayr United ===
In June 2026, Luke McBeth joined fellow [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] side [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] for an undisclosed fee, with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] manager [[Mark Wilson (Scottish footballer)|Mark Wilson]] citing McBeth's  desire for more regular playing time as the reason for the move.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Luke McBeth joins Ayr United for an undisclosed fee |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/luke-mcbeth-joins-ayr-united-for-an-undisclosed-fee/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

'''Marco Alin Rus''' (born 23 January 2003) is a Romanian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|AyrUnite}} club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].

Born in [[Cluj-Napoca]], he moved to England at the age of 9. He played for the youth academies of English clubs [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]], [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] before signing a senior contract at Coventry and spending time on loan at [[Hereford F.C.|Hereford]], [[Chorley F.C.|Chorley]] and [[Universitatea Cluj]]. He joined Ayr United on a permanent basis in June 2024.

==Early life==
Rus was born in [[Cluj-Napoca]], but when he was 9 he moved to England with his family. He played for the youth academies of English clubs [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]], [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/sport/17762177.southampton-signed-sam-bellis-marco-rus/ |title=Southampton have signed Sam Bellis and Marco Rus |work=Southern Daily Echo |date=11 July 2019 |access-date=20 August 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.ro/fotbal/romanian-liga-i/2023-2024/un-jucator-roman-din-anglia-a-semnat-si-va-juca-pentru-prima-data-in-superliga-romaniei_sto10022774/story.shtml|title=UN JUCĂTOR ROMÂN DIN ANGLIA A SEMNAT ȘI VA JUCA PENTRU PRIMA DATĂ ÎN SUPERLIGA ROMÂNIEI|publisher=eurosport.ro}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.playsport.ro/un-fotbalist-roman-din-anglia-a-semnat-cu-u-cluj-al-6-lea-transfer-pentru-sabau-406337|title=Un fotbalist român din Anglia a semnat cu U Cluj. Al 6-lea transfer pentru Sabău|publisher=playsport.ro}}</ref>

==Club career==

=== Coventry City ===
In the summer of 2021, Rus joined the academy of [[EFL Championship]] club [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] after being released by [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] at the end of the previous season. After a trial period, he signed a two-year contract until June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turner |first=Andy |date=2021-09-03 |title=Inside story behind Sky Blues signing Marco Rus from Southampton |url=https://www.coventrytelegraph.net/sport/football/transfer-news/coventry-city-transfers-marco-rus-21479786 |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=[[Coventry Telegraph]] |language=en}}</ref>

In June 2023, Rus signed a new two-year contract at Coventry until 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-21 |title=Marco Rus signs new two-year deal with Coventry City |url=https://www.coventryobserver.co.uk/sport/football-marco-rus-signs-new-two-year-deal-with-coventry-city/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=[[Coventry Herald|Coventry Observer]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== Loan to Hereford ====
On 3 December 2022, Rus joined [[National League North]] club [[Hereford F.C.|Hereford]] on a one-month loan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lawrence |first=David |date=2022-12-03 |title=Hereford FC sign teenage attacking midfielder on loan |url=https://www.herefordtimes.com/sport/23167742.hereford-fc-sign-teenage-attacking-midfielder-loan/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=[[Hereford Times]] |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut the same day in a 2–1 league defeat away against [[King's Lynn Town F.C.|King’s Lynn Town]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lawrence |first=David |date=2022-12-03 |title=King's Lynn Town v Hereford FC LIVE minute by minute updates |url=https://www.herefordtimes.com/news/23167719.kings-lynn-town-v-hereford-fc-live-updates/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=[[Hereford Times]] |language=en}}</ref> He scored his first and only goal for Hereford three days later on his home debut in a 1–1 league draw against [[Chorley F.C.|Chorley]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lawrence |first=David |date=2022-12-06 |title=Hereford FC v Chorley LIVE minute by minute updates |url=https://www.herefordtimes.com/news/23174453.hereford-fc-v-chorley-live-minute-minute-updates/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=[[Hereford Times]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== Loans to Chorley ====
On 23 March 2023, Rus joined National League North club [[Chorley F.C.|Chorley]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-23 |title=Marco Rus joins on loan |url=https://www.chorleyfc.com/blogs/news/marco-rus-joins-on-loan |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=Chorley FC |language=en}}</ref>

On 9 December 2023, Rus returned to Chorley on a one-month youth loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-09 |title=TRANSFER: Marco Rus joins Chorley FC on loan |url=https://www.ccfc.co.uk/news/2023/december/transfer-marco-rus-joins-chorley-on-loan/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=Coventry City |language=en-gb}}</ref>

==== Loan to Universitatea Cluj ====
On 13 February 2024, Rus joined Liga I club [[Universitatea Cluj]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-13 |title=TRANSFER: Marco Rus joins FC Universitatea Cluj on loan |url=https://www.ccfc.co.uk/news/2024/february/transfer-marco-rus-joins-fc-universitatea-cluj-on-loan/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=Coventry City |language=en-gb}}</ref> He made his league debut against [[FCSB]] on 19 February 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/reactie-marco-rus-u-cluj-fcsb-731257.html|title=Jucătorul transferat de U Cluj din Championship a debutat cu FCSB și a oferit primele declarații: "Am avut puține emoții, U Cluj e un club mare"|publisher=gsp.ro}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.zcj.ro/sport/marco-rus-dupa-ce-a-debutat-in-alb-si-negru-nu-am-putut-refuza-u-cluj-e-un-club-foarte-mare--259931.html|title=Marco Rus, după ce a debutat în alb și negru: "Nu am putut refuza U Cluj, e un club foarte mare"|publisher=zcj.ro}}</ref>

=== Ayr United ===
On 15 June 2024, Rus signed for Scottish Championship club Ayr United for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turner |first=Andy |date=15 June 2024 |title=Coventry City complete first outward transfer as midfielder moves for 'undisclosed' fee - CoventryLive |url=https://www.coventrytelegraph.net/sport/football/transfer-news/coventry-transfers-marco-rus-ayr-29361794 |access-date=15 June 2024 |website=[[Coventry Telegraph]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His father, [[Alin Rus|Alin]], was also a professional footballer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.prosport.ro/fotbal-intern/superliga/fotbalistul-transferat-din-anglia-in-superliga-romaniei-fascinat-dupa-ce-a-debutat-in-meciul-cu-fcsb-19832375|title=Fotbalistul transferat din Anglia în Superliga României, fascinat după ce a debutat în meciul cu FCSB: "N-am mai jucat cu 25.000 de oameni în tribune!". '''Anton Dowds''' (born 19 November 1996) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|AyrUnited
}} [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

==Career==
===Early career===
Dowds joined [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] in 2018 from Heriot Watt University where he picked up end of season awards as Player and Coaches' Player of the Year as well as top scorer.<ref name=EFFC>{{cite web|url=https://eastfifefc.info/latest-news/532-anton-dowds-signs-contract-extension|title=Anton Dowds Signs Contract Extension|website=East Fife F.C.|accessdate=9 September 2024}}</ref> Dowds was named the [[2018–19 Scottish League One|League One]] player of the month for January 2019, scoring four goals and assisting another.<ref name=POMjan>{{cite web|url=https://eastfifefc.info/latest-news/599-player-of-the-month-award-for-anton-dowds|title=Player of the Month Award For Anton Dowds|website=East Fife FC|accessdate=9 September 2024}}</ref> Following a successful first season at East Fife, where he finished as the club's top scorer,<ref name=procontract /> Dowds signed a contract extension until 2020.<ref name=EFFC />

On 20 July 2020, Dowds moved to [[Scottish League One|League One]] rivals [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], signing a full-time professional contract.<ref name=procontract>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/east-fifes-anton-dowds-moves-to-falkirk-2918967|title=East Fife's Anton Dowds moves to Falkirk|website=Fife Today|date=20 July 2020|accessdate=9 September 2024}}</ref>

With his deal due to expire Falkirk, Dowds signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in the [[Scottish Championship]] on 13 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/anton-dowds-signs-a-pre-contract-agreement-with-the-club/ |title=Anton Dowds signs a pre-contract agreement with the Club |work=ptfc.co.uk |publisher=Partick Thistle FC |date=13 June 2022 |accessdate=13 June 2022 |archive-date=23 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220523120818/https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/anton-dowds-signs-a-pre-contract-agreement-with-the-club/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=Partickmove /> He made his debut for the club in a 2–0 home victory over [[Fraserburgh F.C.|Fraserburgh]] in the [[2022–23 Scottish League Cup|Scottish League Cup]].<ref name=Partickmove /> In his first season at the club, he scored seven goals in 35 appearances across all competitions.<ref name=Partickmove />

===Ayr United===
On 12 September 2023, Dowds joined [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan from Partick Thistle for the remainder of the [[2023–24 Ayr United F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref name=Partickmove>{{cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/anton-dowds-heads-to-ayr-on-loan/|title=Anton Dowds heads to Ayr on loan|website=Partick Thistle F.C.|date=12 September 2023|accessdate=9 September 2024}}</ref> Dowds scored a hat-trick for Ayr United in a 3–2 away victory over [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] on 17 February 2024 in the [[2023–24 Scottish Championship|league]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68144676|title=Airdrieonians 2-3 Ayr United: Anton Dowds hat-trick secures away win|website=BBC|date=17 February 2024|accessdate=9 September 2024}}</ref>

On 25 May 2024, Dowds signed a one-year deal with Ayr United following a successful loan spell.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/anton-dowds-signs-for-season-202425|title=Anton Dowds Signs For Season 2024/25|website=Ayr United|date=25 May 2024|accessdate=9 September 2024}}</ref>

Dowds started the [[2024–25 Ayr United F.C. season|2024–25 season]] in fine form, scoring four goals in his first five [[2024–25 Scottish Championship|league]] outings to send his club to the top of the table.<ref name=SPFLpom /> He was recognized with the SPFL Championship player of the month award for August 2024 for his efforts.<ref name=SPFLpom>{{cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/anton-dowds-claims-august-award#:~:text=Anton%20Dowds%20has%20been%20named,first%20month%20of%20the%20season.|title=Anton Dowds claims August Award|website=SPFL|accessdate=27 September 2024|date=11 September 2024}}</ref> In October 2024, Dowds underwent season-ending surgery to repair a ruptured cruciate ligament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/ayr-united-hotshot-anton-dowds-33796613|title=Ayr United hotshot Anton Dowds on preparing to hit long road to recovery|website=Daily Record|date=2 October 2024|accessdate=11 November 2024}}</ref>

'''Josh Rae''' (born 17 October 2000) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]]  for {{Scottish football updater|RaithRov}} side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

== Career ==
Rae attended [[Graeme High School]] and came through the youth systems of [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]],<ref>[https://newsquest.newsprints.co.uk/25650011-12-year-old-joshua-rae-pictured-near-his-home-in-croy-north-lanarkshire-with-his-father-robert-joshua-is-keeper-for-the-hamilton-academicals-u15-team-joshua-who-is-nearly-6ft-2inches-tal/ 12 year old Joshua Rae pictured near his home in Croy, North Lanarkshire with his father Robert], ''Newsquest'', 18 September 2013</ref><ref>[https://spfl.co.uk/news/hamilton-give-13-year-old-goalkeeper-game-time-in-under-20-game Youngster gets Accies chance], [[Scottish Professional Football League]], 6 March 2014</ref> [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26480459 Celtic sign 13-year-old Hamilton goalkeeper Joshua Rae], ''BBC Sport'', 7 March 2014</ref> and [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]<ref>[https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/news/joshua-rae-leeds-united-peterhead-league-one/ Joshua Rae hoping for Peterhead table climb], Ben Banks, ''Not The Old Firm'', 11 December 2020</ref> before beginning his senior career with [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]]. He has also played for [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]], [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]],<ref>[https://www.peterheadfc.co.uk/2020/10/05/welcome-joshua-rae/ Welcome Joshua Rae], Peterhead FC, 5 October 2020</ref><ref>[https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/peterhead-fc/2782879/peterhead-josh-rae-cove-rangers/ Josh Rae growing in confidence as Peterhead's number one], Press & Journal, 6 January 2021 {{subscription required}}</ref> [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]]<ref>[https://qosfc.com/news-5441 Welcome - Josh Rae], Queen of the South FC, 18 June 2021</ref> and [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>[https://www.airdriefc.com/2223-news/220623/keeper-josh-signs-up Keeper Josh signs up], Airdrieonians FC, 23 June 2022</ref><ref>[https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/airdrie-penalty-hero-sets-sights-30037818 Airdrie penalty hero sets sights on Premiership play-offs], Andy McGilvray, ''Daily Record'', 22 May 2023</ref>

He joined St Johnstone of the [[Scottish Premiership]] in the summer of 2024,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c066ed5pp1zo|title=St Johnstone sign keeper Rae on two-year deal|date=10 June 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>[https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/5006226/st-johnstone-josh-rae-airdrie/ St Johnstone sign Airdrie goalie Josh Rae on 2-year deal], Eric Nicolson, ''The Courier'', 10 June 2024</ref> as competition for [[Ross Sinclair (footballer)|Ross Sinclair]] following the departure of [[Dimitar Mitov]].<ref>[https://www.glasgowworld.com/sport/football/celtic/former-celtic-player-set-for-big-opportunity-at-premiership-rivals-4851050 Former Celtic player set for 'big opportunity' at Premiership rivals after having to be 'patient'], Martyn Simpson, ''Glasgow World'', 4 November 2024</ref>

Josh Rae signed a loan deal with Raith Rovers in  February 2025 however the deal turned to a permanent transfer with Rae signing for Raith Rovers on a permanent basis in May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Club |first=Raith Rovers Football |title=Josh Rae |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/team/josh-rae/ |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=Raith Rovers Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Rae is currently on a two-year deal with Raith Rovers which expires in May 2027.

'''Elyh Samuel Harrison''' (born 19 February 2006) is an English [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|GreenocM}} club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on loan from {{English football updater|ManchesU}} club [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].

==Club career==
As a youth player, Harrison joined the [[youth academy]] of [[Premier League]] side [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]]. Subsequently, he joined the youth academy of [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]]. In 2022, he joined the youth academy of [[Premier League]] side [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and helped the under-18 team win the [[Premier League Cup (football)|2024 Premier League Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.snl24.com/kickoff/worldnews/african-football/five-wonderkids-bafana-bafana-could-lose-to-foreign-countries-adam-pearlman-elyh-harrison-alwande-roaldsoy-ayanda-sishuba-david-katlego-hansen-20240425|title=Five wonderkids Bafana could lose to foreign countries|magazine=[[Kick Off (magazine)|Kick Off]]|date=25 April 2024|access-date=6 February 2025}}</ref> Two years later, he was sent on loan to [[Chester F.C.|Chester]], where he made eighteen league appearances.<ref>{{Soccerway|856729}}</ref>

On 22 July 2025, Harrison joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.shrewsburytown.com/news/2025/july/22/goalkeeper-elyh-harrison-joins-on-loan-/ |publisher=Shrewsbury Town|title=Goalkeeper Elyh Harrison joins on loan!|website=ShrewsburyTown.com|date=22 July 2025 |accessdate=22 July 2025}}</ref>

On 28 July 2026, Harrison joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carney |first=Sam |title=Loan news: Harrison joins Morton {{!}} Manchester United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/loan-news-harrison-joins-greenock-morton |access-date=2026-07-28 |website=www.manutd.com |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Harrison played for the [[England national under-18 football team]] and the [[England national under-19 football team]]. English newspaper ''[[Manchester Evening News]]'' wrote in 2024 that he was "one of the most promising homegrown goalkeepers of his generation".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/who-elyh-harrison-manchester-united-28526385|title=Who is Elyh Harrison? Manchester United youngster named in squad vs Newport County|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[Manchester Evening News]]|date=28 January 2024|access-date=6 February 2025}}</ref> Through his parents, he is eligible to play for the [[South Africa national soccer team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/soccer/premier-league/who-is-elyh-harrison-bafana-bafana-eligible-teen-promoted-to-manchester-united-first-team-training-8b2b0b6e-547c-46cd-8be2-8efcad587662|title=Who is Elyh Harrison? '''Ben Brannan''' (born 30 January 2007) is a Scottish footballer who currently plays as a defender for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Brannan {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Kilmarnock {{!}} Age 18 {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=165796 |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

== Career ==
Brannan started his career in the [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] youth academy, working his way up until signing professionally in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Highet |first=Lochlin |date=2023-07-27 |title=Brannan signs first pro deal |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/brannan-signs-first-pro-deal/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Kilmarnock FC }}</ref>

In February 2025, Brannan was sent out on loan to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in [[Scottish League One]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-20 |title=Caley Thistle seal deal to bring in young Premiership talent |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-seal-deal-to-bring-in-young-premiership-talent-374993/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Inverness Courier |url-access=subscription}}</ref> making his debut in a 1–1 draw with [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inverness CT vs Montrose: Scottish League One stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gejnv4v71t |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=[[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> before scoring his first professional goal two weeks later in a 4–1 win over [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inverness CT vs Stenhousemuir: Scottish League One stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwy1me9lpg7t |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=BBC Sport }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Brannan {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Inverness Caledonian Thistle {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=203483 |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

In May 2025, after finishing the season with Inverness, Brannan was recalled by Kilmarnock as he went on to captain ''Killie'' in a 2–0 win over [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] to lift the [[Scottish Youth Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carson |first=Callum |date=2025-05-06 |title=Kilmarnock skipper hopes Hampden success leads to earning first team trust |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/kilmarnock-skipper-hopes-hampden-success-35177469 |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Daily Record }}</ref>

== International career ==
In February 2023, Brannan received his first international youth call up, making his debut on 21 February in a 3–1 loss to [[Denmark national under-17 football team|Denmark]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denmark U16 vs ScotlandU16 (International Friendly - 2023/02/21) Live Data, Analysis, Predictions |url=https://www.footballant.com/matches/2351831 |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=www.footballant.com |language=en}}</ref> He was then promoted to the Under 17s team, where he was substituted on in a [[UEFA European Under-17 Championship|UEFA U17 European Championship]] qualifying match against [[Kazakhstan national under-17 football team|Kazakhstan]], with Scotland winning 2–0.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Scotland-Kazakhstan {{!}} UEFA Under-17 2024 |url=https://www.uefa.com/under17/match/2036957--scotland-vs-kazakhstan/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Christopher John Cupps''' (born May 26, 2008) is an American professional [[soccer]] player who plays as a [[center-back]] for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on loan from [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Chicago Fire FC|Chicago Fire]].

==Club career==
Cupps is a youth product of [[Chicago Fire FC|Chicago Fire]] since 2017. In 2024, he started playing with their [[Chicago Fire FC II|reserves]] in the [[MLS Next Pro]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://meninred97.com/christopher-cupps-the-chicago-fires-present-and-future/,%20https://meninred97.com/christopher-cupps-the-chicago-fires-present-and-future/|title=Christopher Cupps: Chicago Fire's Present and Future - MIR97|first=Alex|last=Calabrese|date=September 25, 2025}}</ref> On February 18, 2025, he signed his first professional contract with Chicago Fire as a [[Homegrown Player Rule (MLS)|Homegrown Player]] until 2028, with options for 2029 and 2030.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagofirefc.com/news/chicago-fire-fc-signs-academy-defender-christopher-cupps-to-first-team-contract-as-a-homegrown-player|title=Chicago Fire FC Signs Academy Defender Christopher Cupps to First-Team Contract as a Homegrown Player | Chicago Fire FC|website=chicagofirefc}}</ref> He debuted with the senior Chicago Fire team in a 3–1 [[U.S. Open Cup]] win over [[New England Revolution]] on May 21, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://readtheforum.org/26462/sports/former-latin-student-christopher-cupps-makes-professional-soccer-debut-at-age-16/|title=Former Latin Student Christopher Cupps Makes Professional Soccer Debut at Age 16|date=June 3, 2025}}</ref>

On 24 August 2026, Cupps joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on loan until the end of 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=24 August 2026 |title=Chicago Fire FC Loans Homegrown Defender Christopher Cupps to Scottish Championship side Greenock Morton F.C. |url=https://www.chicagofirefc.com/news/chicago-fire-fc-loans-homegrown-defender-christopher-cupps-to-scottish-championship-side-greenock-morton-f-c |access-date=2026-11-01 |website= |publisher=Chicago Fire FC |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Cupps was called up to the [[United States men's national under-17 soccer team|United States U17]]s for the [[2025 FIFA U-17 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://meninred97.com/christopher-cupps-named-to-u-17-world-cup-roster/,%20https://meninred97.com/christopher-cupps-named-to-u-17-world-cup-roster/|title=Christopher Cupps Named to U-17 World Cup Roster - MIR97 Media|first=Alex|last=Calabrese|date=October 16, 2025}}</ref>
